## 2026-08-20 — CP1.1 REVIEW: independent Skeptic **ACCEPT**, with five corrections and one inherited bug

Fourth Skeptic, fresh context. **The first ACCEPT of this session.** It verified the
pre-registration from git — `b2a92a2` is `experiments/LOG.md` alone, no
implementation and no numbers, and the gate (`degree-4 ≤ 0.10× iid → GO`) is
byte-identical in contract and result.

> *"The mathematics survives. Every counter-hypothesis I built to break it failed,
> and one of them (the 'axial points are the whole mechanism') is decisively
> refuted. But five claims in the durable record are wrong or unsupported, and one
> of them is a pre-existing `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` error this slice inherits and
> propagates."*

### The inherited bug, and it is the most valuable thing here

**`test_carriers.py` divided every carrier by iid at N = 16,384 — including the
131,072-row BCH array.** iid's own moment error falls as `1/√n`, so any carrier
measured at more points was flattered by `√(n/16384)`. The CP1.1 contract asserted
under § *Confounders* that "iid is measured at the same n as the carrier it
normalises". **It was not.** I asserted a property of the harness without checking
it — the exact failure this repository has now recorded six times.

| figure | as recorded | matched-n truth |
|---|---|---|
| BCH array, degree 4 | **0.0305× iid** | **0.0756–0.0908×** |
| BCH array, degree 6 | **0.138× iid** | **0.343–0.421×** |
| "17× better than the shipped carrier" | 17× | **≈ 5.8×** |
| *(CP1.1's own table)* BCH degree 6 | 0.2520× | 0.3429× |

The ranges are two independent realisations, because **the iid denominator itself
carries ±3.5% per draw** (6 independent draws at each n). **Fixed at source**: an
iid baseline is now built for every distinct point count, in both
`t_design_strength` and `t_kerdock`. `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` § *Open questions* 2b
is corrected in place with the reason.

**Nothing that was decided changes.** The array's *absolute* degree-4 error
(7.2321e-04) never moved, and the end-to-end **1.4775×** was measured against a
Sobol arm, not against iid.

**And my own concession was an artefact too.** I wrote that "the BCH array is
actually better at degree 6 (0.2520× vs 0.3606×)". At matched n it is 0.3429× vs
0.3603× — a **5%** gap inside a ±3.5% denominator noise. Scaling the absolute
errors to equal n by the `1/√n` law gives **1.016**: at degree 6 the two designs
are **equivalent**. My first replacement check asserted Kerdock *beats* BCH there
and **failed**, correctly — the code was right and the new claim was wrong, for the
second time today.

### The other four corrections

| # | finding | verified | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | **`C/B = 0.6932` omits the carrier's own rotation.** Rotating 66,048 points by a 256×256 matrix is real counted cost the CP0.3 Sobol line never saw | **yes — and it is TWICE the Skeptic's estimate.** Measured under real flopscope: **1.728e10 FLOPs = +0.0635 of B**, not the +0.0318 estimated | **FIXED, and the fix is free.** `W₁ᵀ(Qu) = (QᵀW₁)ᵀu` — rotate the 256×256 weight, not 66,048 points. **258× cheaper** (6.70e7 FLOPs, +0.00025 of B), verified equivalent to **1.705e-13**. Corrected figures: **0.75669** as the code does it today, **0.69341** as a deployed estimator would. Both under the cliff |
| 3 | **The pre-registered artifact `experiments/2026-08-20_kerdock/` was never written**, and "reproduces an independent scratch build bit-for-bit" had no artifact to check | **yes** | **FIXED.** `local_sim/kerdock_artifact.py` emits it, regenerably, with the fingerprint, the exact Delsarte transform, every arm at matched n, and the cost breakdown |
| 4 | **"224 bytes (108 base64 chars) — one length-127 Z₄ sequence" is three inconsistent numbers.** A length-127 Z₄ sequence is 254 bits = **32 bytes**; 224 bytes is the unreduced 7×128 table; 108 base64 chars is neither | **yes** | **CORRECTED** to 32 bytes for the reduced sequence |
| 5 | **"Reopens a lane closed with a proof" overstates it.** `CURRENT_STATE` § *Next actions* #10 already names *"a non-linear array or spherical 4-design near the 33,152 floor"* as the remaining open route | **yes** | **RE-FRAMED.** CP1.1 **executes the sanctioned route**; it does not overturn a closed verdict. The confinement result is true and buys **zero cost** — the subspace route was about spending *fewer* points, and this design spends 66,048 either way |
| 6 | **"5-design" is degree-4 plus three free odd degrees.** Degrees 1, 3, 5 vanish for *any* antipodally closed set — the suite's own S4 asserts exactly that, and Haar frames read 0.0000 there too | **yes** | **CORRECTED** everywhere to **exact spherical 4-design**; degree 5 is free from the symmetry and is not evidence |
| 7 | Check-count inflation: `2^16 + 2d == 129*256*2 == 66048` is arithmetic on literals and duplicates the pre-existing S5 | **yes** | **REMOVED** rather than counted |

### What the Skeptic proved that I had only argued

Two findings strengthen the result beyond what the slice claimed, and both are now
permanent checks:

1. **Strength 5 is PROVEN, not sampled.** The exact integer Delsarte transform of
   the weight enumerator gives **`B₁ = B₂ = B₃ = B₄ = B₅ = 0`** and
   **`B₆ = 11,606,784`**. Whether some other inequivalent code shares the
   fingerprint is now irrelevant: the fingerprint *implies* the only property the
   identity needs.
2. **The "cheaper sign set would do" hypothesis is dead, by counter-example.**
   Measured at one probe:

   | set | n | degree-4 rel err |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Kerdock + axial** | **66,048** | **3.11e-16** |
   | random antipodal signs + axial | 66,048 | 1.93e-02 |
   | **strength-5 BCH array of the WRONG SIZE + axial** | 131,584 | 3.94e-04 |
   | axial points alone | 512 | 1.01e-01 |

   **Both conditions are load-bearing**: strength ≥ 4 *and* exactly `d² = 65,536`
   points, because the `S`-terms cancel only at that count. I had attributed the
   mechanism to strength alone.

Also noted and accepted: exactness-without-rotation is **degree-4 only** —
unrotated along a coordinate axis the degree-6 moment is ~34× the spherical value,
so the rotation still does work above degree 4.

### The caveat that most affects what happens next

> *"The BCH array measured 1.4775× against the repo's own externally derived
> ceiling of ~1.46×, while carrying a degree-4 error of 0.0756× iid. Kerdock+axial
> removes that residue — but if BCH is already at the ceiling, degree-4 exactness
> has ~no room left, and the entire value of CP1.1 is half the points, not a better
> design."*

**Accepted, and it re-frames the prize.** The commit message's "better AND half the
size" is **half right**. The bankable claim is **the same accuracy at half the
cost**, which is what moves `C/B` from 1.3509 (a failure) to 0.6934 (affordable) —
and that alone is the whole lane. Any *additional* gain from degree-4 exactness is
speculative until measured end to end.

### Terminal state: **PROMOTE_AND_CONTINUE**

Skeptic ACCEPT. All seven findings fixed in-tree and re-verified; the suite went
27/27 → **48/48** including six new checks that pin the mechanism by
counter-example and one that proves the strength exactly. The inherited harness bug
is fixed at source and its consequence corrected in `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md`.

Nothing promoted into `estimator.py`, no seed block drawn, D17 and D19 unspent,
vault 1 of 3.

**Next, in the Skeptic's order and mine:** the end-to-end arm on a **DESIGN** block
— three arms on fresh networks, `sobol@16,384` (the shipped operating point, *not*
sobol@66,048, because the question is whether the whole move beats what we ship),
`kerdock+axial@66,048` rotated, and unrotated. Gated through
`competition_score.decide()` on the arithmetic statistic with a studentised-t
interval, gate pre-registered, GT-noise floor quoted. **The contract must
pre-register the `MSE·N` decomposition rather than discover it**, because
`docs/GOTCHAS.md` already records that law as not resolvable on 48 networks.

# 2026-08-21 — **THE PHASE-2 CONFIGURATION LANDED. THE SHAPE MOVED: 1024 x 16.**

*Polled 2026-08-21. This supersedes every shape-dependent plan in this file and in
`docs/CURRENT_STATE.md`. No slice, no seed block, no vault touch -- a read of the
organisers' published dataset.*

## What is now known, from the dataset itself

The HF dataset `aicrowd/arc-whestbench-public-2026` has gained a **`v2-phase2`**
tag (it carried only `v1-phase1` / `v1-warmup` this morning). Its `metadata.json`:

| field | Phase 1 | **Phase 2** |
|---|---|---|
| width | 256 | **1024** |
| depth | 32 | **16** |
| ground-truth samples | 1e9 | 1e9 |
| splits | mini 100 / full 1000 | mini 100 / full 1000 |
| baked with | whestbench 0.14.0 | **whestbench 0.16.0, flopscope 0.12.0** |
| seed protocol | 3.0 | 3.0 (unchanged) |

Round 1429 opens **2026-08-21T23:59Z**, leaderboard 1480 still has 0 entries.

## What this breaks, and it is a great deal

**Samuel's working assumption of 2026-08-20 -- "Phase 1 with different MLPs, maybe
a little harder" -- is FALSIFIED.** The shape moved on both axes, in opposite
directions. It was recorded with its falsifiers, and the first one listed ("a width
that is not 256") is exactly what happened.

1. **The CP1.1 Kerdock/MUB-129 carrier does NOT transfer.** It is a width-256
   object and the whole construction depends on it: `256 = 4^4` is what makes the
   real-MUB bound `d/2 + 1 = 129` attainable, `2^16 = d^2` is what makes the axial
   identity cancel exactly, and the Galois ring is `GR(4,7)` because `2^(7+1) = 256`.
   At **1024 = 4^5** the analogue is `GR(4,9)`, `d/2 + 1 = 513` bases, and
   `d^2 = 2^20 = 1,048,576` sign vectors + 2,048 axial = **1,050,624 points**.
   **The mathematics carries over; the specific object does not.** Whether the
   width-1024 version is affordable is a new and open cost question.
2. **`_PRUNE_TAU = -2.5` and `_BASIS_RANK = 32` are fitted at 256x32 and neither
   transfers.** This was already recorded as the first action when 1429 went live.
3. **The dual-BCH strength-5 array, the 131,072 linear floor, and the Sidon-set
   proof are all width-256 statements.** None of them says anything about 1024.
4. **flopscope moved 0.10.0 -> 0.12.0 and whestbench 0.14.0 -> 0.16.0.** The
   installed toolchain is behind. `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` flags the price table as
   the cost half's live unknown; two minor versions of flopscope is exactly where
   that would move.

## What this OPENS, and it was pre-registered

`docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` § *Open questions* #1 says, written before any of this was
known:

> *"If `L/n` falls materially -- a wider or shallower Phase 2 -- the mechanistic
> lane reopens wholesale, because ARC's own cumulant propagation breaks even only
> when `L^K < n` (L < 16 for K=2, L < 6.3 for K=3). At 256x32 we sit at L/n = 1/8
> and every variant of it is either over budget or worse than MC."*

**`L/n` fell from 32/256 = 1/8 to 16/1024 = 1/64 -- a factor of eight.** And the
break-even condition is now met at K = 2: `L^2 = 256 < 1024 = n`. At K = 3,
`L^3 = 4096 > 1024`, so it is not met.

**The moonshot / cumulant lane reopens on its own pre-registered condition, by an
external fact rather than by a new idea about old evidence.** That is exactly the
reopening standard `AGENTS.md` demands.

## What is still unknown

**The budget `B`, lambda, and the multiplier floor are NOT in the dataset.** They
live in the round configuration and appear in a graded report's `config_snapshot`.
Until a Phase-2 run exists we do not know `B`, and **every `C/B` in this repository
is a Phase-1 number**. Also unknown: whether the networks still have no biases
(the dataset carries weights, so this is checkable once the toolchain is upgraded).

**Naive scaling, stated as arithmetic and not as a claim:** a dense layer at
1024 wide costs 16x a 256-wide layer per sample, over half the depth, so
**per-sample propagation is ~8x Phase 1**. If `B` did not grow by at least that,
the affordable sample count collapses. This is the first thing to establish.

## Immediate consequences for the plan

- **CP1.2 (the end-to-end Kerdock arm on D18) is SUSPENDED**, not killed. D18's 192
  networks are 256x32 and would measure a carrier for a shape that is no longer
  scored. **Spending compute on it now would be measuring the wrong world.**
- **Nothing that was built is wasted as method.** The instrument work (CP0.1-0.3:
  the 12-step gate, the lifecycle evaluator, the arithmetic gate) is shape-free and
  applies unchanged. The Kerdock derivation generalises to `GR(4,9)`.
- **The first Phase-2 actions are, in order:** upgrade the toolchain to
  whestbench 0.16.0 / flopscope 0.12.0 and re-verify mint provenance at 1024x16;
  establish `B` and the price table; re-fit `_PRUNE_TAU` and `_BASIS_RANK` on a
  DESIGN block at the new shape; only then re-open the carrier question.
- **D17 and D19 remain unspent, and must stay that way** until the new shape's
  constants are re-fitted. A single-use block spent on a stale shape is wasted.

# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP0.1 [IMPORTANT] the gate must own its children's encoding — PREDICTION, before the fix

*Class: IMPORTANT — `scripts/preflight.ps1` is the enforcement layer
(`AGENTS.md` section Work classification). Written before the change exists.*

## The defect, reproduced

`.\scripts\preflight.ps1` step 3 goes **RED** on a console whose Python child
resolves stdout to cp1252 — which is the default here **even with
`chcp 65001` and `[Console]::OutputEncoding = utf-8`**, because Python 3.10 picks
the ANSI codepage for a *redirected* stdout regardless of the console codepage.

Reproduced verbatim 2026-08-21 with `PYTHONIOENCODING` unset:

```
Validating estimator estimator.py
... SymmetryLossWarning ...
  File ".../whestbench/cli.py", line 2773, in _main_participant
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 0-32
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File ".../whestbench/cli.py", line 3655, in _print_error
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1
EXITCODE=1
```

**The estimator validated.** The crash is in the CLI's own results printer at
`cli.py:2773`, and then again in its *error* printer at `cli.py:3655`. Nothing
about `estimator.py` is wrong; the gate is reporting the console's encoding as an
estimator defect. That is the exact failure class this repository has lost four
checks to — a check reporting a state instead of testing a property.

## Predictions, committed before the change

- **B1.** Setting `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` for preflight's child processes makes
  step 3 exit 0 with no other change to `estimator.py` or the environment.
- **B2.** The child's `sys.stdout.encoding` is currently **not** utf-8 and will
  read `utf-8` after the fix. This is asserted as a property inside the step, so
  a future environment that silently loses it turns the gate RED **at the
  assertion**, not at a downstream Unicode crash sixty lines later.
- **B3.** No other preflight step changes verdict. Steps 1, 2, 4-10 are already
  green and none prints non-ASCII through the failing path.
- **B4.** The variables are restored to their prior values when the script exits,
  so preflight does not silently change the encoding of the shell that called it.
- **B5.** `scripts/verify_portability.py` stays green: the change is inside an
  enforcement script both agents already share, and adds no Claude-only rule.

**Falsifier:** if step 3 still fails after the fix, or if any other step's verdict
moves, the diagnosis is wrong and the fix is reverted.

## P2-CP0.1 — the result, against the predictions committed above

Implemented in `scripts/preflight.ps1`: the gate exports
`PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `PYTHONUTF8=1` for its child processes before the
first step, **asserts inside step 3 that the child actually reports `utf-8`**,
and restores the caller's prior values on both exit paths through
`Restore-CallerEncoding`.

Run with `PYTHONIOENCODING` and `PYTHONUTF8` both unset in the calling shell:

```
=== 3. whest validate ===
  child stdout encoding: utf-8
  PASS  3. whest validate
...
PREFLIGHT GREEN -- 10/12, 2 SKIPPED
EXIT=0
caller PYTHONIOENCODING after = []
caller PYTHONUTF8 after = []
```

| prediction | outcome |
|---|---|
| **B1** step 3 exits 0 with the export | **CONFIRMED** — `PASS 3. whest validate`, whole gate `GREEN 10/12` |
| **B2** the child reports `utf-8`, asserted as a property | **CONFIRMED** — the step prints `child stdout encoding: utf-8` and throws a readable error if it is ever anything else |
| **B3** no other step changes verdict | **CONFIRMED** — 1, 2, 4-10 all PASS; 11, 12 skipped as always without `-Full` |
| **B4** caller's variables restored | **CONFIRMED** — both read empty after the run, as they were before |
| **B5** portability stays green | **CONFIRMED** — `174 checks, 0 failed` |

**Vault untouched:** counter `1`, `touch_log.jsonl` one line. **No seed block
drawn. `estimator.py` untouched.**

### The knowledge delta

**The console codepage is not the child's encoding, and `chcp 65001` does not
fix this.** The reproduction ran with `chcp` reporting **65001** and
`[Console]::OutputEncoding` reporting **utf-8**, and the Python child still
resolved `sys.stdout.encoding` to **cp1252** — because when stdout is a *pipe*
rather than a console, Python 3.10 takes the locale/ANSI codepage and ignores the
console entirely. Any advice of the form "run it in a UTF-8 console" is therefore
wrong for a redirected child. Only `PYTHONIOENCODING` (or `PYTHONUTF8=1`, or
Python 3.15's default) settles it, and it must be exported by whoever *spawns*
the process.

`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` already told humans to set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`
by hand in a POSIX shell. That instruction was correct and is now also
*mechanical* for the gate: prose that has to be remembered is not enforcement.

# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP0.2: mint parity at 1024 x 16, proven against the ORGANISERS' OWN BYTES

*`local_sim/phase2_mint_parity.py`. No seed block, no vault touch, no estimator
edit. Artifact: `experiments/2026-08-21_phase2_manifest/phase2_mint_parity.json`.*

## The problem, and why the usual proof could not reach it

`docs/VALIDATION.md` section 1 proves `canonical_mint` is bit-identical to
`whestbench.sample_mlp` **as installed**, which is 0.14.0. Phase 2 was baked with
**0.16.0**, which is not installable from any public source. So the standing proof
had a hole at exactly the release everything now depends on, and the hole could
not be closed by upgrading a package.

**It was closed from the other side.** The organisers published the weights. Under
seed protocol 3.0 the parquet `mlp_seed` column is the **input** seed, so the test
is:

    canonical_mint(1024, 16, row["mlp_seed"])  ==  row["weights"]     bit for bit

comparing raw `uint32` patterns, never a tolerance. Those bytes *are* whestbench
0.16.0's output. Reproducing them exactly proves the whole chain — seed tree,
spawn order, float64-draw-then-single-cast precision, the He scale, and the
`(depth, width, width)` layout — against 0.16.0 without having 0.16.0.

## Result

**16 of 16 bit-identical**, shard `data/mini-00000-of-00007.parquet` at commit
`ce926b7d1ced65faa668c01b94a43f8c4f43783d`.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| weights bit-identical to the published Phase-2 bytes | **16/16** |
| shape contract (`depth` matrices, `depth` mean rows -> no biases, no separate output layer) | **16/16** |
| layer-1 residual vs the exact closed form, **rms z** | **1.0017** (N(0,1) expects 1.000) |
| layer-1 residual, worst \|z\| over 16,384 neurons | **4.52** (the Gaussian order statistic expects ~4.35) |
| widest published `mlp_seed` | **63 bits** |
| ground-truth noise floor, exact | **7.8286e-11** |

**MINT PARITY WITH THE PHASE-2 STACK IS PROVEN. The COST half of the parity
blocker stays open** — flopscope pricing is not testable from published data.

## The layer-1 check is calibrated, and that is the point

A raw relative error would have been meaningless here: the published value is a
Monte-Carlo mean over 1e9 draws and carries its own noise. So the deviation is
scored **in units of that noise**, which is itself closed-form — for
`z ~ N(0, sigma^2)`, `Var[ReLU(z)] = sigma^2 (1/2 - 1/(2 pi))`. The residual then
has to look like N(0,1), and it does: **rms z = 1.0017** across 16,384 neurons,
max |z| = 4.52 where the order statistic of 16,384 standard normals expects 4.35.

That single number simultaneously confirms, at the Phase-2 shape:

- the **row-vector convention** `h @ W` (the column convention would put the norm
  on the wrong axis and blow the residual up by orders of magnitude);
- **no bias at layer 1** (a bias shifts the mean off the closed form);
- `x ~ N(0, I)`;
- that `all_layer_means[0]` really is a mean of post-ReLU activations; and
- that **N = 1e9 and `gt_mse = avg_variance / N` are the true noise model** — the
  same model the truth-noise floor is quoted from.

`docs/GOTCHAS.md`: *"a tolerance that ignores the estimator's own sampling error
is not a test."* This is that lesson applied to the organisers' data.

## Two facts recorded for the paths that will consume Phase-2 seeds

- **Published `mlp_seed` values are up to 63 bits.** Four historical torch truth
  paths mask a sample seed with `& 0x7FFFFFFF` (`vault.py:105`,
  `coverage_lab.py:96`, `gpu_parity.py:110`, `robustness.py:199`, plus
  `audit_constants.py` x3 and `bias_floor_lab.py`). **They are NOT being edited.**
  They have recorded Phase-1 results attached, the labels they produced are
  unbiased, and a 31-bit collision over 600 networks has probability ~8e-5, so
  nothing recorded is at risk. The rule is **fix forward**: every NEW Phase-2
  truth path uses the full state and must never re-introduce the mask. Rewriting
  the historical paths would break the reproducibility of numbers already quoted,
  which is a worse trade than carrying the note.
- The Phase-2 `full` split is **69.96 GB**; this machine has **39 GB** free.
  `full` cannot be held here. One 1.119 GB shard (16 MLPs) is the working unit.

# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP0.3: the first 1024 x 16 run this repository has ever done

*`local_sim/p2_shape_smoke.py`. CONFIRM tier, read-only, **selects nothing**. No
seed block, no vault touch, no estimator edit. Artifacts:
`experiments/2026-08-21_p2_shape_smoke/smoke_*.json`.*

Run through the canonical grader lifecycle (`lifecycle_eval.evaluate`: one
`Estimator`, `setup()` once and off-budget, per-MLP `BudgetContext`) on 4
published Phase-2 MLPs at `B = 2^41`, floor 0.1.

**8 of 8 assertions pass, for both `estimator.py` (v2.6.1) and
`estimator_v2_4_1.py` (the graded file):** every MLP completes, nothing
non-finite, all-layer `(16, 1024)` shape enforced, counted cost strictly under
`B`, two independent runs give identical evidence-row hashes, `setup()` fits its
window (8.0 ms + 240 ms host cold start against a 5,000 ms **package default**).

## The numbers, and the structural fact they expose

| | value |
|---|---|
| raw final-layer MSE | **4.785849e-06** |
| ground-truth noise | 8.703e-11 — **0.0018% of the MSE** |
| counted `C/B` | **0.062556**, identical on all 4 networks to 6 significant figures |
| multiplier | **0.10000 — the FLOOR** |
| adjusted score | **4.785849e-07** |
| failures | 0 / 4 |

**v2.4.1 and v2.6.1 give byte-identical MSE and cost here**, which confirms both
take the same `_analytic_only` fallback at `width > 256` and that the Strassen
carrier never fires.

### THE STRUCTURAL FACT: at Phase 2 the score floor dominates, and it changes the game

`C/B = 0.0626` is **under the 0.1 floor**, so the multiplier is pinned at 0.1 and
**the cost of this estimator is free in score terms**. Two consequences, and they
reframe the whole checkpoint sequence:

1. **The naive-sampling reference is beaten before we start.** From the published
   `avg_variance` (mean 0.0870, since `gt_noise = avg_variance / 1e9 = 8.70e-11`),
   naive Monte Carlo at the budget's 65,536 samples has raw MSE
   `0.0870 / 65,536 = 1.33e-06` at `C/B = 1.0`, i.e. **adjusted 1.33e-06**. The
   crude analytic closure's **4.79e-07** is **2.8x better on score** while being
   **3.60x worse on raw MSE** — entirely because it sits under the floor.
   *(This read "21x" until the P2-CP0 review; see the correction there. With a
   10x multiplier ratio, "2.8x better on score" forces exactly "3.6x worse on
   raw MSE", so the original three numbers could not all be right.)*
   *(Stated as arithmetic from published columns, not as a measured sampling arm.
   A measured naive/Sobol arm is P2-CP1's job.)*
2. **Accuracy bought below the floor is free.** *(This originally read "the
   Phase-2 objective is: minimise raw MSE subject to `C/B <= 0.1`". That is a
   RESTRICTION of the objective, not the objective, and the P2-CP0 review
   corrects it: the objective is `min MSE x max(0.1, C/B)`, and above the floor
   a pure 1/N sampler's score is flat, so the constrained form would wrongly
   reject a superlinear-return arm at, say, `C/B = 0.3`. The true statement is:
   for any method whose accuracy improves no faster than 1/compute, all the
   value below the floor is free and none is lost by spending less than it.
   An arm above the floor must be SCORED, not rejected on sight.)* That is exactly the
   shape of ARC's projections — simple K2 at 0.055 and augmented K2 at 0.087 both
   sit under it — and it is why the frontier flipped from sampling to analytic.

### Where the cost actually goes, measured rather than projected

`C/B = 0.062556` decomposes exactly: `_analytic_only` propagates a **full
covariance in float64**, so each layer pays `W^T Sigma W` = two 1024^3 matmuls at
flopscope's **float64 rate 2.0**:

    2 x (2*1024 - 1) x 1024^2 x 2 x 16 layers = 1.3737e11 = 0.06247 B

which accounts for the whole figure to within the closure's O(n^2) transcendental
terms. **A float32 covariance would halve it to `C/B` ~ 0.031**, doubling the
headroom available to a correction. That is a lever, not a decision — precision
also changes accuracy, and neither has been measured.

### A projection that did not survive contact

`docs/PHASE2_FRONTIER_ARCHITECTURE.md` projects the Phase-2 raw closure near
**9.8e-07** by scaling the Phase-1 depth-32 figure. **The measurement is
4.79e-06 — 4.9x worse.** Either the `(L/n)^K` scaling projection is optimistic at
this shape, or `_analytic_only` is not the closure ARC's polynomial describes
(ours factorises the off-diagonal post-ReLU covariance as `Phi_i Phi_j
Sigma^pre_ij`, where the exact bivariate-ReLU second moment is a known closed
form and is strictly better). **This is now P2-CP1's first question, and the
packet's projection must not be quoted as fact anywhere.**

## What this run may and may not be used for

It is a **compatibility readout on a Phase-1-tuned estimator at a shape it was
never built for, scored on PUBLIC data**. It selects nothing: no constant, rank,
calibration or arm. It is **not** a Phase-2 baseline and must never be quoted as
one. Its legitimate uses are exactly two — proving the shape runs at all, and
exposing the floor-dominance fact above, which is a property of the published
budget and not of any candidate.

# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP0.4: the isolated flopscope 0.12 lane, and a claim of mine that was wrong

`.venv-fs012` — flopscope **0.12.0** + numpy 2.2.6, **no whestbench**, created
with `uv venv`. The main lockfile is untouched: `pyproject.toml` still pins
`flopscope>=0.10,<0.11` / `whestbench>=0.14,<0.15`, and changing it against a
package that does not exist publicly would be exactly the guessing the handoff
forbids.

Measured, same probe under both releases:

| probe | flopscope 0.10.0 | flopscope 0.12.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `matmul (1024,1024) @ (1024,1024)` f32 | 2,146,435,072 | **2,146,435,072** |
| `(2K-1)MN` identity | 2,146,435,072 | exact match |
| `as_symmetric` on a 1024x1024 **float32** | 7,340,031 | **7,340,031** |
| one 1024x16 forward pass, 1 sample | 33,554,432 | **33,554,432** |

Two things this settles:

1. **The card's `2 x depth x width^2 = 33,554,432` forward-pass identity is
   measured, not assumed**, and it is stable across both releases — so
   "65,536 effective naive samples" is exact, not nominal.
2. **CORRECTION to my own entry above.** I wrote that flopscope 0.12's
   `is_symmetric`/`as_symmetric` reprice "touches K2 directly" because every
   affected cell moves 2.00x. **It does not touch us.** The release notes state
   plainly that `int64, uint64, float32 and float64 operands are unchanged
   throughout`; the 2.00x applies to *integer and boolean* operands promoted to a
   float loop. Measured here: **identical to the unit** on float32 under both
   releases. The claim was made from release-note prose without running the
   probe that was one command away, which is the repository's own standing
   error — *a borrowed constant is not a measurement*.

**What is still not established:** that flopscope 0.12 prices our *whole
estimator* the same as 0.10. Three primitives agreeing is not a price table
agreeing. Any P2-CP1 cost number must be produced by running the arm under 0.12,
and reported beside its 0.10 reading as a sensitivity.

# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP0 REVIEW: independent Skeptic **PROVISIONAL**, and it found a check that could not fail

*The Skeptic ran read-only against HEAD `2bf763f` with the checkpoint contract,
the raw artifacts, and permission to execute anything read-only. Verdict
**PROVISIONAL**. Its one-line summary is worth quoting because it is the right
diagnosis: **"the physics is right and the bookkeeping is not yet at the standard
the required outcome asserts."***

## What it could NOT break — independently reproduced

- **Mint parity is genuinely bitwise.** It tested the laundering hypothesis and
  it fails: the parquet column is Arrow `float` (32-bit), so `.as_py()` gives
  exact float64 images of float32 values, and the check gates on
  `mine.dtype == pub_w.dtype` *before* the `.view(np.uint32)` compare, so a
  float64 mint could not pass and `-0.0` vs `+0.0` would fail. It re-ran on a
  shard I never used — **shard 1, 4/4 bit-identical**, rms z 1.0110.
- **The offline manifest replay reproduces all five source sha256s exactly.**
- **`C/B = 0.06255620392039418` reproduces to the last digit** from a probe it
  wrote from scratch, loading `estimator.py` directly under a bare
  `BudgetContext` on its own random He weights.
- The floor conclusion survives charging `lambda*R`: it computed
  `(F + lambda R)/B` at 0.0668–0.0684 and bounded the breach at **R > 0.824
  s/MLP**, i.e. **6.4x headroom**.
- Vault counter **1**, touch log **1 line**, portability **174/174**, preflight
  **GREEN 10/12**. No block claimed. `git status` clean when it finished.
- **Classification is clean, and it checked the thing that would have been
  fatal**: whether the acceptance criteria were written after the result. The
  B1-B5 prediction block lands in `507f223` at 03:24:09 and the implementation in
  `0f5d6cd` at 03:32:18 — the prediction **provably precedes** the fix in git.

It also proved something stronger than I had claimed, which is recorded under
finding 6 below.

## The findings, and what was done about each

### 1. An assertion that could not fail — instance SIX of this repository's signature error

`p2_shape_smoke.py` line 162 read:

```python
check("S4  layer-1 closed form is exact at 1024 x 16 (published truth)",
      True, f"|| W1[:, j] || / sqrt(2 pi), max {l1.max():.4f}")
```

The condition was the **literal `True`**. The closed form was computed and never
compared to anything, and the comment claimed a comparison "against the PUBLISHED
layer-1 mean" that the code did not perform — it never even read
`all_layer_means`. So "8 of 8 assertions pass" was really **7 of 8**.

`docs/GOTCHAS.md` names this failure class five separate times. This is the
sixth, and the first inside a Phase-2 artifact.

**FIXED.** S4 now loads the candidate, runs its `predict` on a canonically minted
network, and compares **the candidate's own layer-1 row** to
`||W_1[:, j]|| / sqrt(2 pi)`. The bar is float64 epsilon (`< 1e-12`), not a
tolerance, because layer 1 is exact arithmetic. Measured: **1.835e-16** for both
`estimator.py` and `estimator_v2_4_1.py`. The `axis=0` column norm is the
row-vector convention; the column convention would use `axis=1`, which is exactly
what the assertion now catches.

### 2. The layer-1 z statistic decided nothing, and its bar was wrong

`verdict = w_ok == n_rows == shape_ok` — `layer1_z_rms_mean` was printed and
stored and **never compared to anything**. If rms z had been 675 the tool would
still have printed "MINT PARITY IS PROVEN". The LOG presented it as a check row.

Separately, `_gauss_max_expect` dropped the `1/t` factor from the Gaussian tail
equation and **overstated** E[max]: it returned 4.354 where the Skeptic's 4,000
simulated draws give **4.136 (sd 0.286)** at m = 16,384. My phrasing "4.52
against an expected 4.35" was therefore wrong; 4.52 is +1.3 sd from the true
expectation. Consistent either way, but the label was false.

**FIXED, both.** The approximation is replaced by the **exact** max-order-statistic
p-value `P(max of m iid |N(0,1)| >= z) = 1 - erf(z/sqrt2)^m`, computed stably via
`expm1`. And the statistic now **decides**: bars pre-stated as `rms z in
[0.90, 1.10]` and `P(max) >= 1e-6`, and `verdict` requires them.

The bar is defensible rather than convenient: under the null, rms z has sd
`~1/sqrt(2 * width * n)` = 0.0055 here, so `[0.90, 1.10]` is an **~18-sigma**
window — it cannot fire on noise. And it demonstrably fires on the error it
exists to catch. Measured on the real published rows:

| convention | rms z | max \|z\| | gate |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `axis=0`, column norm — **row-vector, ours** | **1.0120** | 3.59 | **PASS** |
| `axis=1`, row norm — column-vector, wrong | **674.8064** | 2302.99 | **FAIL** |

Current reading: **rms z 1.0017 PASS**, max \|z\| 4.52 with **exact P = 0.095**
— entirely unremarkable, which is the honest description.

### 3. A SECOND implementation of the score identity, inside a Phase-2 artifact

`p2_shape_smoke.py` computed `cb = flops_used / budget` and
`mult = max(floor, cb)` and wrote them to the artifact as `multiplier_min` /
`multiplier_max`. That is the score identity re-implemented in a module whose own
canonical evaluator forbids exactly that — and it **already disagreed** with the
canonical one, 0.0626 against 0.0684, because it used **counted** FLOPs where the
grader's multiplier is a function of **effective** compute `C = F + lambda*R`.

Today `max(0.1, .)` hid the disagreement. At a P2-CP3-class candidate near the
projected 0.087 counted, the artifact would have recorded `multiplier = 0.1`
while the canonical scorer used 0.0928 — and it would have **silently crossed the
floor at counted 0.095**. *(`docs/GOTCHAS.md`: counted compares to counted;
effective compares to effective.)*

**FIXED.** Both frames are now computed, labelled and stored separately, and the
multiplier comes from `competition_score.score_multiplier` on the effective
compute. Measured: counted `F/B = 0.062556`, effective `(F + lambda R)/B =
0.0710-0.0790`. The artifact now also carries `lambda_used`,
`lambda_provenance` ("PHASE-1 value 1e11; Phase-2 lambda is UNPUBLISHED"),
`residual_is_graded: false`, and the **floor margin** — residual would have to
exceed **0.823 s/MLP** to lift the multiplier off 0.1, so the claim carries its
own margin instead of asserting itself.

### 4. A durable-doc arithmetic error in the checkpoint's load-bearing paragraph

I wrote that the analytic closure is *"21x worse on raw MSE and 2.8x better on
score"*. **The 21x is wrong. It is 3.60x.**

`4.785849e-6 / 1.32794e-6 = 3.604`. With a 10x multiplier ratio, "2.8x better on
score" **forces** exactly "3.6x worse on raw MSE" — the three numbers in that one
sentence were internally inconsistent, and the inconsistency was visible without
any new data. The 2.774x score ratio and the 1.328e-6 naive figure are both
confirmed correct.

**CORRECTED in place.** The direction of the conclusion is unaffected.

Two caveats the Skeptic added, both now carried:

- **65,536 samples is not actually achievable.** The card calls the
  effective-sample figure *"an upper bound"* and says RNG, casts and accumulation
  cost *"another 0.4-1%"*. A real naive arm at 65,536 lands at `C/B > 1.0` ->
  `BudgetExhaustedError` -> **failure, multiplier 1.0 against zeroed
  predictions**, which is far worse than 1.33e-6. So the comparison is
  **conservative in our favour** — but it means the naive reference must be run
  at its true budget-maximal N, not at 65,536.
- It is a **measured** number against a **modelled** one, on n = 4 networks whose
  MSEs span 3.70e-6 to 5.89e-6. Legitimate as arithmetic; not a measurement.

### 5. The floor-dominance conclusion was stated as a RESTRICTION of the objective

I wrote: *"the Phase-2 objective is: minimise raw MSE subject to `C/B <= 0.1`."*
**That is not the objective.** The objective is `min MSE * max(0.1, C/B)`.

Above the floor a pure `1/N` sampler's score is **flat**: at `C/B = 0.1` naive MC
affords N = 6,554, giving MSE 1.328e-5 x 0.1 = **1.328e-6** — identical to its
value at `C/B = 1.0`. So the constrained form is correct *for 1/N methods* and
would **wrongly reject a superlinear-return arm above the floor**.

**RESTATED, and it changes how P2-CP1 must be run:** an arm at `C/B = 0.3` must
be **scored**, not rejected on sight. What is true is the weaker and still
strategically decisive statement: *for any method whose accuracy improves no
faster than 1/compute, all the value below `C/B = 0.1` is free, and no value is
lost by spending less than the floor.*

### 6. "0.10 and 0.12 price our primitives identically" — under-evidenced, and FALSE as stated about the price table

Three primitives is not a price table. The Skeptic replaced the claim from both
directions, and I have now turned its probe into a durable artifact,
`local_sim/p2_price_delta.py` -> `experiments/2026-08-21_phase2_manifest/p2_price_delta.json`.

**Much stronger than I claimed, for our candidate:**

| | flopscope 0.10.0 | flopscope 0.12.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| whole `estimator.py` `predict`, 1024x16 | **137,562,547,200** | **137,562,547,200** |
| ops compared / ops that moved | 16 | **0** |
| Skeptic's independent 256x32 full sampling path (`eigh`, `qr`, `norm.ppf`, `take`, `where`, `bitwise_xor`, f32+f64 matmul) | 354,001,749,470 | **354,001,749,470**, all 35 ops |

So `C/B = 0.0626` **does** transfer to 0.12 — for this op mix. That is a
statement about this candidate, not about the price table.

**And FALSE as a statement about the price table.** Of 30 probed primitives,
**4 moved**:

| primitive (256x256) | 0.10.0 | 0.12.0 | |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `nansum` f32 | 65,535 | **131,071** | 2.00x dearer |
| `nansum` f64 | 131,070 | **262,142** | 2.00x dearer |
| `nanmean` f32 | 65,536 | **131,072** | 2.00x dearer |
| **`where(mask, f32_array, 0.0)`** | 524,288 | **262,144** | **0.50x — half price** |

**The `where` row is the one that matters.** Mixing a **Python float scalar** with
a **float32 array** was billed at the float64 rate under 0.10 and is billed at the
float32 rate under 0.12 (NEP-50 weak promotion). That is precisely the spelling a
mixed-precision path produces — and this checkpoint's own headline cost lever is
*"a float32 covariance would halve `C/B` to ~0.031"*. **A float32 arm's `C/B`
measured on 0.10 can read up to 2x high on scalar-mixed ops.** The direction is
conservative (0.10 over-charges), but it is now a measured constraint on
reporting rather than an unexamined assumption.

**Binding for P2-CP1: every arm is priced under BOTH releases and reported with
both readings.** `p2_price_delta.py` is the tool.

### 7. Artifact immutability — the required outcome said "immutable", and it was not

`phase2_mint_parity.py` and `phase2_manifest.py` both wrote with a bare
`open(OUT, "w")`, and `p2_shape_smoke.py` called `os.remove(path)` **specifically
to bypass** `lifecycle_eval.write_evidence`'s refusal-to-overwrite.

The Skeptic destroyed committed evidence by running **the command printed in
`phase2_mint_parity.py`'s own docstring** (`--shard 1 --max-rows 4`): the 16-row
artifact was replaced by a 4-row one, 214 lines deleted. It caught this, verified
it with `git diff --stat`, and restored it. *An evidence file that a documented
invocation can shrink is not evidence.*

**FIXED, three ways:**
- one artifact per `(shard, rows)` and per `(candidate, shard, n)` — a 4-row run
  can no longer shadow a 16-row one;
- a rerun that would change content **REFUSES** with a readable message; a rerun
  producing identical content is a no-op;
- the `os.remove` bypass is deleted, with the reason in the code.

Verified by re-running the exact destructive command: it now writes
`phase2_mint_parity_shard1_rows4.json` and leaves shard 0 alone, and a second
identical run prints `artifact unchanged`.

### 8. `B = 2**41` was a hardcoded literal claiming the card as its source

`width` and `depth` are parsed from `metadata.json`; `B` was a constant. A re-bake
that moved the budget would have been invisible.

**FIXED.** `B` is now **parsed** from the card's Versions table (superscript
digits normalised) and **cross-checked against the card's own "Effective MC
samples" column** — the parse must satisfy `B / forward_flops_per_sample` equal to
a figure the card itself states, or the build refuses rather than guessing.
`phase2_manifest.py` also now **refuses to rebuild** if the `v2-phase2` tag points
at a different commit than the manifest on disk, unless `--allow-rebake` is given
deliberately.

### 9. Two smaller items, both accepted

- **`Restore-CallerEncoding` was not on every path.** A terminating error raised
  outside a `Step` block would leave the caller's shell mutated. **FIXED** with a
  script-scope `trap`.
- **The preflight comment claimed a falsifier the code cannot produce.** It said a
  caller that hard-sets `PYTHONIOENCODING` "must turn the gate RED HERE"; the
  Skeptic ran the gate with `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252` and got **GREEN 10/12**,
  because the export is unconditional — which is the *correct* behaviour (the
  gate owns the setting), but the comment was false. **FIXED**: the comment now
  says what the assertion actually catches, which is a toolchain that ignores the
  variable.
- **`competition_score.score_multiplier`'s docstring still said "the Phase-2 floor
  is not yet published".** **FIXED** — it is published, it is 0.1, and the
  docstring now says where.

### 10. Accepted and recorded, not fixed

- **`MLP.seed` (spawn[2]) is proven against installed 0.14, not against 0.16.**
  The published-bytes check covers spawn[0] only, because the dataset publishes
  weights and not the estimator seed. Irrelevant at 1024x16 today — the analytic
  path never reads `mlp.seed` — but **a P2-CP1 sampling arm will**, and it is a
  bit-reproducibility gap, not a correctness one.
- **`local_sim/phase2_manifest.py` was classified ROUTINE and is an instrument by
  function**: it is now the single source of `width`, `depth`, `flop_budget` and
  `floor` for every Phase-2 consumer. **Reclassified IMPORTANT going forward**;
  further edits get a written prediction. The original classification was
  defensible when it was a poller and stopped being so when things started
  importing it.
- **The strategist packet carries no provenance stamp** — who produced it, when,
  from what. Continuity rule 10 should want one.

## What did NOT change

No estimator edit. No seed block claimed. **Vault counter 1, touch log 1 line.**
Nothing submitted. Both smokes re-run after every fix: **9/9 assertions** for
`estimator.py` and for `estimator_v2_4_1.py`, MSE and cost unchanged to the digit.

# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP0.5 [IMPORTANT] the ledger's artifact hashes fail OPEN — PREDICTION, before the fix

*Class: IMPORTANT — `local_sim/seed_ledger.py` is enforcement, wired into
preflight steps 6 and 8. Written before the change exists. This is the last
P2-CP0 blocker that must close **before the first Phase-2 seed is claimed**,
because it is the mechanism that would record that claim.*

## The defect

`check_ledger` validates an artifact hash **only if one is present**:

```python
if c.artifact and c.artifact_sha256:
    now = _sha256(c.artifact)
    ...
```

A record that names an artifact and carries **no** hash passes silently. Two do:

| block | consumer | artifact | hash |
|---|---|---|---|
| D18 | `local_sim/coverage_lab.py` | `experiments/2026-08-19_coverage/truth_D18.npz` | **blank** |
| D18 | `local_sim/probe_oa_carrier.py` | `experiments/2026-08-19_carriers/oa_truth_D18.npz` | **blank** |

Both files exist on disk. The hole is structural, not accidental: `claim()`
records the artifact **path** before the artifact is written, so its hash is
*necessarily* blank at claim time, and nothing ever fills it in. That is the
"artifact finalization has fail-open paths" defect from the handoff, and it is
the one that would let a Phase-2 truth set be swapped after the arms were scored
against it.

## Predictions, committed before the change

- **L1.** Adding a `finalize()` that appends a `kind="finalize"` record carrying
  the artifact's sha256, and making `check_ledger` **error** on a `claim` that
  names an artifact with no hash from either source, turns `check_ledger` RED on
  exactly **2** records today and green after both are finalized.
- **L2.** `finalize()` **refuses** to record a hash for a file that does not
  exist, so it cannot manufacture a hash for an artifact that was never written.
- **L3.** `kind="finalize"` records are excluded from overlap and SINGLE_USE
  accounting, so finalizing does not look like a second claim. Specifically:
  D18's permitted-overlap report and the SINGLE_USE counts for D12/D14/D17/D19
  are **unchanged**, and D17/D19 still read as unspent.
- **L4.** `local_sim/test_seed_ledger.py` stays green and grows negative tests
  that **provoke** each new refusal rather than asserting it.
- **L5.** Preflight steps 6 and 8 stay green; the gate's verdict does not move.
- **L6.** A gitignored artifact that is absent from a fresh clone must **not**
  turn the gate red — the hash is checked against the record, and an absent file
  is reported, not failed. Otherwise this becomes the fifth "a check that reports
  a state rather than testing a property".

**Falsifier:** if closing the hole requires weakening any existing refusal, or if
any SINGLE_USE/overlap verdict moves, the design is wrong and is reverted.

---

# 2026-08-21 — SLICE CONTRACT P2-CP1: which family owns the Phase-2 frontier, on block **P01**  [PRE-REGISTERED, no data yet]

*Everything below is written before any Phase-2 seed has been claimed and before
any arm has been scored against any fresh truth. The only 1024 x 16 accuracy
number that exists at the time of writing is the P2-CP0.3 compatibility smoke on
**public** rows, which selects nothing.*

**Strategic question**
At 1024 x 16 with `B = 2^41` and a 0.1 multiplier floor, which estimator family
owns the accuracy/cost frontier — the analytic cumulant/closure family, or
sampling? And within the analytic family, how much of the remaining error is the
**post-ReLU covariance truncation** (removable, cheap) versus the **closure's
non-Gaussianity** (removable only by a K3/Edgeworth correction)?

**Current bottleneck**
Every Phase-2 accuracy number in this repository is either a projection or a
public-split compatibility readout. `docs/PHASE2_FRONTIER_ARCHITECTURE.md`
projects the raw closure near **9.8e-7**; the shipped closure **measures 4.79e-6**
on public rows, **4.9x worse**. The plan's ordering (deploy K2, then augmented K2,
then goal-directed K3) rests on that projection, and it has already failed once.
Nothing has been measured on fresh Phase-2 mints at all.

**Evidence**

- **CONFIRMED.** Mint parity at 1024 x 16, 16/16 bitwise against the organisers'
  published `v2-phase2` weights, 4/4 on a second shard
  (`experiments/2026-08-21_phase2_manifest/phase2_mint_parity_shard0_rows16.json`).
- **CONFIRMED.** `B = 2^41`, floor 0.1, no biases, no separate output layer,
  forward pass **33,554,432** FLOPs/sample measured under both flopscope releases.
- **CONFIRMED.** The shipped analytic path costs **`C/B` = 0.062556 counted**,
  effective 0.071–0.079, i.e. **under the floor**; residual would have to exceed
  **0.823 s/MLP** at λ = 1e11 to lift it off.
- **CONFIRMED.** The shipped closure's off-diagonal post-ReLU covariance,
  `c_ij Φ_i Φ_j`, is **exactly the first-order Price/Hermite truncation** of the
  exact map. Verified **bitwise** against `arm_k2p1`
  (`local_sim/p2_test_arms.py` T2). Higher orders cost O(n²) per layer against
  the O(n³) propagation — measured: order 6 costs `C/B` 0.063007 against order
  1's 0.062556, i.e. **+0.72%**.
- **CONFIRMED.** The series converges in the regime the network occupies: the
  closure's own pre-activation |r| has p99 rising 0.081 → 0.314 over the 16
  layers, and only 0.085% of pairs exceed 0.4 at the deepest layer. Order 3 is
  within 2.6e-4 relative at |r| = 0.2.
- **CONFIRMED.** The ladder is **not monotone**: `a_k = He_{k-2}(-α) φ(α)` changes
  sign with α, so where `a_3(α_i)` and `a_3(α_j)` have opposite signs the order-3
  rung overshoots — 22/150 grid points, e.g. α = (−0.3, 0.4), r = 0.6 where order
  2 is off by 8.8e-5 and order 3 by 5.2e-4.
- **CONFIRMED.** Sampling costs 33,587,196 FLOPs/sample end to end (+0.10%
  overhead, **not** the card's 0.4–1%). Budget-maximal N = 62,190 at `C/B` 0.95;
  floor-maximal N = 6,546.
- **INFERRED (arithmetic, not measured).** From the published `avg_variance`
  ≈ 0.0870, naive MC has raw MSE `0.087/N`; at N = 6,546 that is 1.33e-5 at
  multiplier 0.1, i.e. adjusted **1.33e-6**, and at N = 62,190 it is 1.40e-6 at
  multiplier 0.95, i.e. **1.33e-6** again — the flat-score law.
- **SPECULATIVE.** That the Hermite correction is small relative to the closure's
  total error. The order-1 → order-2 shift is 2.55e-4 relative on the final
  layer and the ladder plateaus by order 3, but **shift is not error**: a shift
  toward the truth and a shift away from it look identical without truth.

**Hypothesis**

**H1.** The analytic family owns the Phase-2 frontier. `k2p1` beats every
sampling arm on canonical arithmetic score by **more than 2x**, because it sits
under the floor while sampling's score is flat.

**H2.** The Hermite ladder is a **small** win that converges by order 3.
`k2p2` beats `k2p1` on arithmetic score, `k2p3`/`k2p4`/`k2p6` add little beyond
`k2p2`, and **no rung reaches 1.25x**. Therefore *"augmented K2" as ARC's paper
frames it cannot be the aggressive candidate*, and the aggressive lane must be
K3/non-Gaussian.

**H3.** The residual error is dominated by the closure's **non-Gaussianity**, not
by its covariance truncation. Operationally: `MSE(k2p6) / MSE(k2p1) > 0.7`.

**H4.** The flat-score law holds: `sample_iid_max` and `sample_iid_floor` score
within 10% of each other despite a 9.5x budget difference.

**Mechanism**
The score is `MSE × max(0.1, C/B)`. Any estimator under `C/B` = 0.1 pays the same
multiplier, so accuracy bought below the floor is free — and the whole analytic
family sits at 0.063. A `1/N` sampler's score `(V/N)(Nc/B) = Vc/B` is independent
of N, so sampling cannot buy its way past the floor. Within the analytic family,
Price's theorem gives the post-ReLU covariance exactly as
`Σ_k c^k/(k!(σ_iσ_j)^{k−1}) a_k(α_i) a_k(α_j)`, so the truncation error is a
known, cheap, removable quantity — and what is left once it is removed is the
Gaussian assumption itself.

**Intervention**
Score eleven arms — `k1`, `k2p1`, `k2p2`, `k2p3`, `k2p4`, `k2p6`, `k2p1_f32`,
`sample_iid_max`, `sample_iid_floor`, `sample_orth`, `sample_lattice` — over the
**same** fresh 1024 x 16 networks through the **one** canonical evaluator
(`lifecycle_eval.evaluate`), against **two independent truth replicas**. Every arm
differs from `k2p1` in exactly one place. Nothing is fitted.

**Prediction (builder's, committed before the numbers exist)**

| # | prediction |
|---|---|
| **P1** | `k2p1` beats `sample_iid_floor` on arithmetic score by **2.0x – 4.0x** |
| **P2** | `sample_iid_max` and `sample_iid_floor` agree within **10%** |
| **P3** | `k2p2` beats `k2p1`, arithmetic gain in **[1.02, 1.20]**, t interval excluding zero |
| **P4** | `k2p6` beats `k2p2` by less than **1.03x** — the ladder plateaus |
| **P5** | `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) > 0.7` — covariance truncation is the minority of the error |
| **P6** | `k2p1_f32` costs **0.0606** counted and loses **less than 1%** of score |
| **P7** | `sample_orth` beats `sample_iid_floor` on raw MSE but **loses on score**, because its QR pushes `C/B` to 0.1093 and off the floor |
| **P8** | `k1` is **10x – 40x** worse than `k2p1` on raw MSE |
| **P9** | 0 failures on every arm; `sample_iid_max` does not exhaust the budget |
| **P10** | the depth curve's layer-1 column is identical across all arms and equals the truth-noise floor — layer 1 is exact for every arm, so that column is a built-in calibration of the whole measurement |

**Gate** — frozen now, passed to `decide(gate=...)`, which has no default

- **The conservative statistic is the arithmetic mean of per-MLP canonical scores**
  from `competition_score`, and the arm that owns the frontier is the one that
  minimises it.
- **Deployment gate for P2-CP2** (the conservative candidate): the winning arm
  must beat `k2p1` — the currently shipped algorithm — with **arithmetic gain
  ≥ 1.10x** and a **studentised-t 95% interval on the paired difference excluding
  zero**, with **zero failures**. Below 1.10x, keep `k2p1` and record the ladder as
  a measured negative.
- **Aggressive-lane trigger for P2-CP4:** `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) > 0.7`, i.e. the
  Hermite ladder leaves most of the error standing. If instead that ratio is
  **< 0.3**, the covariance truncation *was* the error, P2-CP3 becomes the whole
  aggressive lane, and **K3 is deprioritised**.
- **Sampling-lane kill:** if the best sampling arm's score exceeds the best
  analytic arm's by **more than 1.5x**, the sampling architecture is closed for
  Phase 2 and `_PRUNE_TAU` / `_BASIS_RANK` are **never refitted**.

**Falsifier**

- **H1 falsified** if any sampling arm's arithmetic score is at or below `k2p1`'s.
  Then the floor argument is wrong or `avg_variance` is not what the card says,
  and the whole checkpoint order has to be rebuilt.
- **H2 falsified** if any Hermite rung reaches **1.25x** over `k2p1`. Then
  augmented K2 *is* the aggressive candidate and P2-CP3 is promoted ahead of CP4.
- **H3 falsified** if `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) < 0.3`.
- **H4 falsified** if the two iid arms differ by more than 10%; then the flat law
  is broken at this operating point, exactly as it was at Phase 1 (T2, 2026-08-19),
  and every argument resting on it must be re-derived.

**Baseline**
`arm_k2p1`, which is **BITWISE** the shipped `estimator.py` `_analytic_only` path
at 1024 x 16 (`p2_test_arms.py` T2, max abs diff 0.000e+00). Tier: **DECIDE**,
fresh mints on a new single-use-free DESIGN block.

**Residual model** — REQUIRED, frozen here by name

Three readings will be reported; **the deciding model is COUNTED FLOPs ONLY**, and
the freeze is recorded here before the block is touched:

1. **counted FLOPs only** — **FROZEN AS THE DECIDING MODEL.**
2. local measured residual at λ = 1e11 — reported, never decides (this machine
   runs 4.3–7.7x the grader's).
3. the graded line `residual ≈ 2.551 ms + 5.780 µs/op` — reported, and flagged
   as **doubly stale**: it was fitted on five *Phase-1* submissions at 256 x 32
   under flopscope 0.10.

Counted FLOPs is the right freeze **here and only here**, for a stated reason
rather than convenience: every arm in this ladder sits at `C/B` between 0.00006
and 0.95, and all the analytic arms are **under the 0.1 floor by a factor of 1.6**,
so the multiplier is pinned at 0.1 for them regardless of any residual model that
does not add 0.823 s/MLP. The cost half therefore cannot change the ranking of the
analytic arms at all, and the sampling arms are separated by counted cost by
construction. **This freeze does not transfer to P2-CP2 or later**, where a
candidate may sit near the floor and the residual price becomes live again.

**Statistic**
Paired on common random numbers — every arm sees the same networks and the same
truth. Binding: **arithmetic** paired score difference with the studentised-t 95%
interval via `competition_score.decide()`. Geometric gain, estimand disagreement
and biggest-mover share are reported as **diagnostics with no authority**.
Percentile and BCa are refused by `decide()` itself. **One shift**: no arm here is
randomised over point-set shifts, and the sampling arms derive their randomness
from `mlp.seed` alone, so shift-averaging does not apply — this is stated because
it is a real limitation on the sampling arms' precision, not an omission.

**Truth and its noise**
Two independent replicas per network, spawned from the evaluator's own sampling
substream, at **2^22 = 4,194,304** samples each. Measured on a probe: replica
disagreement 3.588e-8 against the predicted `2V/N` of 3.540e-8, **ratio 1.0137**,
so independence is measured rather than assumed. Truth noise per replica
**1.77e-8 ≈ 0.37%** of the expected signal. Both ordinary MSEs and the
**cross-product** estimate `mean_j (p_j − y1_j)(p_j − y2_j)` are reported.

**Confounders, and what is done about each**

1. *An arm wins because it is cheaper, not better.* Both frames are reported
   separately and the multiplier comes only from `competition_score`.
2. *The ladder's rungs differ in more than one place.* They are **generated** from
   one source, so they cannot drift; `--check` fails on drift.
3. *Truth noise inflates every MSE equally.* The cross-product estimate removes
   it; layer 1 is exact for every arm, so the depth curve's L1 column is an
   independent read of the noise floor.
4. *A sampling arm gets lucky on one realisation.* Reported with its per-MLP
   spread and sign test; and the two iid arms at 9.5x different N cross-check.
5. *flopscope 0.10 mis-prices a Phase-2 arm.* Every arm's cost is measured under
   **both** 0.10 and 0.12 and any move is printed.
6. *Public leakage.* The ladder reads a fresh DESIGN truth file and nothing else.
   No public number enters any decision.

## Samuel's prediction — recorded 2026-08-21, BEFORE the block was claimed

Asked the three questions `ai/workflows/slice-contract.md` step 4 requires, with
the measured context in front of him and no result in existence.

| question | Samuel's answer |
|---|---|
| Which family owns the Phase-2 frontier, and by how much? | **Analytic wins big (>2x).** Agrees with the builder's P1 (2.0x–4.0x) |
| The shipped closure is the first-order truncation of an exact series; higher orders cost ~0.7% more. What does that buy? | **A small win that plateaus fast.** Agrees with the builder's P3 (1.02–1.20x at order 2) and P4 (order 6 adds < 1.03x over order 2) |
| Anything to change before the block is spent? | **Go, but more networks.** |

**Builder and human agree on both substantive predictions.** That is worth
naming rather than glossing: it means this slice has *low* expected information
if it comes out as predicted, and *high* information if it does not. The
falsifiers in the contract are therefore the load-bearing part of it, and the
result section must lead with whichever of H1–H4 came closest to breaking.

### The one contract change, and its consequence

**n = 48 -> n = 96 networks.** Nothing else in the contract moves: same arms,
same gate, same frozen residual model, same block, same truth design.

- Resolution on the paired difference improves as `1/sqrt(n)`, so roughly
  **+-10% -> +-7%**.
- It costs **GPU minutes, not seeds**: P01 has 600, and 96 leaves 504 free for
  P2-CP2's disjoint DECIDE draw. Truth generation goes ~8.4 min -> ~17 min.
- The ladder run roughly doubles. See the driver note below, which recovers most
  of that.

### A driver change made BEFORE the run, and why it is a correction rather than a convenience

The driver as first written ran each arm **twice**: once through
`lifecycle_eval.evaluate` for the score, and once again outside the budget to
recover per-MLP predictions for the cross-product noise correction and the
depth curve. At n = 96 that second pass is about ninety minutes of pure
duplication.

It is also unnecessary, by an exact identity. Writing `ybar = (y1 + y2)/2`:

```text
  mean[(p - y1)(p - y2)]  =  mean[(p - ybar)^2]  -  mean[((y1 - y2)/2)^2]
```

— expand both sides; the cross terms cancel identically. So the **cross-product
noise-corrected MSE is the ordinary MSE against the AVERAGED replica, minus a
constant that depends only on the truth and not at all on the prediction.** The
evaluator already computes the first term, and the second is measured once from
the truth file.

Three consequences, all of them improvements:

1. **One scored pass per arm**, so there is exactly one set of numbers per arm and
   no possibility of the two passes disagreeing.
2. The subtracted constant `mean[((y1-y2)/2)^2]` **is** the noise of the averaged
   replica, `V / (2N)`, so the correction is now a *measured* quantity with a
   *predicted* value to check it against, rather than an estimate.
3. The bias it removes is **identical across arms**, so it cancels exactly in the
   paired difference — which is the binding statistic. The correction therefore
   changes no comparison; it only makes the **absolute** MSEs quotable next to
   the packet's projection, which is what P2-CP1 has to do.

The depth curve still needs full prediction arrays, so it is computed on a fixed
**subset of 8** networks rather than all 96. A mechanism curve does not need 96
networks, and saying so here is cheaper than pretending it does.

**Nothing about the gate, the arms, the statistic or the frozen residual model
changed.** The contract above stands as written apart from `n`.

*96 fresh 1024 x 16 networks, block P01[40,821,001,000 .. 40,821,001,095], two
independent truth replicas at 2^22 samples each. Eleven arms, one canonical
evaluator, paired on common random numbers. **Zero failures in 1,056
network-evaluations.** No vault touch. `estimator.py` untouched. The contract was
registered before any seed was claimed and is unmodified apart from `n = 48 -> 96`,
recorded with Samuel's prediction.*

## The result, in one line

**The analytic family owns the Phase-2 frontier by 2.57x, and 95% of its
remaining error is the Gaussian closure assumption itself — not the covariance
truncation we have been shipping.** The sampling architecture is closed for
Phase 2 and the aggressive lane is K3/Edgeworth, both by their own pre-registered
triggers.

## The four hypotheses — all CONFIRMED

**H1 — the analytic family owns the frontier: CONFIRMED at 2.566x.**
`k2p1` 4.16474e-07 against the best *valid* sampling arm `sample_orth` at
1.06853e-06. Against `sample_iid_floor` it is 2.714x and against
`sample_iid_max` 2.765x; **2.566x is the conservative reading and the one
quoted**, because it is measured against the strongest sampling arm rather than
the most convenient. The margin does not depend on the broken lattice arm.

*(An earlier draft of this entry quoted 2.711x here while naming `sample_orth`
as the comparator. That was 2.714x — the `sample_iid_floor` figure — attached to
the wrong arm. Corrected before the entry landed; the exact per-arm gains are in
`ladder_frozen.json`.)*

**H2 — the Hermite ladder is a small win that converges: CONFIRMED.**
Order 2 gives **1.0518x**, t-interval **[+4.31%, +5.53%]**, better on **93 of 96**,
sign-test **p = 0.000**. Orders 3, 4 and 6 give 1.0519x — identical to five
significant figures. **Order 2 delivers 99.7% of the entire ladder.** No rung
reaches 1.25x, so augmented K2 cannot be the aggressive candidate.

**H3 — the residual error is the closure's NON-GAUSSIANITY: CONFIRMED at 0.951.**
`MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) = 0.9506` against a trigger of > 0.70. This is the
checkpoint's most consequential number and it deserves its own paragraph below.

**H4 — the flat-score law: CONFIRMED at 1.87%** (frozen model; 1.20% under the effective model, which is what an earlier draft quoted).
`sample_iid_max` (N = 62,190, C/B 0.95) and `sample_iid_floor` (N = 6,546,
C/B 0.10) score within **1.87%** of each other across a **9.5x budget
difference**. A 1/N sampler cannot buy its way past the floor, so there is no
sampling operating point that helps.

## The finding that reshapes the plan

`k2p6` is not another rung — it is the **limit** of the Gaussian-closure family.
The Price/Hermite series converges to the *exact* post-ReLU covariance under the
Gaussian model, and by order 3 it has converged to five figures. So
`MSE(k2p6)` is the floor of everything reachable by improving the covariance map.

**That floor is 95.06% of where we already are.** The exact map removes **4.94%**
of the error. The other **95%** is the assumption that the post-ReLU state is
Gaussian, which no covariance spelling can touch.

Three consequences, and they are the plan:

1. **P2-CP3 as the packet frames it is capped at 1.052x.** Not "probably small" —
   *capped*, because the limit was measured directly rather than approached.
   The lane can be closed on this evidence without building it.
2. **The aggressive lane must attack non-Gaussianity**: P2-CP4's K3/Edgeworth
   correction. The contract's trigger anticipated exactly this and fired.
3. **The packet's accuracy projection is now explained, not merely falsified.**
   It projected the Phase-2 closure near 9.8e-7 by scaling Phase 1; the measured
   value is 4.16e-6. The gap cannot be recovered by a better closure, because we
   have measured the closure family's floor and we are within 5% of it.

## The mechanism curve — why the frontier flipped, and what would flip it back

Every arm returns all 16 layers, so the depth profile is free. Correcting for the
fact that a genuine depth-`L` network affords `N ∝ 1/L` samples at fixed `B`:

| depth | analytic MSE | sampling MSE | ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 1.47e-07 | 9.45e-06 | 64.3 |
| 4 | 8.41e-07 | 1.09e-05 | 13.0 |
| 8 | 2.34e-06 | 1.30e-05 | 5.5 |
| 12 | 3.25e-06 | 1.24e-05 | 3.8 |
| **16** | **3.98e-06** | **1.19e-05** | **3.0** |

**The two families move in opposite directions with depth.** Sampling MSE is
nearly flat — which is the organisers' budget calibration working exactly as
designed, holding ~65k naive samples at every phase. Analytic MSE **grows 27x**
from L2 to L16. The ratio falls as `L^-1.44`, extrapolating to a crossover near
**depth 30 at width 1024**.

Phase 2's depth 16 sits on the analytic side with a **3x margin**. **Two things
this does NOT say:** the crossover is an extrapolation past the data, and it does
not retro-explain Phase 1, where the width also moved (256, not 1024).

**Explicit comparison with ARC's projection, as the contract required.** Their
`MSE_K ~ c_K (L/n)^K` predicts error `~ L^K` with `K = 2`. **Measured exponent on
depth: 1.52** (log-log, L = 2..16; L16/L2 is 27.1x where `L^2` predicts 64x).
The scaling law is directionally right and quantitatively optimistic in our
favour, on one shape at one width. It is a comparison, not a confirmation.

**P10 confirmed, and it is the measurement's own calibration:** the depth curve's
L1 column reads **8.216e-08 for all eleven arms**, because layer 1 is exact for
every one of them. That column is a direct read of the truth-noise floor, built
into the experiment rather than asserted beside it.

result here is one network's story.

**`k2p1_f32` is a case worth naming: its interval EXCLUDES ZERO and it is still a
draw.** The difference is `[1.7e-13, 7.9e-13]` on scores of 4.16e-07 — six orders
of magnitude below anything that could matter, and better on 57 of 96. Statistical
significance without practical significance, and the gate refuses it on the gain
regardless. This is what a correctly-built gate looks like when it is handed a
true null with enough `n` to resolve float noise.

**1. DEPLOYMENT GATE — `k2p2` FAILS it, and the conservative candidate stays `k2p1`.**
The gate was **>= 1.10x** with a t-interval excluding zero. `k2p2` measures
**1.0519x**, interval [+4.31%, +5.53%], 93/96, p = 0.000. The effect is real,
statistically unambiguous, and **below its own bar**. Registered consequence
honoured: **keep `k2p1`.**

**I flagged before the run that this gate may be the wrong instrument, and the
result makes that concrete.** `k2p2` costs **+0.18%** of counted FLOPs, stays
pinned at the floor, and is the strictly more correct mathematics — the same
series carried one term further. A 1.10x bar is calibrated for a change that
*spends* something. **I am not moving a gate after seeing data.** The decision of
whether cost-free changes deserve a separate, lower bar belongs in P2-CP2's
contract and is Samuel's. Stated plainly: at a 1.02x bar `k2p2` would pass
comfortably, and nothing else about the evidence would change.

**2. AGGRESSIVE-LANE TRIGGER — FIRES.** `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) = 0.9506 > 0.70`.
**P2-CP4 (goal-directed K3/Edgeworth) is the aggressive lane.** P2-CP3 is capped
at 1.052x and cannot carry it.

**3. SAMPLING-LANE KILL — FIRES at 2.699x against a 1.5x bar.**
Best analytic `k2p6` 3.95928e-07 against best valid sampling `sample_orth`
1.06853e-06.
**The sampling architecture is CLOSED for Phase 2. `_PRUNE_TAU` and `_BASIS_RANK`
are never refitted** — that work item, carried since the shape changed, is
retired.

*The one caveat this kill deserves, stated rather than buried:* the arms tested
are iid and orthogonal. **A working QMC arm was not tested** (see below), so the
kill rests on the best sampling arm *measured*, not the best *possible*. To close
a 2.699x gap, a QMC carrier would need a **2.7x variance reduction over iid at
N = 6,546 in 1024 dimensions** — a large ask at that effective dimension, and one
Phase-1's own carrier audit never approached (every input-space device there
measured between 0.98x and 1.09x). The lane is closed on the registered trigger;
reopening it needs that 2.7x demonstrated, which is a high and explicit bar.

## An arm that FAILED, and why it is reported rather than repaired

**`sample_lattice` is INVALID — an implementation defect in my generator, not a
result about QMC.** It scored 1.1037e-03, ~100x worse than plain iid.

Diagnosed: the Korobov generating vector is `a_j = base^j mod N` with
`base = (N//3) | 1 = 2183` at `N = 6546`. **2183^2 = 4,765,489 = 728 x 6546 + 1**,
so 2183 is its own inverse mod 6546 and the multiplicative cycle length is **2**.
The 1024 components are `[1, 2183, 1, 2183, ...]` — **two distinct values**. The
"1024-dimensional lattice" is effectively 2-dimensional.

**It is kept in the ladder and reported as invalid rather than dropped.**
Excluding an arm after seeing it fail is post-hoc arm selection, and a repaired
lattice arm would be a *new* measurement needing its own registration. **No
conclusion in this entry rests on it**: it was worse than every other sampling
arm, so the sampling-lane kill is unaffected either way.

## Prediction scorecard — 7 hits, 3 misses

| # | prediction | measured | |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `k2p1` beats sampling 2.0-4.0x | **2.566x** vs the best arm | HIT |
| P2 | the two iid arms agree within 10% | **1.20%** | HIT |
| P3 | `k2p2` gain [1.02, 1.20], CI excludes zero | **1.0518x, [+4.31%,+5.53%]** | HIT |
| P4 | `k2p6` beats `k2p2` by < 1.03x | **1.000136x** | HIT |
| P5 | `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) > 0.7` | **0.9506** | HIT |
| P6 | `k2p1_f32` costs 0.0606, loses < 1% | 0.060602, 1.0000x | **MISS — right number, wrong reason** |
| P7 | `sample_orth` wins on MSE, LOSES on score | wins on **both** (1.0574x on score) | **MISS** |
| P8 | `k1` is 10-40x worse on raw MSE | **54.7x** | **MISS — outside the band** |
| P9 | zero failures on every arm | **0/96 on all 11** | HIT |
| P10 | depth-curve L1 identical = noise floor | **8.216e-08 on all 11** | HIT |

**Samuel predicted both substantive outcomes correctly** — analytic wins big
(>2x, measured **2.566x** against the best sampling arm) and the Hermite ladder
is a small win that plateaus fast
(1.0518x, plateaued at order 2). Builder and human agreed in advance, so the
slice's information is concentrated in the three misses and in H3.

**The most instructive miss is P6, and it is instructive because it was
numerically right.** I predicted `k2p1_f32` would cost 0.0606 counted; it costs
0.060602. But the reasoning was that this is a float32 path, and **it is not**:
`stats.norm.cdf(float32) -> float64` (flopscope >= 0.10, forum 18127), and
`outer(Phi,Phi) * cov` then drags the covariance to float64, so every matmul from
layer 1 onward runs at rate 2.0. Casting back after the stats call gives the real
number: **C/B 0.031294, exactly 0.5003x float64**, at an accuracy cost of
**4.975e-07 relative L2** — four orders of magnitude below the prediction error,
i.e. free.

*This buys no score today* (both are floor-pinned) *and it is not a lever.* What
it buys is **headroom**: free budget under the floor goes from
`0.1 - 0.0626 = 0.0374 B` to `0.1 - 0.0313 = 0.0687 B`, **1.84x more room** for
exactly the K3 correction H3 just made the whole aggressive lane. That makes it a
P2-CP2 deployment detail and a P2-CP4 enabler.

`docs/GOTCHAS.md`: *before quoting an agreement, ask whether the two sides could
ever have disagreed.* A prediction that lands for the wrong reason is the same
trap wearing a different hat.

## Measured alongside, independent of the ladder's outcome

- **Grader-legality is VERIFIED, not asserted.** `whest validate` passes on all
  eight arms tested. The winning arm can become `estimator.py` for P2-CP2 with no
  re-port — which is why the generator emits self-contained files.
- **Peak memory 129-209 MB**, i.e. **0.20-0.32%** of the 65,536 MB package
  default (python-heap lower bound; the grader's limit is RLIMIT_AS over the whole
  address space). Memory is not a constraint for this family — unlike v2.5, which
  this limit killed at 3.9 GB, and unlike a full K3 tensor at 8.6 GB.
- **flopscope 0.10 vs 0.12**: every arm's counted cost was measured under both.
  All eleven agree to the unit.
- **A cost lever priced at zero:** the K2 arms emit `SymmetryLossWarning`, so
  flopscope's symmetry discount is forgone. Not worth taking — the discount
  applies to the O(n^2) elementwise ops, and 99.9% of the cost is the two O(n^3)
  matmuls, which flopscope prices **by shapes only**.

## What this does NOT establish

- **Nothing about the grader.** Package parity is still BLOCKED; every cost here
  is counted FLOPs under a flopscope the Phase-2 stack may not use. `lambda` is
  still unpublished, and the frozen deciding model sidesteps it rather than
  resolving it.
- **Nothing about a QMC carrier.** See the invalid arm.
- **Nothing about K3.** H3 says where the error *is*; it does not say a K3
  correction can *reach* it affordably. That is P2-CP4's question and it is open.
- **Nothing about the private re-run.** 96 networks at one shape.
- The crossover depth ~30 is an **extrapolation past the data**.
