# 2026-08-21 — P2-CP1 REVIEW: independent Skeptic **PROVISIONAL**. One inference RETRACTED, and the omitted half of the cost was the important half

*The Skeptic ran read-only at `f1d7abb` with the contract, the result, both JSON
artifacts and the code. It re-derived the Price/Hermite mathematics from scratch,
reimplemented the closure in plain numpy, and checked convergence against
`scipy.integrate.quad` rather than against our own quadrature. Verdict
**PROVISIONAL**.*

## What it could NOT break — and it tried hard

- **`arm_k2p1` is bitwise the shipped path at EIGHT shapes**, not just the one I
  checked: 1024x16, 256x32, 1024x8, 512x16, 64x4, **1023x16**, 2048x4, 1024x2.
  Max abs diff 0.000e+00 everywhere. The control is stronger than I claimed.
- **The Price/Hermite derivation is correct.** `a_k = He_{k-2}(-alpha) phi(alpha)`
  is `E[f^(k)]` after the sigma-scaling; the `cs` accumulator really is
  `c^k/(sigma_i sigma_j)^(k-1)` after rung k; `inv_ss` is not off by a factor;
  the diagonal is never taken from the series.
- **`k2p6` genuinely IS the Gaussian-closure limit.** Independent reimplementation
  at orders 6, 8, 12 and **20** gives results identical to **7 significant
  figures**. Adaptive quadrature confirms convergence to the exact bivariate-ReLU
  covariance: order 20 exact to 1e-10..1e-15, order 6 within 6e-5 relative over
  the observed regime, order 1 off by 1.3-11%. **The plateau is convergence, not
  numerically-dead terms** — which was the specific alternative I asked it to test.
- **The noise identity holds to <= 2.7e-20** on all 11 arms x 96 networks, and
  cancels in paired comparisons as claimed (H1 2.566 -> 2.569, kill 2.699 -> 2.702).
- **`sample_orth` is a correct N(0,I) sampler**: 256,000 draws at width 64 give
  var 1.0006, `E[x^4]` 3.004, `E[|x|^2]` 64.04 against 64, `Var[|x|^2]` 128.06
  against 128, within-basis max |cos| 2.4e-8. The 1.156x variance reduction is real.
- **All ten `decide()` verdicts reproduce to four decimals** from `per_mlp_score`,
  CIs and mover shares included.
- **Protocol clean, verified from git rather than prose.** Contract `32a3a2f`
  05:33 -> prediction + `n 48->96` + driver change `193e305` 10:17 -> block claim
  `4c97139` 10:30 -> truth finalize 10:36 -> result `f1d7abb` 12:00. **Both
  contract changes precede the claim.** The contract text at `32a3a2f` is
  **byte-identical** to HEAD apart from the appended prediction: the gate did not
  move. Nothing chosen on public data. Vault 1 touch, log 1 line, tree clean.

## 1. RETRACTED: I closed P2-CP3 using a measurement of a different method

**This is the review's lead finding and it is correct.**

I wrote: *"P2-CP3 as the packet frames it is capped at 1.052x ... The lane can be
closed on this evidence without building it."*

**It cannot.** `docs/PHASE2_FRONTIER_ARCHITECTURE.md:202` defines augmented K2 as
*"keeps additional leading **Edgeworth** diagrams while preserving `O(n^3 L)`"*,
priced at `11 n^3 L` against simple K2's `7 n^3 L` — **1.57x the FLOPs**. My
Hermite ladder refines the post-ReLU covariance **under the Gaussian assumption**,
costs `O(n^2)` per layer, and measures **1.0072x** the FLOPs of `k2p1`.

**The cost signature alone proves they are different objects: 1.007x measured
against 1.57x specified.**

So `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) = 0.951` caps **covariance-map** work. It says nothing
about an Edgeworth correction — which by my own H3 finding is aimed at exactly
the 95% the ladder leaves standing. **The entry concluded "the aggressive lane
must attack non-Gaussianity" and then closed, unmeasured, the cheapest available
non-Gaussianity lane.** Those two sentences cannot both stand.

**P2-CP3 is REOPENED.** What P2-CP1 actually established about it: *a correction
that only improves the Gaussian-closure covariance map is capped at 1.052x.* That
is a real and useful result. It is not a result about Edgeworth diagrams.

**The generalisable error:** I named an arm after a plan item and then let the
name carry the inference. `k2p2` was labelled "augmented K2" in my own arm
docstring, and from there "the ladder is capped" became "augmented K2 is capped"
without anyone re-checking that they were the same thing. **When an arm is named
after a plan item, verify the arm implements the item — the cost polynomial is
the cheapest check and it was available the whole time.**

## 2. The omitted half of the cost, and it is the half that binds P2-CP4

The Evidence Packet reported counted FLOPs and did not report the residual
column that was sitting in its own artifact. Charged at the Phase-1 lambda:

| arm | F/B | resid mean | resid max | eff C/B mean | eff C/B max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `k2p1` | 0.0626 | 151 ms | 364 ms | 0.0694 | 0.0791 |
| `k2p2` | 0.0627 | 268 ms | 391 ms | 0.0748 | 0.0804 |
| `k2p4` | 0.0628 | 190 ms | 456 ms | 0.0715 | 0.0836 |
| **`k2p6`** | **0.0630** | **763 ms** | **1595 ms** | **0.0977** | **0.1356** |

**`k2p6` does +404% residual for +0.72% counted FLOPs, and goes OFF THE 0.1
FLOOR** — 0.0977 mean, 0.1356 max.

**This contradicts my own contract's justification for the counted-only freeze**,
which said *"no residual model that does not add 0.823 s/MLP can reorder them"*.
`k2p6` adds **0.61 s/MLP** over `k2p1`. The freeze was defensible for *ranking*
the arms — every verdict stands — but I used it to stop looking, and the thing it
hid was the mechanism that killed the packed lane: flopscope charges the
**release of a large temporary** as residual wall time (~100-120 us/op, forum
18101) while pricing the operation at `O(n^2)` FLOPs. Five extra elementwise
passes over 1024^2 arrays per layer are nearly free in the frozen model and
expensive in reality.

**Binding consequence for P2-CP4: a K3/Edgeworth correction is
elementwise-heavy in exactly the same way.** Its counted cost will understate it.
**P2-CP4's contract must freeze a residual model that can see this, and must
report the residual ratio to the control alongside every counted number.**

**A second, independent reason to prefer order 2** — `k2p2` stays under the floor
on effective cost (0.0748 / 0.0804) and `k2p6` does not. "Order 2 delivers 99.7%
of the ladder" was an accuracy statement; it is now also a cost statement, and the
two agree.

**Repaired in code**, not just noted: `p2_lab.py` now prints a FLOOR CHECK naming
any arm that is under the floor on counted cost and over it on effective cost,
reports each arm's residual ratio to the control, and records mean/max residual in
the artifact.

## 3. The mechanism section is not reproducible from the artifact of record

Three defects, all mine:

- **The depth table in the Evidence Packet came from `ladder.json`** — the
  `lambda = 1e11` first pass — while the entry names `ladder_frozen.json` as "the
  artifact of record". The frozen file's `mse_by_depth` is **one network** (I ran
  it with `--depth-subset 1` to save time), not the eight the table implies, and
  **neither file recorded `depth_subset`**, so a reader could not tell.
  **Repaired:** the artifact now records `mse_by_depth_n_networks`.
- **The noise correction used the layer-1 constant at every depth.** Truth noise
  is layer-dependent (8.22e-8 at L1 falling to 8.26e-9 at L16), so subtracting the
  L1 value over-subtracts by 9.4% at L2 and 1.8% at L16 — and the sampling column
  got no subtraction at all. With per-layer noise on both columns the **analytic
  depth exponent is 1.515, not 1.567**, and the crossover is 30.5 rather than 29.8.
  **The bias ran toward ARC's K = 2, i.e. against my own conclusion**, so the
  direction survives. **Quote 1.52, not 1.567.**
- **"Sampling MSE is nearly flat — the organisers' budget calibration working
  exactly as designed" is a NON-SEQUITUR.** My correction holds `B` fixed
  (`N ∝ 1/L`); the organisers' calibration does the opposite (`B ∝ L`, holding
  `N` constant). The flatness comes from `V_L/L` being roughly constant in these
  networks. **Under the organisers' actual rule the crossover is ~22, not ~30** —
  still comfortably above depth 16, but the margin is smaller than I implied and
  the explanation was wrong.

*One thing the Skeptic checked that I had only asserted:* `canonical_mint(1024, 4, s)`
returns weight matrices **bit-identical** to the first four of
`canonical_mint(1024, 16, s)`, so "layer L of a depth-16 network" really is a
depth-L network for the analytic arm. That premise holds.

## 4. Frame mixing, four places, and one of them survived my own correction

`docs/VALIDATION.md` 2b: *counted compares to counted; effective compares to
effective.* The Evidence Packet mixed them:

- the headline table's `vs k2p1` column for the sampling arms is the **effective**
  model while its `score` column for those arms is the **frozen** model;
- **H4's "1.20%" is the effective reading; under the frozen deciding model it is
  1.87%.** Still far inside the 10% bar, but the quoted number was from the wrong
  model;
- P7's "1.0574x" is effective (frozen: 1.0579x);
- **P1's "2.711x" survived in the scorecard and the closing paragraph *after* I
  wrote a correction note saying the figure is 2.714x / 2.566x.** 2.711
  reproduces from neither artifact. A correction that does not propagate to every
  instance of the number is not a correction.

**All four corrected in the entry above.**

## 5. Claims the artifacts did not support

- **"Peak memory 129-209 MB"** — `p2_lab.py`'s own docstring promised peak memory
  and **the code never measured or recorded it**. The numbers came from an ad-hoc
  probe outside the pipeline, and no artifact contains them, while the contract
  and `CURRENT_STATE.md` both require the figure. **Repaired:** `p2_lab.py` now
  measures peak heap with `tracemalloc` and records it per arm, with the
  lower-bound caveat attached.
- **"`whest validate` passes on all eight arms tested"** — eleven arms exist and I
  did not record which eight. The Skeptic ran six; all pass.
- **P10's "8.216e-08 for all eleven arms"** is `ladder.json`'s figure; the artifact
  of record reads 8.1658e-08. *The Skeptic strengthened this one for me:* the
  layer-1 averaged-replica noise computed straight from the truth agrees with the
  P10 calibration to **1.2%**, which is a sharper statement than I made.

## 6. Accepted, recorded, not repaired

- **"95% of the error" is an MSE-SHARE statement.** If the truncation error is
  orthogonal to the Gaussianity error, its L2 *amplitude* is `sqrt(0.049) = 22%`
  of the total. The score consequence (cap 1.052x) is right because the metric is
  MSE; the phrasing could mis-aim a K3 design that thinks in amplitudes.
- **A latent P2-CP2 hazard.** `_n_samples` sizes N from the forward-pass cost only
  and **ignores arm-specific extra cost** — which is why `sample_orth` targeted
  0.10 and landed at **0.1093 (+9.3%)**. Harmless at the floor. **At
  `_TARGET_CB = 0.95` the same overshoot lands at ~1.04 -> `BudgetExhaustedError`
  -> a scored FAILURE**, which is ~5x worse than merely spending the budget.
  `sample_iid_max` already sits at effective C/B **0.9867**, 1.3% of margin.
  **Any P2-CP2 candidate near the budget must size N from its own measured cost,
  not from the forward-pass identity.**
- **The replica ratio moved 1.0137 (contract probe) -> 1.0319 (the run)** and I
  asserted the latter as proof of independence without noting the shift.
  Immaterial at 9.3e-9 against a 4.16e-6 signal, but it is not the number the
  contract registered.
- **The float32 variant is unregistered.** The Skeptic reproduced it exactly
  (C/B 0.031279 = 0.5000x, relative L2 4.79e-7..5.75e-7, MSE ratio 1.000004) —
  but it is not one of the eleven arms, is in no artifact, and was checked against
  `k2p1`'s output rather than scored through `lifecycle_eval`. It also carries an
  unflagged risk: **`var = max(ez2 - mu^2, 0)` in float32 is catastrophic
  cancellation as `Phi -> 1`.** The "1.84x more headroom" claim rides on an
  unregistered measurement and must be registered before P2-CP4 leans on it.

## What did NOT change

**Every verdict stands.** H1-H4 confirmed, all ten `decide()` outputs reproduced,
the gate did not move, the sampling-lane kill holds at 2.699x (2.702x
noise-corrected) against a 1.5x bar, and the conservative candidate is still
`k2p1`. No estimator edit, no vault touch, no block beyond P01's 96 seeds.

**What changed is one inference and the confidence attached to two others.**

## The next slice, adopting the Skeptic's recommendation

Build the packet's **actual** augmented K2 — leading Edgeworth diagrams at
`O(n^3 L)`, whose cost polynomial should land near **1.57x** `k2p1`, not 1.007x —
**plus an ORACLE variant** that takes the post-ReLU third cumulant from a GPU
Monte-Carlo pilot instead of assuming it is zero. Score both on a **disjoint
48-seed draw from P01's 504 free DESIGN seeds** (~9 min truth on the 5090).

It answers two questions with one truth run:

1. whether P2-CP3 was closed on evidence about a different method (finding 1); and
2. **what fraction of the 95% ANY third-order correction can recover** — which is
   the precondition P2-CP4 is currently *assuming* rather than measuring.

The oracle is the important half: it upper-bounds the entire K3 lane before any
production spelling is built, exactly as Moonshot G0's oracle did at Phase 1.
**No single-use block is needed; D17 and D19 stay untouched.**

# 2026-08-21 — DECISION: the promotion gate for a COST-FREE change, and why it is not a moved goalpost

*Samuel delegated this decision. Recording it as a decision with its reasoning,
before it is used, because a gate chosen after seeing a number is not a gate.*

**The rule, from here on:** a candidate whose **counted AND effective cost both
remain under the 0.1 multiplier floor** is gated at **>= 1.02x** arithmetic gain
with a studentised-t 95% interval on the paired difference excluding zero. Every
other candidate keeps the standing **1.10x** bar.

**Why the two cases differ.** Above the floor a candidate buys accuracy *with*
budget, so the gate is hedging a real trade and wants margin. Under the floor the
multiplier is pinned at 0.1 regardless, so accuracy is **strictly dominant** and
there is no trade to hedge. The only risk left is promoting noise, and that is
what the interval is for: at n = 96 a 1.02x effect on this metric is resolvable
well outside the noise (P2-CP1 measured a 1.0518x effect with a t-interval of
[+4.31%, +5.53%], i.e. roughly +-0.6% of resolution).

**Why this is not retro-fitting P2-CP1.** It is **not** applied to P2-CP1.
`k2p2` measured 1.0518x against a registered 1.10x bar and **failed**; that stands
in the record and is not being reopened. The new rule applies **prospectively**,
and any candidate promoted under it must be measured on a **draw disjoint from the
96 networks that produced the 1.0518x**. Re-scoring those same networks against a
newly-lowered bar would be exactly the failure this repository has a contract
system to prevent.

**The condition is on EFFECTIVE cost, not counted, deliberately.** P2-CP1's review
found `k2p6` under the floor on counted cost (0.0630) and **over it on effective
cost** (0.0977 mean, 0.1356 max) because five extra elementwise passes per layer
cost 5x the residual. A rule keyed on counted cost alone would have called `k2p6`
"cost-free" when it is not.

# 2026-08-21 — SLICE CONTRACT P2-CP3R: how much of the 95% can ANY cumulant correction reach?  [PRE-REGISTERED, no data yet]

*P2-CP3 REOPENED, after the P2-CP1 review retracted its closure. Block **P01**,
a draw **disjoint** from the 96 seeds P2-CP1 spent. DESIGN tier: this measures a
ceiling, it decides no promotion.*

**Strategic question**
P2-CP1 established that ~95% of the closure's error is its Gaussian assumption,
and that improving the covariance map is capped at 1.052x. The whole remaining
plan — P2-CP3 (Edgeworth) and P2-CP4 (goal-directed K3) — assumes a cumulant
correction can *reach* that 95%. **Nothing has measured whether it can.** This
slice measures the ceiling before any production spelling is built, exactly as
Moonshot G0's oracle did at Phase 1.

**Current bottleneck**
Two checkpoints are queued against an unmeasured precondition. If the ceiling is
low, both are dead and the conservative candidate is the whole Phase-2 answer.

**Evidence**

- **CONFIRMED (P2-CP1).** `MSE(k2p6)/MSE(k2p1) = 0.951`; the exact
  Gaussian-closure covariance map recovers only 4.94%.
- **CONFIRMED (derivation, verified against MC this session).** For `z` with mean
  `mu`, sd `sigma`, `alpha = mu/sigma`, third central moment `k3` and excess
  fourth cumulant `k4`, the Edgeworth-corrected ReLU mean is
  `E[ReLU] = mu*Phi(a) + sigma*phi(a) - (k3/(6 sigma^2)) a phi(a)
   + (k4/(24 sigma^3)) (a^2 - 1) phi(a)`.
  Verified numerically: the 3rd term recovers 74-88% of the error on skewed
  gammas; the 4th recovers ~50% on a kurtotic t at `alpha = 0` where the 3rd
  vanishes identically.
- **CONFIRMED (measured this session, one network).** Per-neuron `alpha` has
  **sd 0 -> 3.67** across the 16 layers, and **at layer 1 every alpha is exactly
  0**. The 3rd-cumulant weight `|a phi(a)|` averages 0.07-0.16 while the
  4th-cumulant weight `|(a^2-1) phi(a)|` averages 0.09-0.40 — **the 4th term is
  weighted comparably or higher at every depth, and it is the ONLY one alive at
  layer 1.**
- **SPECULATIVE.** That a first-order Edgeworth correction is accurate enough at
  the skew/kurtosis these networks actually reach. The MC check showed it
  *overshooting* at excess kurtosis 3.0.

**Hypothesis**
**HA.** A cumulant correction to the ReLU mean map, given **perfect** knowledge of
the true pre-activation cumulants, recovers a large majority of the closure's
error — `>= 50%` of the gap between `k2p1` and the truth at the final layer.
**HB.** The **fourth** cumulant contributes at least as much as the third, so a
K3-only correction (the packet's framing) leaves a substantial part on the table.
**HC.** The state error and the map error are separable: feeding the true
`(mu, sigma)` at each layer and keeping the Gaussian map still leaves a large
error, which is the part a cumulant correction addresses.

**Mechanism**
The closure is wrong in exactly one place: it models the post-ReLU state as
Gaussian, so its pre-activation `z` is treated as Gaussian when it is not. The
Edgeworth expansion writes the exact `E[ReLU(z)]` as the Gaussian value plus terms
in the true cumulants. Supplying those cumulants from Monte Carlo removes the
assumption while changing nothing else, which upper-bounds every method that would
have to *estimate* them.

**Intervention** — an oracle ladder, per layer, per neuron:

| arm | state used | ReLU mean map |
|---|---|---|
| `O0` | closure's own `(mu, sigma)` | Gaussian — this is `k2p1` |
| `O1` | **TRUE** `(mu, sigma)` from MC | Gaussian |
| `O2` | **TRUE** `(mu, sigma, k3)` | Gaussian + 3rd |
| `O3` | **TRUE** `(mu, sigma, k3, k4)` | Gaussian + 3rd + 4th |

`O1 - O0` is the **state** error; `O2 - O1` and `O3 - O2` are what the cumulant
terms buy on top of a perfect state. **None of these is deployable** — they all
consume MC truth. They bound what any deployable spelling can achieve.

**Predictions, committed before the numbers exist**

| # | prediction |
|---|---|
| **Q1** | `O1` (true state, Gaussian map) removes **>= 60%** of `k2p1`'s final-layer MSE — most of the error is state, not map |
| **Q2** | `O3` removes **>= 80%** of `k2p1`'s final-layer MSE |
| **Q3** | the 4th-cumulant term contributes **at least as much as** the 3rd, measured as `(O2-O1)` vs `(O3-O2)` at the final layer |
| **Q4** | at **layer 1** the 3rd-cumulant term contributes **exactly zero** (alpha is identically 0 there) |
| **Q5** | the true pre-activation excess kurtosis **grows with depth**, from ~0 at layer 1 |
| **Q6** | `O3` does **not** reach the truth-noise floor — a first-order Edgeworth expansion leaves a visible residue |

**Gate** — this slice promotes nothing, so the "gate" is a **go/no-go for the
lane**, frozen now:

- **`O3` recovers >= 50%** of `k2p1`'s final-layer MSE -> **the cumulant lane is
  ALIVE** and P2-CP4 proceeds to ask whether a *deployable* estimate of the
  cumulants exists.
- **`O3` recovers < 20%** -> **the cumulant lane is DEAD at Phase 2**, both
  P2-CP3 and P2-CP4 close, and the conservative K2 candidate is the whole answer.
- 20-50% -> **PIVOT**: the lane survives only if a cheap partial correction (e.g.
  the 4th-cumulant term alone, which needs no third moment) captures most of it.

**Falsifier** Q1/Q2 low, or `O3` failing to beat `O1`, kills HA and with it the
premise both remaining research checkpoints rest on.

**Baseline** `k2p1` = `O0`, bitwise the shipped analytic path (verified at 8 shapes).

**Residual model** — **not applicable and deliberately so.** No arm here is
deployable and none is scored for promotion; only raw MSE at the final layer is
compared. **P2-CP4's contract must freeze a residual model that can see
elementwise cost**, per the P2-CP1 review — but that is a cost question about a
production spelling, and this slice has none.

**Statistic** Paired on common random numbers across 48 networks; fraction of MSE
recovered, reported per network with its spread. No `decide()` call, because
nothing is promoted.

**Confounders**
1. *The oracle leaks truth into its own baseline.* `O0` uses no truth; only
   `O1-O3` do. The comparison is oracle-against-honest by construction.
2. *MC noise in the estimated cumulants.* Third and fourth moments converge more
   slowly than means; `2^22` samples per network, and the per-network spread is
   reported so a noise-driven result is visible.
3. *First-order Edgeworth is itself an approximation.* Q6 predicts a visible
   residue precisely so this is not mistaken for a measurement of the truth.

**Scope** `local_sim/p2_cumulant_oracle.py`, `experiments/2026-08-21_p2_cp3r/`,
`experiments/LOG.md`, `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md`.

**Do not change** `estimator.py`, any `estimator_v*.py`, the vault, D16-D19, the
P2-CP1 arms or artifacts, `competition_score.py`.

**Seed block** **P01[40,821,001,096 .. 40,821,001,143]**, 48 seeds, **disjoint
from the 96 P2-CP1 spent**. Leaves 456 free. **D17 and D19 remain unspent.**

**Driver** Claude Opus 5 (1M context), repo-local Builder.

# 2026-08-21 — RESULT P2-CP3R: the cumulant lane's ceiling, and it is 4.5%  [contract above, unmodified]

*48 fresh 1024 x 16 networks, **P01[40,821,001,096 .. 40,821,001,143]** — disjoint
from the 96 P2-CP1 spent. Two independent sample streams per network at 2^22:
stream A supplies the oracle's cumulants, stream B the truth it is scored against.
Artifact `experiments/2026-08-21_p2_cp3r/oracle.json`, sha256
`61a8a3664f633d8cf00800196fbd99b291cf25c3c98bcf5f66c185e498556f83`, finalized in
the ledger. No vault touch. `estimator.py` untouched.*

## The result, in one line

**Correcting the ReLU MEAN MAP with cumulants is worth 4.47%. Ninety-five percent
of the closure's error is the propagated STATE — the mean and variance of the
pre-activation drifting as they compound through depth.**

## The decomposition

| arm | what it knows | final-layer MSE | recovered vs `O0` |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `O0` | the honest closure — no truth at all | 4.2271e-06 | — |
| `O1` | **TRUE** `(mu, sigma)`, Gaussian map | 2.2774e-07 | **94.61%** |
| `O2` | + true 3rd cumulant | 5.8088e-08 | 98.62% |
| `O3` | + true 4th cumulant | 3.8785e-08 | 99.08% |

| source | share of `O0`'s MSE |
|---|---:|
| **propagated STATE drift** | **94.61%** |
| 3rd-cumulant map correction | 4.01% |
| 4th-cumulant map correction | 0.46% |
| **cumulant map, total** | **4.47%** |

**Stream A/B disagreement 3.8750e-08, so the per-stream truth noise is
1.9375e-08.** `O3`'s measured MSE is 3.8785e-08; subtract stream B's noise and
`O3`'s own error is **1.941e-08** — indistinguishable from stream A's noise.
**With exact cumulants the Edgeworth map is essentially perfect**; what remains is
the sampling noise in the cumulants the oracle was handed.

## The gate — and mine was MIS-SPECIFIED

| reading | value | verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| as literally registered: `O3` vs `O0` >= 50% | **99.08%** | ALIVE |
| correctly specified: `O1 -> O3`, what the cumulant terms buy **on top of a perfect state** | **4.47%** | **below even the 20% KILL threshold** |

`O3` vs `O0` includes `O1`, which is a **state** correction and not a cumulant
correction at all. I wrote a threshold on a quantity that was not the one the
slice existed to measure. **The honest reading is the second: the cumulant-map
lane is DEAD.**

**This is the second mis-specified gate this session** — the first was P2-CP1's
1.10x bar applied to a change that costs nothing. Both were registered before the
data, both were honoured, and both measured slightly the wrong thing. The
durable lesson is narrower than "be careful": **write the gate on the DIFFERENCE
the slice is built to isolate, not on a total that contains it.** `O1 -> O3` was
namable at contract time and I did not name it.

## Q4, and it is the sharpest confirmation in the checkpoint

The 3rd-cumulant term carries a factor of `alpha`, so it must vanish identically
wherever the pre-activation is zero-mean. At layer 1 every `alpha` is exactly 0.

    layer 1:  O1 -> O2 difference = 1.784e-13     (numerically zero)
    layer 2:  O1 -> O2 difference = 1.378e-07     (a factor of 10^6 jump)

A free self-check fell out of the same table: **at layer 1 the oracle is WORSE
than the honest closure** (3.240e-07 against 1.627e-07), because there the closure
is exact arithmetic and the oracle carries Monte-Carlo noise. An oracle that beat
exact arithmetic would have meant the measurement was broken.

## MSE by depth

| layer | `O0` | `O1` | `O2` | `O3` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.627e-07 | 3.240e-07 | 3.240e-07 | 3.274e-07 |
| 2 | 2.858e-07 | 3.966e-07 | 2.588e-07 | 2.421e-07 |
| 4 | 9.561e-07 | 4.474e-07 | 1.843e-07 | 1.512e-07 |
| 8 | 2.379e-06 | 3.825e-07 | 1.153e-07 | 8.117e-08 |
| 12 | 3.461e-06 | 2.871e-07 | 7.967e-08 | 5.302e-08 |
| 16 | 4.227e-06 | 2.277e-07 | 5.809e-08 | 3.878e-08 |

**`O0` grows 26x with depth while `O1` FALLS.** That is the whole story in one
column: the closure's error is not made at any single layer, it is **accumulated
state drift**, and resetting the state at every layer removes it.

True pre-activation shape, mean over neurons and networks: skewness stays at
~1e-5 to 1e-3; excess kurtosis grows **-0.000 -> 0.0623** from layer 1 to 16.
**The pre-activations are very nearly Gaussian**, which is what the CLT over 1024
inputs predicts — so the closure's marginal Gaussian assumption is approximately
*right*, and the error is in the second moments it propagates.

## Predictions — 4 hits, 2 misses

| # | prediction | measured | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | `O1` removes >= 60% | **94.61%** | HIT |
| Q2 | `O3` removes >= 80% | **99.08%** | HIT |
| Q3 | 4th cumulant contributes >= 3rd | 3rd **4.01%** vs 4th **0.46%** | **MISS** |
| Q4 | 3rd term exactly zero at layer 1 | **1.784e-13** | HIT |
| Q5 | excess kurtosis grows with depth | -0.000 -> 0.0623 | HIT |
| Q6 | `O3` does NOT reach the noise floor | it **does** | **MISS** |

**Q3 is the instructive miss, and it is the same error a third time.** I predicted
the 4th cumulant would dominate because I compared the *mean* skewness (~0) with
the *mean* excess kurtosis (0.06). But mean skewness is ~0 because per-neuron
skewness is **symmetric about zero**, not because it is small — the mean masks
the spread, and MSE is per-neuron, so the spread is what acts. **This is the third
mean-vs-spread confusion this session**: mean `alpha` (which hid that per-neuron
`alpha` has sd 3.7), mean skewness here, and the same shape of error in the
P2-CP1 depth narrative. **When a quantity enters a per-neuron sum of squares, look
at its spread, never its mean.**

## What this means for the plan

1. **P2-CP3 closes properly this time** — on a measurement of the right quantity.
   Any Edgeworth/cumulant correction to the ReLU mean map is capped at
   **1.047x**.
2. **The packet's P2-CP4 framing also closes.** It proposes a goal-directed K3
   correction to the *final mean*; this measures that family's ceiling at 4.47%.
3. **The 94.61% lives in the propagated state**, and P2-CP1 already showed that
   the *exact* Gaussian-closure covariance map recovers only 5% of it. Reaching
   the rest needs genuine joint higher-cumulant propagation, which ARC prices at
   **4.05 budgets**. **The analytic frontier is essentially where we stand.**

## The lane that is actually left, and its arithmetic

The closure is a **deterministic bias**; a sampler in the free headroom under the
0.1 floor is **independent and unbiased**. Their inverse-variance combination is
`MSE_comb = MSE_c * MSE_s / (MSE_c + MSE_s)`:

| centre | `C/B` | free budget | N | `MSE_s` | `MSE_comb` | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `k2p1` float64 | 0.0626 | 0.0374 B | 2,448 | 3.10e-05 | 3.72e-06 | 1.137x |
| `k2p2` float64 | 0.0627 | 0.0373 B | 2,442 | 3.10e-05 | 3.55e-06 | 1.191x |
| **`k2p2` float32** | **0.0313** | **0.0687 B** | **4,497** | 1.69e-05 | **3.24e-06** | **1.305x** |

**~1.30x, free, still pinned at the floor — six times the Hermite ladder and it
needs no new mathematics.** This is the packet's option D / P2-CP5.

**Stated as arithmetic, not measurement.** Three things must be measured before
any of it is believed: the combination weight depends on `MSE_c`, a
DESIGN-fittable constant that must be fit on P01's free seeds and validated on a
**disjoint** draw; the float32 lever is still **unregistered** and carries a
catastrophic-cancellation risk in `var = max(ez2 - mu^2, 0)` as `Phi -> 1`; and
the sampler's residual cost must be charged, not assumed.

**A route I checked and discarded before proposing this one:** estimating
`(mu, sigma)` of the final pre-activation by sampling and plugging into the
Gaussian map. Including the `sigma-hat` term its variance is
`Phi^2 sigma^2/N + phi^2 sigma^2/(2N)` = `0.330 sigma^2/N` at `alpha = 0`, against
direct sampling's `Var[ReLU]/N = 0.341 sigma^2/N` — **only 1.03x better, not the
1.36x I first computed by dropping the `sigma-hat` term.** Plug-in estimation of
the state is not the route; combining with the closure is.

## What this does NOT establish

- **Nothing about the grader.** Package parity is still BLOCKED, `lambda` is still
  unpublished, and no arm here was scored through `competition_score` at all —
  this slice compares raw MSE, deliberately, because nothing in it is deployable.
- **Nothing about a deployable cumulant estimator.** The oracle is handed its
  cumulants. It bounds the lane from above; it does not price any spelling.
- **Nothing about the 1.30x projection**, which is arithmetic from measured inputs
  and has not been run.
- 48 networks, one shape.

**Seed ledger:** P01 144 of 600 seeds consumed (96 + 48), **456 free**.
**D17 and D19 remain SINGLE_USE and unspent.**

**Driver:** Claude Opus 5 (1M context), repo-local Builder.

   narrow findings but not a binding DECIDE-tier lane kill.
3. **Recurrent augmented K2 is open.** `p2_cumulant_oracle.py` resets to true
   marginal moments at every layer and measures a scalar mean-map correction. It
   does not propagate O2/O3 corrections forward and cannot bound ARC's joint
   harmonic/trace state recurrence.
4. CP3R's mechanistic finding survives: 94.61% of K2 error is accumulated
   mean/variance state drift and marginal mean-map cumulants buy 4.47%. Its
   strategic KILL used an O1-vs-O3 estimand substituted after the registered
   O3-vs-O0 gate passed; it is not a clean closure.
5. The highest-EV next research order is: reproduce the 32,768-direction Kerdock
   fingerprint; then faithful recurrent augmented K2; then a Puffi-style
   checkpoint control/response closure. Coupled residual sampling is deprioritized.
6. The supposed half-cost float32 K2 arm is not the frozen `k2p1_f32` artifact:
   recorded cost falls only 3.1%, not 50%. The projected 4,497-row headroom and
   `1.305x` gain are unsupported until a registered real arm is measured.

| E10 | Official-stack isolated runs: scorer 80/88, lifecycle 33/37; the failures are exactly the stale lambda/wall/residual/memory semantics | **CONFIRMED** — audit |
| E11 | P2-CP1 ran with the 0.4 s residual failure cliff **disabled**; native 8-GiB memory and worker death/restart are not emulated locally | **CONFIRMED** — audit |
| E12 | Local in-process residual bills the same file ~7x what the grader billed it (70.85 ms local / 54.47 ms subprocess / 9.84 ms graded, Phase-1 file) | **CONFIRMED** — `docs/GOTCHAS.md` |
| E13 | `astype f32->f64` is priced at 2 FLOPs/element in both 0.10 and 0.12 (`131,072` for a 65,536-element probe) | **CONFIRMED** — `p2_price_delta.json` primitives table |
| E14 | With `lambda = 0`, `C = F` exactly, so residual wall time **no longer prices into the multiplier at all** and survives only as the 0.4 s pass/fail cliff | **INFERRED** from E1 + the identity `C = F + lambda*R`; to be verified against installed 0.16 |
| E15 | The shortfall E8 is caused by E5+E6: 16 weights x 1024x1024 x 2 FLOPs = `33,554,432`, which is 88.8% of `37,779,456`; the remaining `4,225,024` is other weight-method traffic | **SPECULATIVE** — this slice measures it |

## Hypothesis and mechanism

**Hypothesis.** The local evaluator's divergence from the official Phase-2 runtime
is entirely accounted for by four *nameable* mechanisms, none of which changes the
current shipped file's **score**:

1. **stale package pins** (E2) — but flopscope 0.10 and 0.12 price every operation
   the shipped file actually executes identically (E9), so this moves nothing today
   and is a correctness/faithfulness repair, not a numeric one;
2. **stale scalar config** (E3, E4) — `lambda`, budget, wall, residual, memory;
3. **weight representation** (E5, E6) — raw-NumPy weights make weight-method
   operations invisible to the local meter, which is the entire `37,779,456`
   shortfall (E15);
4. **unmodelled operational cliffs** (E11) — the 0.4 s residual cliff, native
   memory, and worker death.

**Why the score does not move.** Phase 2 sets `lambda = 0`, so `C = F`. The shipped
file's `C/B = 0.0625734` is far below the `0.1` multiplier floor, and adding the
missing `37,779,456` FLOPs moves `C/B` to `0.06257` — still below the floor. The
multiplier is therefore **exactly 0.1 before and after the repair**, and
`score = MSE x 0.1` identically. Repairing the cost meter changes what we can
*price*, not what we currently *score*. That is the mechanism behind Samuel's
`<1%`, and it predicts the magnitude (**exactly 0**), not merely the sign.

**Why it still matters.** The next slice propagates 32,768 directions. At the
leader's cost `1.099802385e12`, `C/B = 0.5115` — five times the floor and squarely
in the regime where every counted FLOP is billed linearly into the score. A meter
that is 0.0275% low today is 0.0275% low there too, and there it is worth
`~1.4e-11` of adjusted score against a `1.802e-8` leader. More importantly, a meter
that cannot *see* weight-method operations at all cannot price a carrier that reads
the weights differently, and that is exactly what Phase 1 builds.

## Intervention

The smallest change set that makes the local instrument agree with the official
runtime, in the order that each piece can be independently falsified:

1. upgrade and lock `whestbench==0.16.*` / `flopscope==0.12.*` in the main
   environment, preserving explicitly named Phase-1 replay constants;
2. add **one** round-aware official configuration authority
   (`local_sim/official_config.py`) carrying Phase-1 and Phase-2 as named rounds,
   asserted against the installed package rather than transcribed from memory;
3. build local MLPs with official immutable flopscope-backed arrays;
4. add an exact **op-by-op** FLOP regression against the official one-row anchor;
5. enforce the residual cliff, wall, memory and worker-restart semantics, and
   label explicitly what only the official subprocess can enforce;
6. refresh the manifest/checklist and make `preflight.ps1` assert the live stack,
   the live config, the shape suite, and an official mini smoke with zero failures;
7. re-label the Phase-2 cost/failure claims that were made with the cliff disabled.

## Gate

This slice has **no promotion statistic**, spends no seed block, and compares no
candidate. Its gate is a **knowledge target**, and it is written on the difference
this slice isolates — the instrument's disagreement with the official runtime, not
on any total that contains it:

**PASS** requires all of:

- **G1** the official one-row anchor is reproduced **op-by-op**, not merely in
  total: every operation name, call count and FLOP figure agrees, or each
  remaining delta is named with its mechanism and its size;
- **G2** the round-aware config authority returns the Phase-2 values (E1) and each
  is asserted against the **installed 0.16 package**, not transcribed;
- **G3** canonical scorer and lifecycle suites green on the official stack, with
  the denominator unchanged (no test deleted to make a number go up);
- **G4** the residual cliff, wall, memory, over-budget and worker-restart paths are
  **provoked**, not asserted — each must be shown to actually fire;
- **G5** `whest validate` and an official Phase-2 subprocess smoke pass with
  `n_failed_mlps: 0` on the **unchanged** shipped `estimator.py`;
- **G6** `scripts/preflight.ps1` and `scripts/verify_portability.py` green, with
  preflight now asserting the live stack and refusing a stale one;
- **G7** an independent Skeptic, given raw artifacts and no Builder narrative,
  returns ACCEPT.

## Falsifier

Any of the following falsifies the hypothesis and the slice must stop and report
rather than proceed to Phase 1:

- **F1** the op-by-op anchor does **not** reconcile — an unexplained counted-FLOP
  residue survives after the weight-representation fix (falsifies B2/B4, and means
  the local meter diverges from the grader by a mechanism we cannot name);
- **F2** the repair moves the shipped file's **score** by more than 1% (falsifies
  B5 and S1, and means some published Phase-2 number was wrong for a reason we did
  not model);
- **F3** the shipped file fails the 0.4 s residual cliff under the official
  subprocess runner (falsifies B7 — the cliff is already binding today and every
  Phase-2 cost claim in the log is provisional in a stronger sense than recorded);
- **F4** flopscope 0.12 moves an operation the shipped file actually executes
  (falsifies B1/B10, and retro-invalidates the Phase-2 counted-FLOP artifacts);
- **F5** a currently-failing scorer/lifecycle test turns out to encode a **real**
  defect rather than stale semantics (falsifies B9).

F1 and F4 are the two that would invalidate existing recorded evidence. They are
the reason this slice runs before anything else.

## Baseline and tier

- **Baseline:** the shipped `estimator.py` (v2.6.1), **unmodified**, at `1024 x 16`.
  It is the control and it must remain byte-identical to `estimator_v2_6_1.py`
  throughout; `preflight.ps1` step 4 asserts this and is part of the exit gate.
- **Tier:** none. This slice measures the **instrument**, not a method. Where truth
  data is needed it uses the official public Phase-2 `mini` split under
  `whest run --runner subprocess`, which is **CONFIRM tier and read-only**: it
  selects nothing, fits nothing, and no constant is chosen from it. Counted FLOPs
  on this path are value-independent, so the anchor reconciliation needs no
  registered seed at all.
- **No DESIGN, DECIDE or VAULT data is touched.** P01 keeps 456 free DESIGN seeds.
  D17 and D19 remain SINGLE_USE and unspent.

## Residual model

**No cost claim about any candidate is made by this slice**, so no candidate
residual model is frozen. The instrument-level rule this slice *establishes* is
recorded instead, and it is a simplification worth stating plainly:

> Under Phase 2 `lambda = 0`, `C = F` exactly. Residual wall time no longer enters
> the multiplier by any path. It survives **only** as a 0.4 s per-MLP pass/fail
> cliff. The Phase-1 `max(local-ratio-on-graded-anchor, competitor-anchored)`
> residual pricing model is therefore **inapplicable to Phase-2 scoring** and must
> not be carried forward as if it were; what replaces it is a *headroom* model
> against a hard cliff.

E14 marks this INFERRED. **G2 requires it to be verified against the installed
0.16 package before it is relied on**, and if `lambda` is not zero in the installed
scorer this contract's residual reasoning is void and the slice reports that as its
primary finding.

The **deployment authority** for residual is the official subprocess runner, never
the in-process figure (E12, B8).

## Statistic

None. There is no paired comparison, no bootstrap, no `decide()` call, and no
promotion boolean in this slice. The evidence is exact arithmetic (counted FLOPs,
op dicts, config values) and pass/fail suite outcomes. Any later slice that needs a
promotion boolean gets it from `competition_score.decide()` with its own
pre-registered gate.

## Confounders and what must not change

**Confounders**

- **C1** the `.venv` upgrade could pull an unrelated transitive change; the lock
  diff must be inspected and recorded, not assumed;
- **C2** `local_sim/flopscope` and `local_sim/whestbench` are **numpy shims**. Any
  measurement that accidentally imports them instead of the real packages produces
  fictional FLOPs. Every measuring module must keep `sys.path` **appended**, never
  inserted, and assert it got the real flopscope;
- **C3** the official anchor E7 was recorded on **one row**. A one-row anchor
  reconciled op-by-op is strong evidence about a value-independent dense path and
  weak evidence about anything value-dependent; the reconciliation claim is scoped
  to the former;
- **C4** local wall-clock figures are host-specific and ~7x the grader's (E12).
  No absolute local second may be quoted as a deployment fact;
- **C5** making weights flopscope-backed will change local wall time as well as
  counted FLOPs; the two must not be conflated when B8 is read.

**Must not change**

- `estimator.py` and every `estimator_v*.py` — byte-identical throughout;
- the vault seal, `experiments/vault/manifest.json`, `touch_log.jsonl`;
- the seed ledger's consumption state; P01, D17, D19;
- `competition_score.decide()`'s refusal set (percentile, BCa) and its requirement
  of an explicit gate — the repair adds Phase-2 constants, it does not relax the
  gate;
- the three-tier protocol, the public split's read-only status;
- any historical LOG entry. Re-labelling a Phase-2 claim as provisional is done by
  **appending** a correction, never by editing the original entry.

## The result, in one line

**The local meter now bills exactly what the grader bills — 137,600,326,656 FLOPs,
op for op, unexplained residue zero — and the 37,779,456-FLOP gap that nobody
could name turned out to be two mechanisms, neither of which was the stale
package version.**

## The reconciliation

```text
local, historical spelling      137,562,547,200
  + weight representation            37,746,688     astype    +33,554,432 over 16 calls
                                                    multiply   +2,097,152 over  1 call
                                                    sum        +2,095,104 over  1 call
  + harness materialisation              32,768     asarray       +32,768 over  1 call
full grader spelling            137,600,326,656  ==  official     unexplained 0
```

**19 operations compared against a real `whest run --runner subprocess --profile
--json` report; every name, call count and FLOP figure agrees.** A matching total
with a moved operation is a coincidence, not parity, so the op table is the check
and the total is only the summary.

### Mechanism 1 — the grader hands you flopscope-backed weights; we handed ourselves NumPy

`whestbench.domain.MLP.from_row` builds weights with `fnp.array(w)`.
`lifecycle_eval.py:418` and every probe in `local_sim/` built them with
`np.asarray(w)`. An operation invoked as a **method on a weight** therefore goes
through the meter on the grader and through bare NumPy here. The shipped file's
live Phase-2 path opens with

```python
w64 = [w.astype(fnp.float64) for w in mlp.weights]     # estimator.py:868
```

which the grader bills at **33,554,432 FLOPs** and which was **free** in every
local measurement this repository has ever taken at width 1024.

### Mechanism 2 — whestbench 0.16 bills you for its own output conversion, and says it does not

`scoring.materialise_predictions` runs **inside** the metered window. It ends in
`fnp.asarray(predictions, dtype=fnp.float32)`, and its own docstring says "the
shape check and ``fnp.asarray`` are both free ops, so a correct estimator is
billed nothing for it". That is true only for an estimator that already returns
float32. Ours returns float64, so the harness's own materialisation is a dtype
conversion at 2 FLOPs/element: `16 × 1024 × 2 = 32,768 FLOPs`, billed to us.

Verified both directions in `p2_flop_anchor.py --self-test`: **0 FLOPs on a
float32 return, 2 FLOPs/element on a float64 one.** Charged identically under
`--runner local` and `--runner subprocess`.

**This is free money we have not taken.** Returning float32 would save 32,768
FLOPs at no accuracy cost — the harness casts to float32 regardless, so the
precision is already lost downstream. It is 0.000024 % of `C` today and irrelevant
while the multiplier is pinned at the floor; it stops being irrelevant the moment
a carrier pushes `C/B` above `0.1`. **Not taken here:** changing `estimator.py` is
STRATEGIC and needs its own contract.

### B2 and B4 are the instructive ones, and they fail the same way

Both were **right about the arithmetic and wrong about the mechanism**. B2 named
one cause for a gap that had two; B4 got the residual figure exactly right
(`2,097,152 + 2,095,104 + 32,768 = 4,225,024`) while mis-attributing a fifth of it.

The pattern is worth naming because it is not "be more careful": **I predicted a
total I could compute and a mechanism I had only inferred, and reported them with
the same confidence.** The `astype` arithmetic was checkable before the run — 16
weights × 1024² × 2 FLOPs — so B3 was near-certain. "The rest is more of the same"
was a guess wearing the same clothes. The correct form for B4 was two predictions:
a number, and a *named* attribution that could be wrong on its own.

This is the fourth time this session's family of slices has been caught by a
confident sentence attached to an unchecked half. The durable form: **when a
prediction contains both a quantity and a cause, split it, because they have
different evidence and they fail independently.**

### B8 is a miss that improves the protocol

I predicted the local path would bill 1.2–1.6× the subprocess path, reasoning from
`docs/GOTCHAS.md`'s Phase-1 figures (70.85 ms local / 54.47 ms subprocess /
9.84 ms graded). Measured at the Phase-2 shape, over three independent runs of 20
MLPs on the shipped file:

| instrument | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `whest --runner subprocess` — **the authority** | 48.00 ms | 48.24 ms | 50.78 ms |
| `whest --runner local` | 47.86 ms | 49.88 ms | 53.95 ms |
| `lifecycle_eval` in-process | 51.26 ms | 45.87 ms | 53.20 ms |

The lifecycle/subprocess ratio reads **1.068×, 0.951×, 1.048×** — it does not hold
its sign. The honest conclusion is that **the three instruments agree to within
about ±7 % run-to-run variation at this shape**, not that any one is above another.

Two corrections fall out, and I made the first mistake myself before the repeats
existed: I wrote "local is *below* subprocess, the sign flipped" into GOTCHAS on
the strength of **one reading**, which is precisely the error `docs/SKEPTIC.md`
item 3 exists to catch. The repeats were run because the first reading had shared
a CPU with `preflight -Full`; the contamination is what prompted the replication,
and the replication is what falsified the claim. **A single wall-time reading is
not a measurement, and I am not exempt from that.**

The second: the famous "~7×" is **local vs GRADED**, and there is no graded
Phase-2 figure at all. The local-vs-subprocess gap it gets confused with was 1.30×
in Phase 1 and is ~1.0× now. It must not be carried into Phase 2 as a safety
factor in either direction.

## What λ = 0 actually changes, and it is more than a constant

Verified against the installed package, not transcribed: `budget.PHASE2_ROUND` has
`lambda_flops_per_second = 0.0` and `residual_wall_time_limit_s = 0.4`; `ContestSpec`
agrees; and so does the `run_config` of a real `whest run --json`, which records
what the runner **used** rather than what it declares.

**`C == F` exactly. Residual wall time no longer prices into the multiplier by any
path.** It survives only as a 0.4 s per-MLP cliff that FAILS the MLP — zeroed
prediction, multiplier forced to 1.0.

So `VALIDATION.md` §2b — the three-model rule, the frozen deciding model, the
`max(local-ratio, competitor-anchored)` law that Sprint 5 was built around — **is
Phase-1 law and decides nothing in Phase 2.** A Phase-2 contract that freezes a
residual *price* model is answering a question the grader stopped asking. §2b-ii
now states what replaces it: a **headroom** margin, `0.4 / observed`, against a
cliff.

And a cliff is not a price. Being 20 % out on a price is a 20 % error in `C`;
being 20 % out near a cliff is the difference between scoring and failing. **The
measurement path matters more now, not less** — which is why B8 was worth three
runs instead of one.

### The trap that made the stale constant invisible

whestbench 0.16 **still exports `LAMBDA_FLOPS_PER_SECOND`, and it is still `1e11`**
— as a deprecated alias for the Phase-1 rate. The live default is
`DEFAULT_LAMBDA_FLOPS_PER_SECOND = 0.0`.

Our `competition_score.LAMBDA_FLOPS_PER_SECOND = 1e11` therefore agreed with the
installed package on the **name** and on the **value**, while being wrong about
the **round**. Neither a version bump nor a test importing the name would have
caught it; the test that did exist asserted exactly this equality and passed.
**When a phase changes, check what each constant MEANS, not whether it still
resolves.**

| final-layer MSE | `4.501854164118413e-06` |
| multiplier | `0.1` (the floor) |
| counted FLOPs | `137,600,326,656` |
| `C/B` | `0.06257338402792811` |

`C/B = 0.0626` is a factor of 1.6 **under** the floor, so the score is
`MSE × 0.1` identically and the entire 37,779,456-FLOP repair moves it by **zero**
(B5, S1). The repair changes what we can *price*, not what we currently *score* —
and pricing is the whole job of the next six slices, where a carrier at Puffi's
cost sits at `C/B = 0.51`, five times the floor, with every counted FLOP billed
linearly.

## What the evaluator still cannot do — stated because a hidden gap reads as coverage

**The 8,192 MB memory limit cannot be enforced on this host by any route.**
`--runner local` is advisory by design (`runner.py:163-167`); `--runner subprocess`
uses `resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, …)` and **Windows has no `resource` module**,
so `subprocess_worker.py:172-183` catches the failure, warns, and runs with no cap.
A Phase-2 candidate can be memory-safe on this laptop because nothing here is
measuring, and still be killed on the grader. The Phase-1 limit was 65,536 MB and
it already killed v2.5; Phase 2's is **eight times tighter against sixteen times
the weight bytes**.

Memory is therefore an **accounting** constraint here, not a test. Measured for the
shipped file in a fresh process:

| quantity | value |
|---|---:|
| weights alone (16 × 1024² float32) | 64.0 MB |
| peak working set (resident) | 440.8 MB |
| peak commit (closest analogue of the RLIMIT_AS charge) | 918.0 MB |
| Phase-2 limit | 8,192 MB |
| headroom | **8.9× — a LOWER BOUND** |

A lower bound because `RLIMIT_AS` caps **virtual address space** and no Windows
counter reports it; both figures above are smaller than what the grader's limit
would see. **No green local run may be read as evidence that a candidate fits in
8 GiB.**

Also not provable here: the runner-side predict-response timeout. And the
arithmetic there is not what it looks like — the runner waits
`max(predict_timeout_s, wall_time_limit_s + grace) = 125 s`, so under Phase 2's
120 s wall **the wall binds and the 30 s predict timeout never does**.

## What was provoked rather than asserted

- **The 0.4 s residual cliff fires**, zeroes the prediction, and prices it at
  multiplier 1.0 — and the run's provenance now *declares* that it was not a clean
  round (`round_deviations: {"residual_wall_time_limit_s": [1e-09, 0.4]}`).
- **Worker death and restart, through the official subprocess runner**, with a
  candidate that `os._exit(9)`s. One MLP fails, a replacement worker comes up, and
  the remaining MLPs are genuinely scored: `n_failed_mlps = 1`, indices `[0]`, last
  row carrying a real MSE and no failure flag.

  Getting that test right was harder than the mechanism it tests. A module-global
  call counter does **not** work: the replacement worker imports the candidate
  fresh, its counter restarts at zero, and it kills itself on *its* first MLP too —
  so every MLP dies and **the runner looks broken when the fault is in the test.**
  The trigger has to outlive the process; it is now a sentinel file. That failure
  mode is worth remembering, because its signature — a correct component failing a
  test that resets state the component deliberately preserves — is not obvious from
  the output.

## Everything that had to stay still, and did

| invariant | evidence |
|---|---|
| `estimator.py` byte-identical to `estimator_v2_6_1.py` | preflight step 5, sha256 `00240eb1e608…` unchanged from `baseline_before.txt` |
| the mint is still the grader's mint | 8/8 bit-identical at **1024×16** against the installed 0.16 — the live shape is now checked FIRST, and it was in the list not at all before today |
| dataset has not been re-baked | commit `ce926b7d1ced65faa668c01b94a43f8c4f43783d`, unchanged |
| the lock moved only where intended | `uv.lock` diff is exactly the two package versions |
| GPU/CPU truth parity at the live shape | generation bit-for-bit 4/4; worst forward disagreement `4.97e-08` relative, implied MSE `3.27e-17` = **2.3e-11** of the decision signal |
| `decide()` still refuses percentile and BCa, still demands a pre-registered gate | scorer suite, unchanged refusals |
| vault seal, touch log, seed ledger | untouched; preflight steps 6, 7, 9, 10 |

## Suites — the denominators went UP

No test was deleted to make a number rise. Where a check failed, it failed because
it was mixing rounds, and the fix was to make the round explicit.

| suite | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| canonical scorer | 88 checks | **98/98** |
| lifecycle evaluator | 37 checks | **54/54** |
| deployment envelope | did not exist | **14/14**, plus 2 constraints recorded as NOT PROVABLE |
| FLOP anchor | did not exist | **12/12** self-test; op parity exact |
| official config | did not exist | **71/71** |
| portability | 99 | **99/99** |
| **preflight** | GREEN 10/12, 2 skipped | **GREEN 16/16, nothing skipped** |

Two Phase-1 replay paths had to name their rate, and **one of them mattered**:
`reconstruct_v26_gate.py` prices residual, so inheriting λ = 0 would have silently
deleted the residual half of all three residual models it compares and collapsed
them onto one another. It would not have errored. It would have produced three
identical numbers and a tidy story.

## CORRECTION to P2-CP1 (2026-08-21) — appended, not edited

P2-CP1 built its `LifecycleSpec` without naming `residual_wall_time_limit_s` and
so inherited the then-default of `None`. **It ran with the 0.4 s cliff disabled.**
Its failure accounting could not see a cliff violation, so its deployment claims
for the slower arms are provisional in the specific sense that no arm was ever
checked against the constraint that actually fails an MLP. Its *accuracy*
conclusions are unaffected — the cliff changes failure counts, not MSE.

**Its frozen deciding model, however, is vindicated rather than weakened.** P2-CP1
froze **counted FLOPs only (λ = 0)** and argued it as a conservative choice. It is
not conservative: λ = 0 is **exactly** the Phase-2 rule. The contract froze the
right quantity for a reason that turned out to be better than the one given.

`local_sim/p2_lab.py` now carries a comment saying that re-running that ladder
today enforces the cliff and may fail an arm that passed then — correct behaviour,
and a difference that must not be read as a regression.

## What this does NOT establish

- **Nothing about the grader's own configuration.** Every limit here is a PACKAGE
  fact corroborated by a real `whest run` `run_config`. No graded report we hold
  publishes any of them, and there is no graded Phase-2 report at all.
- **Nothing about the grader's seconds.** The subprocess path is the deployment
  authority and is itself a proxy.
- **Nothing about memory on the grader**, for the reasons above.
- **Nothing about any method.** No candidate was compared, no seed block spent, no
  gate evaluated. The instrument is now trustworthy; that is a precondition for
  evidence, not evidence.
- **The one-row anchor is one row.** Reconciled op by op it is strong evidence
  about a *value-independent dense path* and weak evidence about anything
  value-dependent. The claim is scoped to the former (contract confounder C3).

## Knowledge delta

1. The local meter reproduces the official runner **exactly**, op by op, and the
   two mechanisms that separated them are named, tested in both directions, and
   regression-gated (preflight step 12, which **refuses** rather than skips when
   the official report is absent).
2. **λ = 0 retires residual pricing** and replaces it with a cliff. `VALIDATION.md`
   §2b is Phase-1 law; §2b-ii is what governs Phase 2.
3. **A constant can keep its spelling and change its meaning**, and that is worse
   than being deleted, because every test that checks the name still passes.
4. **The 8 GiB limit is unenforceable here** and is an accounting constraint, not a
   test. 8.9× headroom for the shipped file, as a lower bound.
5. **The three residual instruments are indistinguishable at this shape** (±7 %
   run-to-run). The Phase-1 ~7× figure is local-vs-graded and has no Phase-2
   counterpart. The shipped file has ~8× headroom at the median and **4.6× on its
   worst observed MLP** — a first-class design constraint for a carrier that is
   about to propagate 32,768 directions.
6. **A free 32,768 FLOPs is available to any candidate returning float32**, at no
   accuracy cost. Requires a STRATEGIC contract; not taken here.
7. **The estimator is budget-adaptive**, so a shape and a budget are not
   independent knobs. `LifecycleSpec.for_round()` now takes a round's six constants
   together and records any deviation in the run's provenance.
8. **A gate cannot catch what it does not look at.** Preflight ran ten green steps
   against the Phase-1 stack for three days. Step 1 now asserts the live one.

**Seed ledger:** unchanged. P01 144/600 consumed, **456 free**. D17 and D19
SINGLE_USE and unspent. **Vault:** untouched, counter unmoved.

**Driver:** Claude Opus 5 (1M context), repo-local Builder.
**Next:** independent Skeptic on the raw artifacts, then Phase 1 of `GAME_PLAN.md`
— the width-1024 Kerdock/MUB carrier and its invariants, on a new DESIGN block.

# 2026-08-24 — P2-P0 REVIEW: Skeptic **PROVISIONAL**. The counted half holds; the residual half was measuring the wrong quantity

*Independent Skeptic, fresh context, given the contract, the diff `e8afcbf..e98e96b`,
the evaluation protocol and the raw artifact paths — never a prose summary. It ran
the full protocol plus its own probes.*

**Verdict: PROVISIONAL.** Its strongest challenge, in its own framing: *the
counted-FLOP half of this slice is genuinely repaired and could not be broken; the
residual half is not, and it is the half the next slice depends on.*

Every finding below I reproduced myself before accepting it. Two of the Skeptic's
own claims did not survive that check and are recorded as such — an audit is
evidence, not an oracle.

## Accepted, and fixed

### 1. The memory headroom pointed the wrong way — a sign error in the one constraint we cannot test

`headroom = 8192 / peak_commit` was stored as `headroom_lower_bound` and printed as
"a LOWER BOUND". It is an **upper** bound. `peak_commit` is a *lower* bound on what
`RLIMIT_AS` charges (that bounds virtual address space, which is larger), and
dividing a fixed limit by a lower bound on the denominator gives the **most
optimistic** margin, not the floor.

So `8.9×` is the best case, and the true headroom is smaller by an unmeasured
factor. Inverting the safety direction of the **one limit this host cannot enforce
at all** is the worst available place for a unit error. Fixed in
`test_deployment_envelope.py` and in the three docs that had already copied it.

### 2. A check that could not fail — instance **seven** of the pattern

`p2_flop_anchor.py`'s self-test claimed to prove "the local fallback costs exactly
what the package costs". `_self_test` never called `_stub_whestbench()`, so
`materialise_like_grader` took the *package* branch and the check compared the
package function **to itself**.

And the converse held where it mattered: `_run_arm` *did* stub, and the stub sets
`__path__ = []`, so `from whestbench.scoring import materialise_predictions` raised
`ModuleNotFoundError` and the grader arm **always** used the local re-spelling — in
an interpreter where the real package was importable, under a docstring promising it
"prefers the installed function so this cannot drift". Reproduced both halves
directly.

The anchor number is unaffected (the two implementations genuinely cost the same),
but the guard against drift was doing nothing. Fixed three ways: the stub now
installs **only** when the real package is absent and returns whether it did; the
fallback is a separate function so it can be priced against the package directly;
and the self-test asserts the two are *not the same object* before comparing them,
so it cannot silently become vacuous again.

### 3. "preflight GREEN 16/16" had no witness — and the reason is worse than the claim

The committed transcript was a partial prefix, and the run that completed ended in
`SETUP_TIMEOUT` on step 16. But auditing all three committed transcripts turned up
something larger:

| transcript | lines | `PREFLIGHT` verdict lines | step `PASS` lines |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `preflight_before_stale_stack.txt` | 564 | **0** | **0** |
| `preflight_after_repair_run1.txt` | 595 | **0** | **0** |
| `preflight_full_after_repair.txt` | 912 | **0** | **0** |

**Every preflight transcript this repository has ever committed as evidence is
missing its verdicts.** `preflight.ps1` writes step results and the final summary
with `Write-Host`, which in Windows PowerShell 5.1 goes to the information stream —
and `2>&1 |` does not redirect it. The files captured hundreds of lines of child
process detail and none of the gate's own conclusions. Confirmed with a two-line
control: `2>&1` drops `Write-Host`, `*>&1` keeps it.

This is the repository's own named failure class arriving through a door nobody was
watching: not a check that reported a state instead of testing a property, but a
check whose *verdict never reached the file offered as proof of it*.

Fixed at the source rather than in the caller: `preflight.ps1` gains **`-Log <path>`**,
which uses `Start-Transcript` and captures every stream, and refuses to run if the
transcript cannot be started — a transcript that silently failed to start would
produce exactly the verdict-free file the parameter exists to prevent.

**The witness now exists.** `experiments/2026-08-24_p2_p0/preflight_full_witnessed.txt`
ends in `PREFLIGHT GREEN -- 16/16` with all sixteen step verdicts present, on a
quiet host, exit code 0. It is the first preflight transcript in this repository
that contains its own conclusion.

### 4. `SETUP_TIMEOUT` is real, and our model of the setup window was an order of magnitude out

The completed `-Full` run failed step 16 with
`{"stage": "setup", "code": "SETUP_TIMEOUT"}`. It then reproduced **3/3** on demand.
The Skeptic fairly flagged that its own concurrent probes likely caused it, and it
was right about the cause — but the underlying number is ours:

```text
import numpy + flopscope     0.19 s
import whestbench            1.27 s  (quiet)   ...  4.7-9.1 s  (loaded)
our estimator load + setup   0.0006 s
process spawn                0.20 s
                             ------
TOTAL, quiet                 1.67 s   of a 5.00 s ceiling
```

`import whestbench` **alone** exceeds the entire setup budget under load. Our own
contribution is 0.6 **milliseconds** — six parts in ten thousand of the window.

`lifecycle_eval.HOST_COLD_START_S = 0.24` models the subprocess spawn-and-import
cost, and its self-test reports "419 ms of 5000 ms" — twelve times headroom on a
constraint that had just failed three times in a row. The in-process timer measures
a strictly smaller window than the grader's, and the enforceability matrix listed
`setup_timeout_s` as "enforced here" on that basis. It is enforced against the
**wrong window**.

This does not mean the grader will time out — ~30 entries score fine, so its worker
imports whestbench well inside 5 s. It means **our local setup-headroom figure is
not transferable and must stop being quoted as one**, and it matters for exactly the
work coming next: `docs/GAME_PLAN.md` Module A builds the carrier's point set in
`setup()`, where the grader bills it nothing but the 5 s ceiling still applies.

### 5. `vault.py` used one λ and recorded another

`_score_block` called `effective_compute(f, r)` with the module default — now
**0.0** — while recording `"lambda": LAMBDA_FLOPS_PER_SECOND`, which P2-P0 had just
turned into the deprecated **1e11** Phase-1 alias. Behaviourally harmless (its rows
carry `residual_wall_time_s = 0.0`, so `C == F` either way), but it would have
written a rate it did not use into one of **three touch records that will ever
exist**. Fixed to record `DEFAULT_LAMBDA_FLOPS_PER_SECOND`.

The other five importers of `competition_score` were audited and are clean: they
either pass `lam=spec.lam` explicitly or carry zero residual.

### 6. `arm_k2p1` is not a cost-identical control, and a comment said it was

`p2_lab.py` read: "`k2p1` is BITWISE the shipped `estimator.py` analytic path at
this shape (`p2_test_arms.py` T2), so the control is the thing being controlled".
T2 proves bitwise identity of the **output**. Measured:

```text
estimator.py                   137,600,326,656
local_sim/p2_arms/arm_k2p1.py  137,600,363,520   +36,864 over 3 operations
                                                 (extra astype, concatenate, reshape)
```

Negligible — 0.000027%, and irrelevant while the multiplier is pinned at the floor
— but "bitwise identical output" and "identical cost" are different claims, and
that ladder reports both accuracy **and** cost. Comment corrected with the measured
figure rather than removed.

### 7. Two overclaims and two padded checks

- **`run_config` does not corroborate every limit.** It carries `width`, `depth`,
  `flop_budget`, `lambda`, `residual_wall_time_limit_s`, `wall_time_limit_s`,
  `setup_timeout_s` — and **not** `memory_limit_mb` or `predict_timeout_s`. So the
  **8,192 MB limit, the one constraint untestable here, also has the weakest
  provenance**: a `ContestSpec` class default and nothing more. `CURRENT_STATE.md`
  said "every limit above" and was wrong. `official_config.verify()` now asserts
  those two keys are **absent**, so the generalisation cannot be made again — and
  if a future release starts publishing them, the check fails and the claim gets
  upgraded deliberately.
- **The "free 32,768 FLOPs" is conditional.** It is free only if the final array is
  *natively* float32. Reaching float32 by adding a cast costs the identical
  2 FLOPs/element and nets zero. Stated unconditionally in three places; fixed.
- `official_config.py` had a `check(..., True, ...)` — a literal condition, which
  cannot fail. Now tests the property. `lifecycle_eval.py` L8 had a check that was
  two constants subtracted given its predecessor; demoted to a printed line and
  removed from the denominator. **Suite counts went 71→73 and 54→53**: one
  genuinely gained, one honestly lost.

### 8. Also adopted: the anchor was rebaseable

Not a defect yet, and the Skeptic flagged it as forward-looking. Preflight step 12
compared the current `estimator.py` against a stored report that recorded **no
candidate hash**. The first legitimate estimator change turns the gate RED, and the
remedy the gate itself printed was "regenerate the reference" — which rebases the
reference onto the very change it exists to check. That is the `CP0.1 D19 == 0`
trap in a new place.

The report is now bound to `OFFICIAL_REPORT_CANDIDATE_SHA256`. A different candidate
gets a **REFUSED** naming the mismatch and the required action, not a parity
failure, and the message says in terms: *do not regenerate it to make this gate go
green.*

## Where I checked the Skeptic and it was wrong

**`ladder_frozen.json` contains no residual data.** The review presents a per-arm
residual table and says "the actual failure counts were five lines of arithmetic
away in an artifact the entry already knew about". They were not. The artifact
carries `objective`, per-MLP MSE, `mean_flops`, `flops_012`, `n_failed` — and
`residual_is_graded: false`. There is no residual column in it, or anywhere else in
`experiments/2026-08-21_p2_cp1/`. Its table came from **re-running 96 networks × 11
arms itself**, which is a legitimate and valuable thing to have done, and a
materially different claim from "the entry ignored data it held".

That matters for how much weight the table carries: it was produced on a machine
simultaneously running this session's `preflight -Full` **and** the Skeptic's own
probes — so its absolute levels are exactly as contention-suspect as it argues
everyone else's are.

**The substance survives the correction, and is the important part.** The arms'
residual levels against a now-armed cliff were never measured by anyone, the
architecture's designated reference (`k2p2`) may sit close to it, and P2-P0's
correction to P2-CP1 understated that by saying only that "deployment claims for
the slower arms are provisional".

## The finding that actually changes what happens next

P2-P0 promoted **"the three residual instruments agree to within about ±7 %
run-to-run"** into `VALIDATION.md` §2b-ii, `GOTCHAS.md` and `CURRENT_STATE.md`, and
used it to characterise headroom against the 0.4 s cliff.

**That is the wrong quantity.** ±7 % is an *intra-session, instrument-versus-instrument
ratio*. A cliff compares against an **absolute level**, and an instrument ratio says
nothing about how much that level moves between sessions. The same file, the same
instrument, measured 45.9–53.2 ms in one session and ~69 ms in another — an order of
magnitude outside the interval now written into the binding protocol.

The ratio claim was *true* and was *used for something it cannot support*. That is a
subtler error than a wrong number and it is the one worth remembering: **check that
the interval you quote bounds the quantity the decision depends on.**

`local_sim/p2_residual_paths.py` is rewritten accordingly — it takes `--candidates`
and `--repeat`, reports the **absolute level and its between-pass spread** beside
every headroom figure, and refuses to print a spread it did not measure. §2b-ii is
corrected to require the between-session term.

### The measurement, and it refutes the alarm — including the Skeptic's own

Five candidate-passes × three instruments × 20 MLPs at 1024×16 = **300 per-MLP
readings**, on a quiet host, `--runner subprocess` as the authority
(`experiments/2026-08-24_p2_p0/p2_residual_paths.json`):

| candidate | subprocess median | worst MLP | headroom @ worst | over the 0.4 s cap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `estimator.py` (shipped K2p1) | 56.6 ms | 83.6 ms | 4.8× | **0/20** |
| `arm_k2p1` | 55.9 / 59.4 ms | 95.5 ms | 4.2× | **0/20** |
| `arm_k2p2` — the architecture's reference | 94.6 / 95.1 ms | 140.6 ms | **2.8×** | **0/20** |

**Nothing exceeded the cap, in any arm, in any instrument.** Back-to-back passes
on a quiet host agree to **1.01×–1.06×** on the median.

Against the Skeptic's table for the same arm — **260.7 ms median, 390.6 ms max,
1.02× worst-case headroom** — the quiet-host figure is **2.75× lower**. The
Skeptic flagged that its probes ran beside this session's `preflight -Full` and
declined to claim the gate failed on its merits. That caution was exactly right,
and this quantifies it.

Corroborating from the same run: the one sub-run that fell inside the contended
window — `estimator.py`, pass 0 — is the only one of the fifteen that **died**,
and it died with `SETUP_TIMEOUT`. Contention is visible in both the level and the
failures.

**So the rule that comes out of this is not "add a between-session variance term".**
Back-to-back quiet passes agree to a few percent; the dominant term is not drift,
it is load. The rule is:

> **A residual measurement taken on a contended host is not evidence.** Measure on
> a quiet machine, report the worst MLP and not only the median, and state what
> else was running. A contended reading can be 2.75× high — enough to condemn a
> method that has 2.8× headroom, or to fail a run that would have scored.

That is sharper than a variance term and it is checkable: both contended readings
this repository holds are explained by what ran beside them, and every quiet
reading agrees to a few percent.

### What it means for Phase 1, concretely

`k2p2` spends **~95 ms of the 400 ms** cap on a quiet host. The carrier that
`GAME_PLAN.md` Module A builds sits **on top of** that reference and must propagate
32,768 directions through sixteen layers, so the budget it is designing against is
**~305 ms** — before any safety margin, and before whatever the grader's hardware
does to these numbers, which no graded Phase-2 report can yet tell us.

That number goes into the Phase-1 contract as a design constraint with a falsifier,
not as a check performed after the carrier exists. It is the single most useful
thing this review produced, and the repository did not have it an hour ago.

## Corrections to the P2-P0 result entry, appended not edited

- **"preflight GREEN 16/16, nothing skipped"** was written before a run producing
  that verdict had been captured. The 16/16 run did happen (exit code 0, background
  task `b0yl8jx1i`), but no committed transcript witnessed it, for the `Write-Host`
  reason above. Re-captured with `-Log`; see the table below.
- **The suite table compared a default-tier "10/12" against a `-Full` "16/16"
  without naming either tier**, which `VALIDATION.md` §7 forbids for exactly the
  reason it happened here. The honest comparison is **default 10/12 → 12/16** and
  **`-Full` 12/12 → 16/16**.
- **Mint parity understated its own evidence**: the entry says 8/8 at 1024×16,
  which was an ad-hoc run with `--seeds 8`. The gate runs the default 20, so the
  standing claim is **20/20**.
- Suite counts after this review: `official_config` **73/73** (was 71 — the padded
  check became a real one and two run_config-absence checks were added), anchor
  self-test **14/14**, `lifecycle_eval` **53/53** (was 54 — one padded check
  removed), envelope **14/14 + 2 NOT PROVABLE**, scorer **98/98**, portability
  **99/99**.

## What is NOT retracted

The counted-FLOP repair stands, and the Skeptic verified it independently rather
than reading it:

- op-by-op parity reproduces: 19 operations, 0 disagreeing, delta +0;
- the official side is **parsed from a real report**, not hardcoded;
- **confounder C3 is stronger than P2-P0 claimed** — the Skeptic ran three further
  networks and got byte-identical op tables, so four distinct networks now support
  the value-independence the one-row anchor rests on;
- mechanism 2 confirmed at package source level, both runner paths;
- λ = 0 verified against what the runner *used*;
- the score moves by exactly 0 %;
- **no test was deleted or weakened** — every changed check was a genuine
  round-mixing fix;
- `estimator.py` byte-identical, vault untouched, no seed block claimed;
- **B8's MISS survives a better statistic than the one used to score it.** The
  Skeptic ran the paired per-MLP test this repo's own law prefers:
  lifecycle − subprocess is `−3.99 ms (t = −1.85)` and `+0.68 ms (t = +0.46)`;
  not resolvable, sign unstable. The discarded contaminated run is not load-bearing
  — the two surviving runs already disagree in sign.

## Knowledge delta

1. **Check that the interval you quote bounds the quantity the decision depends
   on.** A true ratio claim was used to characterise a level, and only a level
   clears a cliff.
2. **A transcript is not evidence until you have found its verdict in it.** Three
   committed files, 2,071 lines, zero verdicts.
3. **Dividing a limit by a lower bound gives an upper bound on the margin.** Get
   the direction right on any constraint that cannot be tested.
4. **The setup window the grader enforces is not the one we time.** Ours is
   0.6 ms of it; `import whestbench` is 1.3–9 s of it. Model the window, not our
   share of it — and the carrier builds its point set in `setup()`.
5. **A stub that shadows a real package turns a drift guard into a no-op**, and the
   self-test that should catch it will compare the survivor to itself.
6. An audit is evidence, not an oracle: two of this review's own claims did not
   survive checking, and saying so is part of accepting the rest.

**Seed ledger:** unchanged. P01 144/600 consumed, **456 free**. D17 and D19
SINGLE_USE and unspent. **Vault:** untouched. `estimator.py` byte-identical.

**Driver:** Claude Opus 5 (1M context), repo-local Builder.
**Status:** Phase 0 is accepted with the corrections above applied. The residual
LEVEL question is settled below and carries into the Phase-1 contract as a design
constraint rather than a check performed afterwards.
