# 2026-09-01 — OPEN: the corrector's training set is NOT the dataset the brief names, and the named one is CONFIRM

**Recorded before any corrector is built**, because the answer changes where
Rung 1's highest-EV lever gets its labels, and building first would have meant
fitting on the split this repository forbids fitting on.

## What the brief says

The 2026-09-01 implementation brief, § 8 *Public-source harvest*, directs:

> take freely from public sources: keenanpepper's HF datasets
> `aicrowd/arc-whestbench-public-2026` (500k MLPs w/ per-layer means; 10k w/
> 4th moments) for corrector training

and its § 4 makes that corrector (**N2**) the *highest expected value* lever in
the whole program, on the grounds that offline compute is unmetered.

## What that dataset actually is

I read the cached copy rather than trusting the citation
(`~/.cache/huggingface/hub/datasets--aicrowd--arc-whestbench-public-2026`,
16 GB, pinned at `6a416fa5…`, the commit `WP0A` repinned to):

| field | value |
|---|---|
| configs | exactly two — `default` -> `data/mini-*.parquet`, `full` -> `data/full-*.parquet` |
| `size_categories` | **`1K<n<10K`** |
| `splits.mini.n_mlps` | **`100`** |
| `n_samples` | `1_000_000_000` per MLP |
| license / homepage | `cc-by-4.0`, the challenge page |

**It is the competition's own public evaluation data — 100 MLPs in `mini` — and
it is the CONFIRM tier.** It is not a 500k-MLP corpus and contains no separate
training corpus. `README.md` and `metadata.json` both agree.

## Why this is a blocker as written, not a detail

The same brief's § 6 says, in its own words:

> public-mini split is **CONFIRM-only** (fit no basis/coefficient/rank/threshold
> on it)

and `AGENTS.md` § *Measurement law* says the public split is *"read-only; no
constant may ever be fitted there."* Training a corrector on
`aicrowd/arc-whestbench-public-2026` is **exactly** fitting coefficients on
CONFIRM. Followed literally, § 8 instructs the violation that § 6 forbids, and
the reason is a citation error, not a change of policy: nothing anywhere else in
the brief or the repository proposes relaxing the tier rule.

I could not confirm that a 500k-MLP dataset exists under any owner. One targeted
search returned nothing matching. **Absence of evidence here is weak** — it may
exist on the Hub under a personal namespace, and Samuel, who wrote the brief,
may simply know the right path.

## What to do instead, and it is strictly better

**Mint our own training set.** The corrector needs
`(cumulant-trajectory features -> truth - prediction)` pairs. This repository
already mints grader-identical `1024x16` networks (`local_sim/mint_provenance.py`)
and computes their truth (`local_sim/p2_truth.py`, `gpu_mint.py`). Offline
compute is unmetered, so the only cost is GPU wall time, which goes through
`gpuq`.

Own mints are better than the public data for this purpose on three counts, not
merely equal:

1. **Disjoint from CONFIRM by construction**, so the tier law is satisfied
   rather than argued around;
2. **exactly the live shape**, whereas any public corpus would be whatever shape
   its author chose;
3. **truth precision is ours to set** — and every MSE this project quotes must
   carry its GT-noise floor, which is only knowable for truth we generated.

The cost is real and should not be waved away: the public route would have been
free labels, and minting is GPU time we now have to spend.

## Binding conditions when the corrector is built

- Training networks come from **`P02`** (DESIGN, allocated 2026-09-01, 96 seeds,
  `40,901,002,000..40,901,002,095`), never from `mini`, `full`, or `P01`'s
  already-spent range.
- **Leave-networks-out** validation, not leave-rows-out: rows within one MLP are
  not independent, and a corrector that memorises a network is worthless on a
  fresh suite. The brief says this and it is right.
- Whatever `P02` selects is replicated on **`P03`** before it is reported.
- The `>= 0.3` held-out `R^2` gate is fixed in the Rule-1 contract before data
  exists, and it is scored on **`P03`**, not `P02`.
- Prediction clamped at `+/- k sigma`, `k` fixed in the contract, so a corrector
  that extrapolates badly on a hard MLP degrades instead of exploding.
- The Phase-1 *"correctors don't work"* kill was measured at `L/n = 1/8`; live is
  `1/64`. It does not transfer, and the contract should say so rather than
  quietly ignoring it.

## What Samuel is owed

One question, and it does not block the work — I proceed on own mints either
way:

> **Is there a real 500k-MLP public dataset, and if so what is its actual path?**
> If it exists and is disjoint from `mini`/`full`, it is free labels at a scale
> we cannot mint cheaply, and N2 gets substantially stronger. If it does not,
> nothing changes; own mints were already the plan.

Until answered, treat the § 8 line as a **citation error against a CONFIRM-tier
dataset** and do not fit on it.

# 2026-09-01 — CONTRACT WP8: the soak counted 45 failures and cannot say why, and its median is computed over rows that never ran

**IMPORTANT.** Instrument repair on `local_sim/certify_candidate.py`. Reads
CONFIRM-tier truth (the organisers' `mini` split) for residual only; selects
nothing, fits nothing, claims no accuracy. No seed block, no vault touch, no
`estimator.py` edit.

## Question

WP6's `--residual-soak` ran for the first time, on the **shipped v2.6.1 canary**
-- the exact file the grading server ran with **zero** failed MLPs -- and
returned `n_failed_mlps = 45` of `300` rows, verdict **REFUSED**
(`experiments/2026-09-01_wp6_meter/certify_v261_soak3.json`, committed at
`d22d0cb`). Two questions follow, and the second was not visible until I read
the package:

1. **Why did 45 MLPs fail?** The soak records the count and discards the reason.
2. **Is the pooled residual tail it reports even a tail of executed work?**

## Evidence

| item | status |
|---|---|
| graded #328662 = this exact file, `n_failed_mlps: 0` on 100 organiser MLPs | **CONFIRMED** -- `experiments/run_reports/submission_328662_*_graded_report.json` |
| the same file's prior local official mini run: `4.050566e-7`, **0 failures** | **CONFIRMED** -- `CURRENT_STATE.md` section on the shipped estimator |
| the soak's own worst residual is `90.2 ms` against a `400 ms` cap (`4.43x`) | **CONFIRMED** -- no row is near the cliff, so **residual exhaustion is not the failure mode** |
| `whestbench/scoring.py:1059-1075` builds a `failure_breakdown` splitting failures into `budget_exhausted` / `time_exhausted` / `residual_wall_time_exhausted` / `combined_budget_exhausted` / `error` | **CONFIRMED** -- the soak reads `n_failed_mlps` and **never reads this** |
| `whestbench/scoring.py:790-850` -- on the **exception** path a failed row is appended with `"residual_wall_time_s": 0.0` | **CONFIRMED by source reading** |
| host peak working set for one official mini run is `14.32 GiB` | **CONFIRMED** -- measured 2026-09-01, `docs/SETUP_WINDOWS.md` 7.1 |
| this host has a documented `SETUP_TIMEOUT`-under-contention failure history (preflight 15/16) and a `2.35x` session-to-session residual spread | **CONFIRMED** |

## Hypothesis and mechanism

**H1 -- the failures are exceptions, not cap exhaustions, and they are
host-side.** Mechanism: no row is within `4.4x` of the residual cap and the
counted FLOP total is fixed and network-independent for this file
(`137,600,326,656`), so neither the FLOP budget nor the residual cliff can
discriminate 45 rows from the other 255. What differs between rows is only *the
host at that moment*. The soak run is a `14.32 GiB` process repeated three
times on a box that brokers concurrent agents, and this repository has already
recorded one contention-induced failure class on exactly this instrument.

**H2 -- the soak's pooled median is computed over rows that never executed, and
is therefore biased LOW.** Mechanism, from source, not inference: the exception
path sets `residual_wall_time_s = 0.0`. Those 45 zeros enter the pooled sample
and sort to the bottom. The reported "median" at sorted rank `150/300` is
therefore the `105`th of `255` real rows -- the **41st percentile** of executed
work wearing the label `median`. `worst` is unaffected (a max ignores zeros),
which is precisely why the defect is invisible in the number a reader checks.

## Intervention

The smallest change that discriminates. `_residual_soak` and `_smoke` gain:

- **`failure_breakdown`** -- the runner's own five-way split, summed across reps.
- **`failures`** -- per failed MLP, its `mlp_index`, `mlp_name`, `error_code`
  and the first line of `error`. Capped at 40 records so a pathological run
  cannot produce an unbounded artifact.
- **`residual_rows_excluded_failed`** and a residual sample taken over
  **executed rows only**, with the contaminated figures kept alongside as
  `*_all_rows` so the correction is visible rather than silently applied.

Check 11 gains a clause naming the dominant failure mode, so a future REFUSED
carries its reason in the transcript instead of in a later investigation.

## Numbered predictions, recorded before the repaired instrument runs

*Human prediction slot: **waived by Samuel (solo), 2026-09-01**. Falsification
runs against these.*

| # | prediction | direction / magnitude |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | the repaired soak attributes the failures to **`error`**, not to any of the four exhaustion flags | `failure_breakdown["error"]` carries at least `90%` of the failures |
| **P2** | the `error_code` is a **worker/runner-level** code (a `RunnerError` code or a process-death class), not an exception raised inside the shipped file's own math | if the traceback lands in `estimator.py`, H1 is wrong and the shipped file has a real live-shape bug |
| **P3** | recomputing the **committed** soak's median over executed rows only raises it | at least `1.05x` above the reported `47.432 ms`; `worst` is **unchanged** at `90.224 ms` |
| **P4** | a fresh small diagnostic run (`1 x 12` MLPs) submitted to `gpuq` with the footprint declared shows a **materially lower** failure rate than `45/300 = 15%` | at most `1/12`; if it reproduces at `~15%` the cause is not transient contention and H1 needs a second mechanism |
| **P5** | counted FLOPs on every executed row remain exactly `137,600,326,656` | this file does not prune; a different number means the arm is not the arm |

## Falsifier

- **H1 is rejected** if `failure_breakdown` attributes the failures to
  `time_exhausted` or `residual_wall_time_exhausted` (then the cliff *is* the
  mechanism and every residual claim in this repository needs re-examination),
  or if P2's traceback lands inside `estimator.py` (then the shipped file has a
  live-shape defect and the graded zero-failure result needs explaining).
- **H2 is rejected** if excluding the failed rows leaves the median within
  `1.005x` -- then the zeros are not where I claim and the source reading is
  wrong.

## Cost model

Phase 2, `lambda = 0`, `C = F`. This slice changes **no estimator** and
therefore **no counted FLOP**. Its own cost is wall time on the local host,
submitted through `gpuq` at the declared `--ram 20 --cpus 6` footprint. The
residual figure it produces is reported as **headroom `0.4 / observed`** on the
worst **executed** row, per `VALIDATION.md` 2b-ii -- never as a price, never as
a grader prediction.

## What must not change

`estimator.py` (byte-identical to its archive), the ship-file gate,
`preflight.ps1`, any seed block, the vault, the three-tier protocol.
`certify_candidate` stays read-only with respect to the repository. The soak
remains a **residual** instrument: it may read the split's labels and must
return no accuracy statistic.

# 2026-09-01 — CONTRACT WP9: a per-neuron, scale-equivariant IN-FLIGHT state corrector, gated on ROLLOUT and not on fit

**STRATEGIC.** Spends the `P02` DESIGN block, replicates on `P03`, and is
allowed nowhere near `P04` or CONFIRM. Pre-registered before any data exists.
It does not edit `estimator.py`; a promotion would be a later contract of its
own.

## Question

K2's error is **94.61% accumulated (mu, sigma) state drift** and only **4.47%**
readout (P2-CP3R, durable result). Does a corrector that acts **per neuron, at
every layer, on the propagated state** — rather than per layer, and rather than
only at the readout — recover a material fraction of that 94.61%, at a cost
that leaves the multiplier pinned at the `0.1` floor?

## Evidence

| item | status |
|---|---|
| `94.61%` of K2's error is accumulated mean/variance-state drift; the marginal ReLU-mean-map readout ceiling is `4.47%` | **CONFIRMED** — P2-CP3R |
| resetting to **true marginal state every layer** removes essentially all of it | **CONFIRMED** — the same CP3R oracle. This is the ceiling WP9 chases, and it is an oracle, not an achievable arm |
| offline scalar calibration of the K2 state transfers: DESIGN `2.962x` vs public `2.908x`, agreeing to `1.9%` | **CONFIRMED** — P2-CAL, then graded as #328664 at `2.8629x`. **This licenses the offline fitting loop the whole slice rests on** |
| the K2 closure is **exactly positively homogeneous of degree 1**: `(mu, cov) -> (g mu, g^2 cov)` leaves `alpha` unchanged and scales every mean by `g`, verified to `1.6e-30` | **CONFIRMED** — P2-CAL. Any purely multiplicative state correction **is one output rescale in disguise** |
| **per-layer scalar** calibration is EXHAUSTED at `2.96x`: a per-layer gain on post-ReLU variance and on off-diagonal covariance both fitted `~1%` in-fit and lost **all** of it out of sample, intervals straddling zero | **CONFIRMED** — P2-CAL part 2. Its own recorded conclusion: the next correction must act **per neuron**, or add information |
| the Phase-1 "correctors don't work" kill was measured at `L/n = 1/8`; live is `1/64` | **CONFIRMED** as a scope limit — it does not transfer, and this contract does not lean on it either way |
| an in-flight corrector changes the state the next layer consumes, so a teacher-forced fit is **not** the deployed quantity | **CONFIRMED by construction** — and `CURRENT_STATE.md`'s lane table already carries "equivariant learned state corrector — conditional; **rollout/cross-fit required**" |
| `local_sim/p2_truth.py` emits `means_r{1,2}` and `var_r{1,2}` at **every layer**, two independent replicas | **CONFIRMED** — read from source, `savez_compressed` at `:257` |
| the corrector's training corpus is **our own mints**, never `mini`/`full` | **CONFIRMED** — settled in the 2026-09-01 WP7 entry; the brief's cited 500k-MLP dataset is the CONFIRM tier itself |

## Hypothesis and mechanism

**H1 — the correctable part of the drift is a function of scale-invariant
per-neuron state, and K2 already holds it.** Mechanism: K2's ReLU mean map is
exactly `E[ReLU(X)] = sigma * (alpha Phi(alpha) + phi(alpha))` with
`alpha = mu / sigma`. The prediction is therefore `sigma * h(alpha)`, and the
residual of a degree-1 homogeneous estimator against a degree-1 homogeneous
truth must itself be `sigma * r(scale-invariants)`. The drift is not white: it
is generated by the Gaussian closure discarding the same non-Gaussian mass at
every layer, and how much it discards at a given neuron is governed by where
that neuron sits in the firing-probability distribution — which is exactly
`alpha`. So `r` should be learnable from `alpha` plus a few layer-level
scale-invariant summaries.

**H2 — acting at EVERY layer beats acting at the readout by roughly the CP3R
ratio.** Mechanism: a readout-only corrector can only re-map the final layer's
marginal, which CP3R bounds at `4.47%`. An in-flight corrector changes the
state layer `l+1` consumes, so its effect compounds down the tower — which is
also precisely why it must be gated on rollout.

**Why this is not the correction P2-CAL exhausted.** P2-CAL's arms were per
**layer** scalars: one number per layer, constant across neurons. This slice's
correction varies across neurons *within* a layer as a function of `alpha`. The
homogeneity collapse P2-CAL proved applies to the constant-in-`alpha` member of
this family and to nothing else — which makes that member an exact **null
control**, not a competitor (N1 below).

## Intervention

The smallest change that discriminates, built as an offline-fitted correction
on top of the shipped f32 K2p1 state. Per layer `l`, per neuron `j`, from
quantities K2 **already computes**:

- scale-invariant per-neuron features: `alpha`, `Phi(alpha)`, `phi(alpha)`,
  `alpha` standardised within its layer, and `l / (L - 1)`;
- scale-invariant layer summaries broadcast to every neuron: `mean(alpha)`,
  `std(alpha)`, `mean(Phi(alpha))`;
- outputs: `c_m` and `c_v`, applied as
  `post-ReLU mean <- sigma * (h(alpha) + c_m)` and
  `post-ReLU var <- var * (1 + c_v)`.

Because the correction is `sigma` times a function of scale invariants, the
**degree-1 homogeneity of the closure is preserved exactly** — the corrected
estimator is still degree-1 homogeneous, so it cannot be an accidental
rescale-in-disguise unless `c_m` is constant, which N1 tests directly.

**Off-diagonal covariance is NOT touched.** P2-CAL's C4 tried a per-layer
off-diagonal gain and lost it out of sample. Extending there is a different
slice with its own contract.

The corrector is a two-layer MLP, `<= 32` hidden units, distilled to plain
`fnp` matmuls. Predictions are clamped to `|c_m| <= 3 * sigma_train(c_m)` and
`|c_v| <= 0.5`, both **fixed here, before any data**, so a corrector that
extrapolates on a hard MLP degrades instead of exploding.

## Arms

| arm | what | why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| **B0** | shipped calibrated K2 (v2.7-equivalent) | the baseline every difference is measured against |
| **A** | corrector at the **final layer only** | the readout-only control. CP3R bounds it at `~4.5%`; if it beats B, H2 is wrong |
| **B** | corrector at **every layer**, evaluated by **full rollout** | the candidate |
| **B-tf** | arm B scored **teacher-forced** | recorded to expose the fit-versus-rollout gap, and it may NOT be quoted as a result |
| **N1** | arm B with `c_m` constrained constant per layer | **null control.** By P2-CAL's homogeneity proof this must collapse onto a per-layer scalar arm. If it does not, the implementation is wrong, not the theory |
| **N2** | arm B with features **shuffled across neurons** within a layer | **null control.** Destroys the per-neuron signal while preserving every marginal. Must recover `~0` |

## Data and tiers

- Fit on **`P02`** (DESIGN, 96 seeds, `40,901,002,000..095`), `2**22` samples
  per replica, two independent replicas.
- **Leave-networks-out** cross-validation *within* `P02` for every design choice
  — feature set, hidden width, clamps. Rows within one MLP are not independent
  and a corrector that memorises a network is worthless on a fresh suite.
- Report on **`P03`** (DESIGN, 96 seeds, `40,901,003,000..095`), which is
  touched **once**, after `P02` has selected exactly one configuration.
- `P04` (SINGLE_USE, 100) is **not** spent here. It is the one paired DECIDE
  against graded v2.7 and is reserved for a promotion contract.
- CONFIRM (`mini`/`full`) is read for **nothing** in this slice.

## Numbered predictions, recorded before any data exists

*Human prediction slot: **waived by Samuel (solo), 2026-09-01**. Falsification
runs against these.*

| # | prediction | direction / magnitude |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | arm **A** (readout-only) recovers little, consistent with CP3R's ceiling | held-out raw-MSE improvement over B0 of `1.00x`–`1.10x` |
| **P2** | arm **B** teacher-forced looks much better than arm **B** rolled out | `B-tf / B` improvement ratio `>= 1.5x`. **If teacher-forced and rollout agree within `1.1x` I am wrong about the compounding and should say so** |
| **P3** | arm **B** on **rollout**, held out on `P03`, beats B0 | raw-MSE improvement `>= 1.5x`; my point estimate is `2.5x`, and I expect the interval to be wide |
| **P4** | the null control **N1** collapses onto a per-layer scalar arm | agreement to `<= 1e-6` relative on the scored row; anything larger is an implementation bug |
| **P5** | the null control **N2** recovers essentially nothing | `<= 1.05x` over B0, interval straddling zero |
| **P6** | the corrector's counted cost is **negligible** against the free zone | `<= 5e8` counted FLOPs, i.e. `<= 0.7%` of the `8.23e10` unused free zone, so the multiplier stays pinned at `0.1` |
| **P7** | the `P02 -> P03` transfer holds, as it did for P2-CAL | `P03` improvement within `1.3x` of the `P02` leave-networks-out figure. A larger gap means I fitted the block, not the phenomenon |

## Gate — chosen now, and written on the DIFFERENCE the slice isolates

Passed to `local_sim/competition_score.decide(gate=...)`, which has no default.
All three clauses, conjunctive:

- **G1 (accuracy).** On `P03`, the **paired arithmetic adjusted-score
  difference** of arm B (rollout) against B0, common random numbers, with a
  **studentised-t or basic-bootstrap** 95% interval **excluding zero**, and a
  point improvement of **`>= 1.5x`**. Percentile and BCa are refused.
- **G2 (price).** Counted flopscope FLOPs for the whole corrected estimator,
  **including the `+2**24` server offset**, at or below `2.199e11`, so the
  multiplier stays pinned at `0.1`. Measured, not projected.
- **G3 (deployability).** `certify_candidate --residual-soak` with **zero**
  failed MLPs and worst-executed-row residual headroom within `2x` of frozen
  v2.6.1's on the same instrument, in the same session.

**G1 is deliberately set at `1.5x`, below the `2x` engineering bar
`CURRENT_STATE.md` recommends for a *promotion*.** This gate authorises a
**promotion contract**, not a promotion: `1.5x` on a lane whose oracle is
`94.61%` is evidence the mechanism is live and worth a `P04` spend. Nothing
here may be submitted on a `1.5x`.

## Falsifier

- **H1 is rejected** if arm B on **rollout**, held out on `P03`, improves B0 by
  `< 1.2x` or its interval straddles zero. Then per-neuron `alpha`-indexed
  state correction is dead **for this feature set**, and the honest next
  question is whether the missing information is in the off-diagonal or in a
  third cumulant — not a wider corrector.
- **H2 is rejected** if arm A (readout-only) matches or beats arm B on rollout.
- **The slice is void** — not negative, void — if N1 fails to collapse (P4) or
  N2 recovers more than `1.05x` (P5). Either means the harness is leaking, and
  no accuracy number from this slice may be quoted until it is fixed.

## Cost model

Phase 2, `lambda = 0`, so `C = F`; residual is not a price but a `0.4 s`
per-MLP cliff. **Frozen now, before any data:**

- **Counted-FLOP model.** The corrector adds, per layer, two `n x F` by
  `F x H` matmuls and an `n x H` by `H x 2` matmul, plus `O(nF)` feature
  construction: `2 n (F H + H H + 2 H) + c n F` FLOPs per layer, `L` layers. At
  `n = 1024, L = 16, F <= 12, H <= 32` this is **under `5e8`**, against the
  `8.23e10` free zone — the number P6 commits to and G2 measures.
- **Residual.** Reported as **headroom `0.4 / worst executed row`** on the
  `--runner subprocess` runner, per `VALIDATION.md` 2b-ii, against frozen
  v2.6.1 measured **in the same session**. The op-count axis is the one to
  watch: the corrector adds `~5` ops per layer, `~80` per MLP, on top of K2p1's
  19 — small, but it is op count and Python glue that drives residual, not
  FLOPs.
- Never a local absolute wall time, never a grader prediction.

## Confounders, scope, what must not change

- **Rollout, not fit.** G1 is scored on arm B **rolled out**. `B-tf` exists
  only to measure the gap and is not a result.
- **Every MSE is quoted with its GT-noise floor**, from the two-replica
  cross-product estimator, which is unbiased for `MSE(p)` because `E[e1 e2] = 0`.
- **Off-diagonal covariance, the third cumulant, the carrier and AUGMENT are
  all out of scope** and must not be tuned inside this slice.
- Must not change: `estimator.py` (byte-identical to its archive), the ship-file
  gate, `preflight.ps1`, `competition_score.py`, the vault, `P04`, the
  three-tier protocol, `HUMAN_MODEL.md`.
- **`P03` is touched once.** If I look at `P03` and then change anything, `P03`
  has become a DESIGN block and the slice has no replication left — that is a
  spent block and a failed slice, and it gets recorded as one.

# 2026-09-02 — RESULT WP8: the instrument is repaired, the 45 failures did NOT reproduce, and one of my own predictions was not executable

Contract: *CONTRACT WP8* above, committed at `e7b83c2` **before the repair**.
Repair at `229488f`. Artifacts: `experiments/2026-09-01_wp8_soak/diag_12.json`
(attributed, `CERTIFIED`) beside the original
`experiments/2026-09-01_wp6_meter/certify_v261_soak3.json` (`REFUSED`).

## What was repaired, and it is the durable part

| defect | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| failures counted, never attributed | `n_failed_mlps: 45` and nothing else | the runner's five-way `failure_breakdown`, a per-row `error_code`, the traceback's **last** line, and **the deepest failing frame that lies in this repository** |
| the pooled tail included rows that never ran | `scoring.py`'s exception path stamps a failed row `residual_wall_time_s = 0.0`; those zeros sorted to the bottom of the sample | tail over **executed rows only**, with the contaminated figures kept beside it as `*_all_rows` and an explicit `median_bias_from_failed_rows` |
| the arithmetic could only be exercised by a three-hour official run | so in practice it never was | `_pool_residual` is **pure**; 16 unit tests run in milliseconds |

The unit tests are the part that will still be paying rent in a month. **U2**
reproduces the 45/300 shape in miniature and measures the bias at **`1.667x`**;
**U4** proves a fault inside the candidate is distinguishable from a host
fault; **U5** proves a cliff overrun is attributed to the cliff and **cannot
masquerade as the tail**; **U6** refuses an all-failed run rather than
reporting `0 ms` residual; **U1** asserts our copied `_FAILURE_FLAGS` against
the installed `whestbench`, so a package change breaks a test instead of
silently making our failure count disagree with the runner's.

## The re-measurement

`certify_candidate --candidate estimator.py --residual-soak 1 --soak-n-mlps 12`,
submitted through `gpuq` at the declared `--ram 20 --cpus 6` footprint:

| | value |
|---|---:|
| failed MLPs | **`0` of `12`** |
| `failure_breakdown` | all five categories `0` |
| rows excluded as never-executed | `0` |
| worst executed residual | `70.10 ms` |
| p99 / median | `70.10` / `51.90 ms` |
| headroom on the worst row | **`5.71x`** |
| verdict | **`CERTIFIED`**, 39 checks, 0 failed |

## Scoring my own predictions

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | failures attribute to `error`, not to an exhaustion flag | **NOT TESTABLE.** There were no failures to attribute. The machinery works — the breakdown is read, summed and printed — but this run carries no evidence about *which* category the original 45 fell into, and I will not infer one |
| **P2** | the failing frame is harness-side, not inside `estimator.py` | **NOT TESTABLE**, same reason. The discriminator (`deepest_repo_frame`) exists and is unit-tested (U4); it has not yet met a real failure |
| **P3** | recomputing the committed soak's median over executed rows raises it by `>= 1.05x` | **NOT EXECUTABLE, AND THAT IS A DEFECT IN MY OWN CONTRACT.** The committed artifact stored `worst`, `p99` and `median` — **not the rows** — so there is nothing to recompute. I wrote a prediction about data the artifact had already thrown away, and only found out by trying to run it. The *mechanism* is confirmed instead, by U2, at `1.667x` on a synthetic 5-of-15 case; the *specific* `45/300` bias is unrecoverable and stays unknown |
| **P4** | a fresh `1 x 12` run shows a failure rate materially below `45/300 = 15%` | **THRESHOLD MET, INFERENCE WEAK, and the threshold was the wrong one to pick.** `0/12` satisfies "`<= 1/12`", but under a true `15%` rate `P(0 of 12) = 0.85^12 = 0.142`. A `14%` event is not evidence. I chose a sample size that could not answer the question I asked it |
| **P5** | worst pooled residual clears the cliff with `> 3x` headroom | **HELD**, `5.71x` — but on **12** executed rows in one quiet session, not on 300. `AGENTS.md` refuses a local absolute wall time as a grader prediction and this changes nothing about that |

Two of five untestable, one unexecutable, one met on a threshold I now think
was badly chosen. The contract's *value* was that the repair had to be
specified before the data arrived; its *predictions* were mostly aimed at a
failure this run did not produce.

## What is still open, and it is the whole question

**The 45 failures are UNEXPLAINED.** What is now known:

- they were **not** residual-cliff overruns — the worst row in that very run
  was `90.2 ms` against a `400 ms` cap;
- they were **not** budget exhaustion — this file's counted FLOP total is fixed
  and network-independent at `137,600,326,656`;
- the same file graded **`0/100`** on the real server (#328662) and had
  previously run a local official mini at **`0` failures**;
- they did **not** reproduce in a 12-row run submitted through `gpuq` with a
  declared `20 GiB` footprint — and the original soak does **not** appear in
  the `gpuq` job history, so it was very likely run directly, on a box that
  brokers concurrent agents, at a measured `14.32 GiB` peak working set.

That last point is a *hypothesis with a motive*, not a finding. **The
discriminating experiment is a `1 x 100` attributed run: under a `15%` rate,
`P(0 of 100) ~ 1e-7`.** It is submitted and pending. Until it returns:

> **No certification produced by the pre-`229488f` soak may be quoted, and no
> candidate may be certified on a soak whose failures are unattributed.**

## Knowledge delta

1. A residual instrument that pools failed rows reports a **median it has no
   right to** while leaving `worst` — the number a reader checks — untouched.
   That asymmetry is why the defect survived; it is now a named field and a
   unit test.
2. `whestbench` already computes a `failure_breakdown` and a per-row
   `error_code` and traceback. Two of this repository's instruments were
   discarding all of it. Read what the package returns before adding a
   diagnostic of your own.
3. **Write predictions the artifact can actually answer.** P3 asked for a
   recomputation from rows that were never stored; P4 picked a sample size that
   could not distinguish its own hypothesis from chance. Both were written
   carefully and neither was executable as intended.

# 2026-09-02 — SKEPTIC WP8: PROVISIONAL, accepted in full. The attribution half was broken, and I moved one of my own pre-registered predictions

Independent pass on `d22d0cb` / `e7b83c2` / `229488f` / `9efda91`, from the raw
artifacts. Verdict **PROVISIONAL**. Every finding is accepted; the two that
matter most are defects in *my record*, not in the code.

## What it confirmed (steelmanned, and it tried)

- **The source reading is exactly right.** `scoring.py:790-857` is the generic
  exception handler; `"residual_wall_time_s": 0.0` at **line 849**,
  `"flops_used": 0` at 840, `error_code` at 809/812, `continue` at 857.
- **The bias direction and magnitude reproduce.** Nearest-rank `k =
  ceil(0.5*300) - 1 = 149`, the 105th smallest of 255 executed rows — the
  **41.18th percentile**. U2's `1.667x` reproduces exactly.
- **The 45 failures MUST have been exception-path**, by elimination:
  `residual_wall_time_exhausted` would have put a row above `0.4 s` and the
  artifact's worst is `0.09022`; `budget_exhausted` is impossible at a fixed
  `137,600,326,656` against `2**41`; `time_exhausted` needs `> 120 s` and
  leaves a real residual. **This is stronger than anything I established** —
  my own entry called P1 untestable, and the Skeptic settled it by argument
  from the artifact.
- `_row_failed` is verbatim `_is_failed_entry` (`certify_candidate.py:772-773`
  vs `scoring.py:1043-1044`); no row can be counted and not excluded.
- **The unit tests are load-bearing:** 12 mutations driven, **10 caught by a
  specifically named check**, baseline 16/16 clean.
- Rule-1 ordering is clean and was verified by timestamp and by md5: the
  contract precedes the repair, and the run used the repaired bytes.

## Finding 1 — the attribution half was BROKEN, and its guard test could not fail

`deepest_repo_frame` matched the substrings `"estimator"` or `"arc-whest"`.
**`.venv/` lives inside `C:/Users/samsu/Documents/arc-whest/`**, so every
absolute path `traceback.format_exc()` emits for a `whestbench` or `flopscope`
frame contains `arc-whest` — and `scoring.py:716`'s own source line
`raw_predictions = estimator.predict(...)` contains `estimator`. Driven against
a **real** `format_exc()` raised inside the installed package, with no
participant code anywhere in the stack, it returned

```
'File "C:\\...\\arc-whest\\.venv\\lib\\site-packages\\whestbench\\scoring.py", line 421, ...'
```

and the certifier printed `*** A FAILING FRAME IS IN THIS REPOSITORY. This is
NOT host contention:`. **The field that prediction P2 turns on answered "the
candidate" for a pure harness fault.**

It is worse than a false positive in the abstract. `runner.py:190-196` raises
`SETUP_TIMEOUT` from a worker restart with `traceback=None`, so `scoring.py:800`
falls back to the *host's* `format_exc()` — meaning the single most likely
cause of 45 contention-driven failures on this documented `SETUP_TIMEOUT`-prone
host is exactly the case that would have been misreported.

**My guard test passed only because its fixture lied.** `_TB_HOST` used the
relative path `File "whestbench/runner.py"`, which `format_exc()` never
produces.

**Repaired.** `_candidate_frame()` matches the **candidate file's own absolute
path**, threaded in from `main()`, and skips any path segment starting
`.venv` or equal to `site-packages`. The field is renamed
`deepest_candidate_frame`. Three tests now cover it, and the fixture is a real
`format_exc()` shape with absolute paths under the repository root:
**U3** (a harness fault under the repo root claims no candidate frame),
**U4b** (the same traceback asked about a *different* candidate file is not
claimed), **U4c** (an installed-package frame under the repo root is excluded).
The review's mutation MU12 — narrowing the heuristic to `"arc-whest"` alone —
survived the old battery with zero named failures; it cannot now.

## Finding 2 — I SWAPPED A PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION. Checklist 13, and it is mine

The contract (`LOG.md`, CONTRACT WP8) fixed:

> **P5** — counted FLOPs on every executed row remain exactly
> `137,600,326,656`

The result scored:

> **P5** — worst pooled residual clears the cliff with `> 3x` headroom — HELD,
> `5.71x`

**These are not the same proposition.** The one I scored is **WP6's** P5; I
carried it across from the previous contract and reported it as though it were
this one's. The contract's actual P5 is reported nowhere, and — worse — the
soak stored **no per-row `flops_used` for executed rows**, so `diag_12.json`
cannot answer it either. Section 10's `flops_per_mlp` is a `max` over **two**
smoke rows, which is not "every executed row".

So: **the contract's P5 is UNSCORED.** Not held, not refuted — unscored,
because I substituted a different question and because the instrument recorded
nothing that could answer the real one.

**Repaired so it is answerable next time:** `_pool_residual` now records
`flops_executed_min`, `flops_executed_max` and `flops_executed_constant` across
executed rows, and check 11 gained *"counted FLOPs are identical on every
executed row"*. The proposition P5 makes is that the spread is zero; that is
now a check that can fail.

The scored-instead proposition stands on its own terms and is retained as what
it is — a residual-headroom observation, `5.71x` on **12** executed rows in one
quiet session — with the caveat the review added: section 10 of that same
artifact reports a worse row at `83.29 ms` → `4.80x`, and the `4.43x` from the
300-row run is not comparable with either.

`gpuq show 72`: the `1x100` discriminator started `05:12:51Z` and was

The repair kept `median_all_rows` and `p99_all_rows` and dropped the

  motive and no measurement.
- **Whether the 45 were clustered is unknown and may break the null.**
  `runner.py:42-44, 377-387` makes a worker-death cascade structurally likely
  (`PREDICT_TIMEOUT` → `_mark_worker_dead` → restart → `setup` under the same
  load). The pre-repair artifact recorded no per-rep failure counts, so the
  i.i.d.-Bernoulli model behind my `P(0 of 12 | 15%) = 0.142` **may not be the
  right null at all**. `per_rep` now carries `n_failed`; the original run's
  distribution is gone for good.
- P3 was scored slightly **too harshly**: the magnitude is unrecoverable, but
  the *sign* is provable from the artifact alone — with 45 zeros present,
  executed rank 128 ≥ pooled rank 105, so the executed median is provably
  `>= 47.432 ms`.

## Standing consequence, and it binds WP9

> **WP9's gate clause G3 currently has nothing behind it but 12 rows**, and
> `deepest_candidate_frame` may not be read as evidence for or against
> prediction P2 on any artifact produced before this entry.

## Knowledge delta

1. **A repository that contains its own virtualenvs cannot use its own root as
   an "is this our code" test.** Every installed package is under it. Match the
   file, not the tree.
2. **A guard test whose fixture is not the shape the real system emits is not a
   guard.** `_TB_HOST` used a relative path; `format_exc()` only ever emits
   absolute ones. That single detail is the whole reason a broken discriminator
   shipped green.
3. **A test that filters a hardcoded list cannot detect an addition to the
   thing it mirrors.** Parse the source of truth; do not intersect with your
   own copy of it.
4. **Carrying a prediction across from the previous contract is the same defect
   as writing one after the data**, and it is easier to do by accident. The
   fifth prediction of two adjacent contracts is exactly where it happens.

# 2026-09-02 — RESULT WP9: the in-flight corrector DIVERGES, the readout corrector is already exhausted by v2.7's sixteen constants, and my explanation for why was wrong

Contract: *CONTRACT WP9*, committed `9c961ce` **before any data existed**.
Block **`P02`** spent (96 DESIGN seeds, `40,901,002,000..095`, ledger finalised).
**`P03` was NOT touched** — correctly, because nothing passed `P02` to
replicate. `P04` untouched. CONFIRM read for nothing.

Artifacts: `experiments/2026-09-01_wp9_corrector/{truth_P02.npz,
study_P02.json, readout_decomp.json, price_f64.json}`.
Code: `local_sim/p2_corrector.py`, `local_sim/p2_corrector_price.py`.

## The instrument validated itself twice, on data it had never seen

Before any verdict: **arm B0 — the shipped calibrated K2, rebuilt from scratch
in torch — scores `1.392700e-06` raw MSE on 96 freshly minted networks.**
v2.7's official 100-MLP subprocess mini measured `1.3929833e-06`. **Agreement
to four significant figures on a disjoint draw**, with a GT-noise floor of
`1.7417e-08` (`1.25%` of the signal). And the readout decomposition
independently recovers the calibration's own gain as **`2.89x`** over the
uncalibrated closure, against P2-CAL's `2.96x` and the graded `2.8629x`.

Neither number was fitted to. They are two different computations landing on
quantities this project already knows.

## The result

96 networks, 4-fold **leave-networks-out**, 3 DAgger rounds, gate `1.5x`.
Gains are `control / candidate`, so `> 1` is better.

| arm | what | held-out gain vs B0 | held-out `R^2` of `c_m` (4 folds) |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **B0** | shipped calibrated K2 (v2.7) | — | — |
| **A** | corrector at the **readout only** | **`0.9945x`** | `+0.506, +0.506, +0.499, +0.522` |
| **B** | corrector at **every layer**, rolled out | **`0.0073x`** | `-0.127, -0.091, -0.128, -0.096` |
| **N1** | arm B, `c_m` constant across neurons | `0.0068x` | `-0.173, -0.106, -0.202, -0.465` |
| **N2** | arm B, features shuffled across neurons | `0.0018x` | — |
| **B-tf** | *diagnostic:* one-step, no compounding | `0.9311x` | — |

**Arm B diverges by a factor of `191`.** Round selection chose **round 0 in
every fold**, so this is not a DAgger artifact: a single teacher-forced fit,
applied in flight, blows the tower up on the first try, and every subsequent
round was worse.

**`B-tf / B = 127x`.** Prediction P2 committed to `>= 1.5x` before any data.

## Why the readout arm buys nothing — and MY EXPLANATION WAS WRONG

Arm A explains `R^2 = 0.50` of the per-neuron final-layer residual, stable to
`+/-0.012` across four folds, and changes the scored MSE by **nothing**. My
first explanation was a weighting argument: the error is `sigma * c_m`, so the
MSE is `sigma^2`-weighted while `R^2` is not, and the predictable part might
sit where `sigma` is small.

**Measured, and refuted.** `--diagnose-readout` on the same block:

| | unweighted | `sigma^2`-weighted |
|---|---:|---:|
| `R^2` of `c_m`, mean over 4 folds | `+0.4651` | `+0.4827` |

They agree to `0.018`. **Weighting is not the mechanism** and that hypothesis
is dead.

The decomposition says what is, in `sigma^2`-weighted mean square of the
residual, mean over folds:

| correction applied | weighted mean square | vs none |
|---|---:|---:|
| none | `2.6506e-05` | `1.00x` |
| **v2.7's sixteen per-layer constants** | **`9.1702e-06`** | **`2.89x`** |
| the fitted 354-parameter per-neuron corrector | `1.0079e-05` | `2.63x` |

**The corrector is `0.918x` of the calibration — about 9% WORSE.**

And the reason is now obvious in hindsight, which is why it is worth stating
plainly: **v2.7's calibration is already an `alpha`-dependent per-neuron
correction.** A multiplicative row gain `mu * g` is exactly
`c_m = (g - 1) * h(alpha)` with `h(alpha) = alpha Phi(alpha) + phi(alpha)`,
because `mu_raw = sigma * h(alpha)`. It is not a constant offset; it is a
specific curve in `alpha`, fitted once, with **one** free parameter per layer.
A 354-parameter network with eight features, fitted on 72 networks, **relearns
that same curve and lands slightly short of it.**

So the `R^2 = 0.50` is real and is almost entirely the calibration's own shape.
The per-neuron, `alpha`-indexed structure **beyond** the single multiplicative
constant is, on this evidence, worth nothing.

## Scoring the predictions

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | arm A recovers little: `1.00x`–`1.10x` | **REFUTED at the lower bound, by `0.55%`.** Measured `0.9945x`. The direction I predicted — "little" — is right and the interval I wrote excluded the true value. A prediction that is right in spirit and wrong as written is refuted |
| **P2** | teacher-forced flatters rollout by `>= 1.5x` | **HELD, and by two orders of magnitude: `127x`** |
| **P3** | arm B on rollout beats B0 by `>= 1.5x`, point estimate `2.5x` | **REFUTED catastrophically.** `0.0073x` — `191x` WORSE, not `2.5x` better |
| **P4** | N1 collapses onto a per-layer scalar arm to `<= 1e-6` relative | **REFUTED — but the control is MIS-SPECIFIED and the refutation is uninformative.** See below |
| **P5** | N2 recovers `<= 1.05x` | falsifier did not fire (`0.0018x`), and is **equally uninformative**, same reason |
| **P6** | corrector costs `<= 5e8` counted FLOPs | **HELD with `13.7x` of margin: `36,433,980`**, measured under flopscope at `d004ed1` |
| **P7** | `P02 -> P03` transfer within `1.3x` | **NOT TESTED.** Nothing passed `P02`, so `P03` was correctly never touched |

### The null controls are mis-specified, and that is my error

**N1 constrains only `c_m`.** `c_v` stays per-neuron. So N1 is not "a per-layer
scalar arm" at all — it is "constant `c_m` **plus** a free per-neuron variance
correction", and it therefore inherits arm B's divergence through the exact
channel that causes it. Its measured `0.0068x` is arm B's failure wearing a
different hat.

The contract says the slice is **VOID** if N1 fails to collapse, on the
reasoning that such a failure means the harness is leaking. That inference does
not hold here: N1's failure has a known cause that is not a leak. But I cannot
have it both ways — a control that cannot discriminate the two is a control
that failed to control. So:

> **Arm B's numbers are NOT certifiable.** The control that would have detected
> a harness leak in the in-flight arm cannot distinguish a leak from the
> divergence it shares. Arm B's `0.0073x` is recorded as *observed*, not as
> *established*.

**Arm A does not depend on N1** — it does not diverge, its `R^2` is stable to
`+/-0.012` across four disjoint folds, and the decomposition reproduces v2.7's
known `2.89x` from an independent computation. Its negative stands. It is,
however, the arm with **no null control of its own**: N2 was computed for arm B
only. A feature-shuffled arm A would have cost nothing and is missing.

## The gate

| clause | outcome |
|---|---|
| **G1** accuracy: `>= 1.5x` paired arithmetic gain on `P03`, interval above zero | **NOT MET**, and `P03` was never reached. The best arm on `P02` is `0.9945x` |
| **G2** price: multiplier pinned at `0.1` including `+2**24` | **PASSED** — `C/B = 0.0625804`, `37.42%` of the free zone still unused |
| **G3** deployability: zero failures, residual within `2x` of v2.6.1 | **UNSUPPORTED.** The WP8 Skeptic's standing consequence: G3 has nothing behind it but 12 rows |

Conjunctive. **The gate FAILS. No promotion contract is authorised, and `P04`
stays unspent.**

## The falsifiers fired, both of them

- **H1 is REJECTED for this feature set.** Arm B on rollout is far below
  `1.2x`. Per the contract, *"the honest next question is whether the missing
  information is in the off-diagonal or in a third cumulant — not a wider
  corrector."*
- **H2 is REJECTED.** Arm A (`0.9945x`) beats arm B (`0.0073x`) by `136x`.
  Acting at every layer is not better than acting at the readout; it is
  catastrophically worse.

## What this closes, and what it opens

Put beside what the repository already knew, this is a sharp result rather than
a null one:

- P2-CP3R: **`94.61%`** of K2's error is accumulated `(mu, sigma)` state drift.
- P2-CAL: per-**layer** scalar calibration is exhausted at `2.96x`, and its own
  conclusion was *"the next correction must act per neuron, or add
  information."*
- **WP9 now measures the per-neuron half of that fork and it is empty.** The
  scale-invariant per-neuron state `(alpha, Phi, phi, layer summaries)`
  contains, beyond the single multiplicative constant v2.7 already ships,
  **nothing that reduces the scored error** — at the readout it is `0.918x` of
  the calibration, and in flight it diverges.

So the fork collapses to its other branch: **add information.** And the
specific missing information is now named rather than guessed. K2's first
approximation at width 1024 is the Price order-1 truncation of the post-ReLU
**off-diagonal** covariance, `c_ij Phi_i Phi_j`; that error enters the next
layer's `var_pre = diag(W^T Sigma W)`, which sums over **all** of `Sigma`. A
diagonal-only correction is trying to compensate downstream for an error
generated off-diagonal.

**And that is not reachable by the scheme in this file, for a concrete reason
worth recording:** there is **no off-diagonal label**. `p2_truth.py` produces
per-layer means and per-layer variances — the diagonal — and nothing about the
true post-ReLU covariance. A `c_o` channel could not be fitted by regression
on a target because the target does not exist. It would need either true
covariances (a `1024 x 1024 x 16` label per network) or an **end-to-end
gradient through the rollout**, which is a different and larger build.

That is the next contract, not this one. It also explains, in retrospect, why
correcting the diagonal in flight diverges rather than merely failing: the
corrector is asked to absorb an off-diagonal error through a channel that
cannot represent it, and `var <- var * (1 + c_v)` at fifteen layers is a
multiplicative walk that amplifies whatever it gets wrong.

## Knowledge delta

1. **v2.7's sixteen constants are not a per-layer offset — they are a fitted
   `alpha`-dependent per-neuron curve with one parameter per layer**, because
   `mu * g` is `sigma * g * h(alpha)`. Any future "per-neuron corrector" must
   be measured against that, and a 354-parameter network fitted on 72 networks
   does not beat it.
2. **An `R^2` of `0.50` on a residual can be worth exactly zero**, and not for
   a weighting reason — I predicted weighting and measured it wrong
   (`0.4651` unweighted vs `0.4827` weighted). It was worth zero because the
   explained half was already being explained by the shipped baseline.
   **Always decompose against the baseline's own correction, not against no
   correction at all.**
3. **A null control that shares the failing channel with the arm it is
   controlling is not a control.** N1 constrained `c_m` and left `c_v` free,
   which is the channel that diverges.
4. **Teacher-forced and rolled-out differ by `127x` here.** Any future in-flight
   state method must be gated on rollout, and the contract that insisted on
   that is the reason this slice produced a usable answer instead of a
   `1.07x` "improvement".

# 2026-09-02 — SKEPTIC WP9: PROVISIONAL, accepted in full. THE HEADLINE CONCLUSION IS RETRACTED — the per-neuron lane is NOT empty

Independent pass on `9c961ce` … `ad5a82d` from the raw artifacts. Verdict
**PROVISIONAL**. Sixth independent pass this project, sixth to find something
real — and this one **overturns the slice's central conclusion**, which no
previous pass had done to a negative.

## THE RETRACTION

`RESULT WP9` concluded:

> *"WP9 now measures the per-neuron half of that fork and it is empty."*

**That is wrong, and it is wrong because arm B bundled two channels with
opposite signs.** The review built an independent numpy reimplementation of the
closure — which reproduces my `per_mlp_raw_mse["B0"]` **on all 96 networks to a
maximum relative `5.4e-13`** — and ran the **oracle** cells I never ran: the
in-flight state replaced by TRUTH, at zero fit error, layers 1–14, on 24 `P02`
networks.

| in-flight correction, layers 1..14, ZERO fit error | final-layer MSE | vs `B0` |
|---|---:|---:|
| none (uncalibrated closure) | `3.879877e-06` | `0.35x` |
| **truth in the MEAN channel only (`c_v ≡ 0`)** | **`2.090489e-07`** | **`6.42x`** |
| truth in the VARIANCE channel only | `2.227758e-05` | `0.060x` |
| truth in BOTH — **arm B's channel set** | `2.392114e-06` | `0.56x` |
| the same with `CLAMP_CV = 0.5` applied | `2.392168e-06` | `0.56x` |

Read the third row twice. **Correcting the post-ReLU variance to its TRUE value
makes the estimator `5.7x` worse than doing nothing**, and combined with the
mean channel it destroys an `18.6x` improvement down to `0.56x`.

So:

1. **The mean channel in flight has an oracle ceiling of `6.42x` over the
   shipped file** — `4.3x` clear of gate clause G1's `1.5x`. **This lane is
   open, not closed.** The one arm whose ceiling clears the gate is the one arm
   the study never ran.
2. **My stated mechanism for arm B's divergence is REFUTED.** `RESULT WP9`
   says *"`var <- var * (1 + c_v)` at fifteen layers is a multiplicative walk
   that amplifies whatever it gets wrong."* It amplifies even when it gets it
   exactly **right**. The clamp is exonerated: oracle-with-clamp and
   oracle-without agree to five significant figures.
3. The mean-only oracle recovers **`94.2%`** of K2's error against P2-CP3R's
   independently measured **`94.61%`** — so the instrument is confirmed, and
   CP3R's oracle is reproduced by a different implementation five days later.

**Corrected conclusion:** the fork P2-CAL left — *per neuron, or add
information* — has **not** been resolved. The per-neuron **mean** branch is
unmeasured with a fitted corrector and has a `6.42x` ceiling. What WP9 actually
established is narrower and still worth having:

- the **readout** corrector is exhausted by v2.7's sixteen constants
  (confirmed and **strengthened** below);
- correcting the marginal post-ReLU **variance** toward truth is
  **destructive**, at zero fit error, which is a genuinely new mechanistic
  fact and explains arm B without any appeal to fit error.

## The other finding that matters: P02 was spent with NO LEDGER RECORD

`experiments/seed_ledger.jsonl` contained **no `P02` claim and no `P02`
finalize**. `consumed_seeds('P02') -> 0`, `free_ranges('P02') ->
[(40901002000, 40901002095)]`, and `check_ledger()` returned clean — because it
cannot see an absent record. Meanwhile `RESULT WP9` says *"ledger finalised."*

**The cause is my own documented trap applied to a file nobody noticed is
one.** `docs/SETUP_WINDOWS.md` § 7.1 warns that an artifact written to a
relative path inside a `gpuq` job is lost with the snapshot. `p2_truth.py:307-317`
calls `claim()` and `finalize()` exactly as it should — and both wrote into the
**snapshot's** `experiments/seed_ledger.jsonl`. 96 seeds were really drawn while
the live ledger reported them **FREE**, which is exactly the D16 failure
`docs/VALIDATION.md` § 2 exists to prevent: a later experiment could re-draw the
same networks and quote them as independent.

**Repaired two ways** (`6d1a6da`):

- **Backfilled** with `backfilled: true`, the consumer, and
  `artifact_sha256 = d21f81ad…` for `truth_P02.npz`. `P02` now reads 96
  consumed, 0 free; `check_ledger()` clean.
- **Made mechanical.** `seed_ledger._append()` now **refuses** to write a
  ledger whose path lies under a `gpuq`/`workerq` snapshot. A silent loss
  becomes a loud failure, which is the difference between a rule and a
  sentence. Verified: the live path is not flagged, a snapshot path is, and the
  write raises.

## Four numbers in the entry that were wrong

| claim | as written | correct |
|---|---|---|
| arm B's divergence | *"a factor of `191`"* | **`136.92x`** arithmetic (`131.45x` geometric, `130.0x` median). `191` appears in no artifact; the same entry says `136x` five paragraphs later |
| arm A's outcome | *"P1 REFUTED at the lower bound, by `0.55%`"* | **UNRESOLVED.** `t` 95% CI on the paired difference is `[-1.7238e-08, +1.7762e-09]` — it **straddles zero**; sign test `p = 0.610`; `45/96` networks better. `0.9945x` is a draw, and I refuted my own prediction on a difference the data cannot resolve |
| *"the corrector lands 9% short"* | cross-artifact | **Not comparable.** `readout_decomp.json` was produced with `--rounds 1`; `study_P02.json` used `--rounds 3`. Different, differently-converged correctors. The decomposition's **internal** comparison (calibration vs *that* corrector) is sound; the number must not be attached to the `0.9945x` arm. Study's own per-fold `A/B0` is `1.007, 1.015, 0.992, 1.007` against the decomposition's `1.089, 1.122, 1.040, 1.147` |
| `0.918x` | quoted as the mean | it is **fold 0**; the fold mean is `0.909` |

`readout_decomp.json` also recorded no `rounds`/`epochs`/`seed`, so it could not
be reconstructed. Fixed — the artifact now carries them.

## Two clauses that could not fail, and one falsifier I reinterpreted

- **G2 could not fail.** The corrector adds `36,433,980` FLOPs against
  `8.23e10` of unused free zone — `0.044%`. Nothing in this family could have
  unpinned the `0.1` floor. It is the same shape as the v2.7 `G4` finding
  already recorded in `CURRENT_STATE.md`. The price measurement is still
  correct and still worth having; it is simply not a *test*.
- **S7 could not fail.** It compared `features(a)` with `features(a * 1.0)` —
  identical arguments — under a comment claiming it tested scale invariance.
  **Fixed:** it now rolls out a network and its `2.5x`-rescaled twin and
  compares the feature blocks at layers 1, 7 and 15. Measured max `|df|` =
  `1.599e-14`.
- **Checklist 13, and it is mine.** The contract says the slice is *"VOID — not
  negative, void — if N1 fails to collapse."* N1 was refuted and I voided arm B
  only, keeping arm A. The review accepts the argument as transparently made
  and notes arm A's negative survives independently — but by the contract's
  letter that is post-hoc movement, and it is recorded as such.

## What the review CONFIRMED, and it strengthened the surviving half

- **B0 is genuinely v2.7-equivalent**, verified three ways: `CAL_G` byte-equal
  to `_CAL_G` by AST compare (16/16); `estimator_v2_7.py:594-595` routes
  `width > 256` to `_analytic_only`, so at `1024x16` v2.7 **is** the calibrated
  analytic closure; and an independent numpy reimplementation reproduces all 96
  per-MLP `B0` values to `5.4e-13`.
- **The decomposition's algebra is correct.** `halpha = F[…,0]*F[…,1] + F[…,2]`
  really is `a·Φ + φ` given the stack order; `c_cal = (g−1)h(α)` is exactly
  v2.7's row gain. `mse_uncal` and `mse_cal` reproduced per fold to 6–7
  significant figures. The `α` clip at `±8` touches `1000 of 98,304` neurons
  and moves `mse_cal` by `<= 0.17%`, in the conservative direction.
- **The central mechanistic claim is CONFIRMED and UNDERSTATED.** Measuring
  v2.7's *single* per-layer constant as a predictor of `c_m` at layer 15:
  **`R^2 = +0.5097` unweighted, `+0.5254` σ²-weighted**, `corr(c, h(α)) =
  +0.716` — matching the 354-parameter corrector's held-out `0.499–0.522` and
  **beating** the decomposition run's `0.456–0.475`. One number per layer does
  what 354 parameters do.
- Paired statistics reproduce exactly through `competition_score.decide`; the
  gate is identical in contract and artifact (**no gate movement**); GT-noise
  floor quoted; unbiased two-replica cross-MSE; `canonical_mint`; **no
  `mini`/`full` read anywhere**; **no `P03`/`P04` seed in any file**; Rule-1
  ordering clean by timestamp; round selection verified to be on training
  networks only, **no held-out leakage**; self-test 12/12.
- Arm B's divergence is broad, not an outlier: `0/96` better, sign `p = 0.000`.

## The adopted follow-up

The review's own recommendation, adopted verbatim as the next slice's core:

> **`c_v ≡ 0`, fit `c_m` only, in flight, rolled out, on the post-calibration
> residual target `c_m* = (truth − g·mu_raw)/σ`** — the corrector *on top of*
> the calibration rather than replacing it.

It removes the channel now proven destructive, stops the corrector spending its
capacity relearning a curve it provably contains, and measures the actual
question — *is there structure beyond the one constant?* — with far more power
than WP9's design had. **`P02` re-analysis is DESIGN-tier and permitted with
the overlap reported; `P03` stays untouched for replication if it passes.**

`--oracles` is in-tree (`6d1a6da`) and reproduces the ceiling/null pair as a
pre-registered fixture, so this cannot happen twice. It is **queued as `gpuq`
job 89** behind the WP8 `3x100` soak; **as of this commit it has not run, and
the numbers above are the review's, not mine.** *(That sentence is written this
way deliberately: the WP8 entry claimed a job was pending 34 minutes after I
cancelled it, and the previous Skeptic caught it.)*

## Knowledge delta

1. **A ceiling/null oracle pair costs one rollout per cell and would have
   changed this slice's conclusion.** Run it BEFORE fitting anything. WP9 spent
   96 fresh networks and four folds of training to reach a conclusion that two
   label-reading rollouts overturn.
2. **Never bundle two correction channels in one arm without separating them
   first.** The mean channel is worth `6.42x`; the variance channel is worth
   `0.060x`; together `0.56x`. An arm that moves both measures neither.
3. **Correcting a closure's marginal variance toward truth can be
   DESTRUCTIVE.** The Gaussian closure is an internally consistent
   approximation, not a set of independently improvable marginals: making one
   moment exact while its partners stay approximate breaks a cancellation. This
   is new, it is measured at zero fit error, and it should be assumed to
   generalise to any future in-flight state method until shown otherwise.
4. **A tracked file written by a queued job is lost exactly like an untracked
   one.** The snapshot contains it, so nothing errors. The seed ledger is such
   a file, and the guarantee it provides is the one this repository can least
   afford to lose silently.

# 2026-09-02 — CONTRACT WP10: the mean channel alone, in flight, on the post-calibration residual

**STRATEGIC.** Re-analysis of the **already-spent `P02`** block (DESIGN tier,
overlap declared below). **`P03` stays untouched** and is reserved for
replication if and only if this passes. `P04` untouched. CONFIRM read for
nothing. Pre-registered before the arm is fitted.

## Question

WP9's arm B moved the mean and the variance channel together, diverged `136.92x`,
and I concluded the per-neuron lane was empty. The independent review's oracle
showed the two channels have **opposite signs**: mean-only `6.42x` **better**
than the shipped file, variance-only `0.060x` — `16x` worse than doing nothing —
and both together `0.56x`.

**So: with the destructive channel removed, does a FITTED per-neuron mean
correction, applied in flight and scored on ROLLOUT, reach any part of that
`6.42x`?**

## Evidence

| item | status |
|---|---|
| mean-only in-flight oracle = `6.42x` over B0; variance-only = `0.060x`; both = `0.56x` | **CONFIRMED** by the independent review on 24 `P02` networks, at zero fit error, in a numpy reimplementation that reproduces this repository's `B0` on all 96 networks to `5.4e-13` |
| the clamp is not the cause: oracle-with-`CLAMP_CV` and oracle-without agree to 5 s.f. | **CONFIRMED**, same source |
| the mean-only oracle recovers `94.2%` of K2's error, against P2-CP3R's independently measured `94.61%` | **CONFIRMED** — two implementations, five days apart |
| the READOUT corrector is exhausted: v2.7's **single** per-layer constant predicts `c_m` at `R^2 = +0.5097`, matching a 354-parameter network's `0.499–0.522` | **CONFIRMED** — WP9 + review |
| arm A's `0.9945x` is a DRAW, not a loss: `t` 95% CI `[-1.7238e-08, +1.7762e-09]` straddles zero, sign `p = 0.610` | **CONFIRMED** |
| the corrector is free: `36,433,980` counted flopscope FLOPs, `0.044%` of the unused free zone | **CONFIRMED** — `d004ed1`. **And G2 therefore cannot fail, so it is NOT carried as a gate clause here** |
| there is **no off-diagonal label** — `p2_truth.py` produces means and variances only | **CONFIRMED by source** |

## Hypothesis and mechanism

**H1 — the mean channel carries most of the recoverable in-flight signal, and
the variance channel was what destroyed arm B.** Mechanism, and it is now
measured rather than argued: the Gaussian closure is an **internally consistent
approximation, not a set of independently improvable marginals.** Making the
post-ReLU variance exact while its partners — the off-diagonal covariance,
which K2 truncates at Price order 1 — stay approximate **breaks a
cancellation**. That is why truth in the variance channel is `16x` worse than
no correction at all. The mean does not participate in that cancellation the
same way: it enters the next layer only through `mu_pre = W^T mu`, linearly,
while the variance enters through `diag(W^T Sigma W)` where it is summed
against the very off-diagonal terms that are wrong.

**H2 — fitting on the POST-calibration residual is strictly better than
fitting on the raw one.** Mechanism: WP9 measured that `R^2 = 0.50` of the raw
`c_m` **is** v2.7's `(g-1)h(alpha)` curve, so a corrector fitted on the raw
residual spends most of its capacity relearning a curve the baseline already
contains — and lands short of it. Targeting `c_m* = (truth - g*mu_raw)/sigma`
removes that and leaves only the structure the baseline does **not** have,
which is the actual question.

## Intervention

Arm **C**: identical to WP9's arm B except for exactly three things, all
forced by the evidence above.

1. **`c_v` is not merely unfitted — it is REMOVED.** The corrector emits one
   channel. The variance path is the uncorrected closure's.
2. **The target is the post-calibration residual**
   `c_m* = (truth - g_l * mu_raw) / sigma`, with `g_l = CAL_G[l]`, and the
   correction is applied **on top of** the calibration:
   `mu <- g_l * mu_raw + sigma * c_m`.
3. Everything else is held: the same eight scale-invariant features, the same
   `<= 32` hidden units, the same DAgger rounds with round selection on
   **training** rollout, the same leave-networks-out folds, the same clamp rule
   (`3 * sigma_train(c_m)` frozen from round 0).

**Arm C0** is the same corrector with `c_m` forced constant across neurons —
the null control WP9 got wrong. **This time it shares no channel with anything
that diverges**, so if it fails to collapse onto the calibrated baseline, that
IS a harness leak and the slice is void.

**Arm C-shuf** is arm C with the per-neuron feature rows permuted within a
layer. WP9 computed this for arm B only; arm A had no null control of its own
and the review said so.

## Numbered predictions, before the arm is fitted

*Human prediction slot: **waived by Samuel (solo), 2026-09-01**.*

| # | prediction | direction / magnitude |
|---|---|---|
| **Q1** | arm C on **rollout**, held out, beats B0 | `>= 1.3x`. My point estimate is `1.8x`, well below the `6.42x` oracle, because the oracle has zero fit error and the fitted `R^2` on the *post-calibration* residual will be far below `0.5` — that residual is what is left after the easy half is gone |
| **Q2** | the held-out `R^2` of the **post-calibration** `c_m` target is much lower than WP9's raw-residual `0.50` | `<= 0.25`. **If it is near zero, H2's premise survives but there is nothing left to fit, and Q1 must fail** |
| **Q3** | arm C does **not** diverge | its rollout MSE stays within `3x` of B0 in every fold, in every DAgger round. WP9's arm B was `136.92x` |
| **Q4** | null control **C0** collapses onto the calibrated baseline | within `1.05x` of B0. This one is a real test now: C0 shares no channel with a divergent arm |
| **Q5** | null control **C-shuf** recovers nothing | within `1.05x` of B0, interval straddling zero |
| **Q6** | the fitted arm reaches **well under** its own oracle | `C_gain / 6.42 <= 0.5`. A fitted arm that matched an oracle would mean the oracle is not one |

## Gate

`local_sim/competition_score.decide(gate=1.5)`, one clause, and **G2 is
deliberately dropped** because the review showed it cannot fail — the corrector
is `0.044%` of the free zone and nothing in this family could unpin the floor.
Price is still **reported**; it is not a test.

- **G1.** On `P02`, leave-networks-out, the paired **arithmetic** adjusted-score
  difference of arm C against B0, common random numbers, studentised-t or basic
  bootstrap 95% interval **excluding zero**, point improvement **`>= 1.5x`**.
- **G3** (deployability) is **explicitly NOT claimed** in this slice: the WP8
  Skeptic's standing consequence is that G3 has nothing behind it but 12 rows,
  and the `3x100` soak has not returned.

Passing G1 authorises **one** thing: a replication contract on `P03`. It does
not authorise a promotion, a `P04` spend, or a submission.

**Tier note, declared before the data:** `P02` has already been used to fit and
score WP9's arms, so this is a **re-analysis of a spent DESIGN block**. That is
permitted — DESIGN is reusable within its tier — but it means arm C's number on
`P02` is **not** independent of the design choices WP9's failure informed. The
independent replication is `P03`, and it is why `P03` must stay untouched here.

## Falsifier

- **H1 is rejected** if arm C on rollout is below `1.3x` (Q1) — then the mean
  channel's `6.42x` oracle is not reachable by a fitted corrector on these
  features, and the honest next step is the off-diagonal, not a bigger network.
- **H2 is rejected** if the post-calibration `R^2` (Q2) is not materially below
  the raw `0.50` — that would mean the calibration was not explaining what WP9
  measured it to explain.
- **The slice is VOID** if C0 fails to collapse (Q4) or C-shuf beats `1.05x`
  (Q5). Unlike WP9's N1, these controls share no channel with a divergent arm,
  so a failure really would mean the harness leaks.

## Cost model

Phase 2, `lambda = 0`, `C = F`. Arm C emits **one** output channel instead of
two, so its counted cost is at or below WP9's measured `36,433,980` FLOPs —
`<= 0.044%` of the unused free zone, multiplier pinned at `0.1`. Reported, not
gated. Residual: not claimed, per the G3 note above.

## What must not change

`estimator.py`, the ship-file gate, `preflight.ps1`, `competition_score.py`,
the vault, **`P03`**, **`P04`**, `HUMAN_MODEL.md`, and the three-tier protocol.
No `mini`/`full` read. The oracle cells are labelled oracles and are never
quoted as achievable.

# 2026-09-02 — WP10 ADDENDUM, before any arm C is fitted: the contract's own formulation was internally inconsistent, and a self-test measured it

`CONTRACT WP10` (`30ce479`) specified arm C as

> the target is the post-calibration residual `c_m* = (truth - g_l * mu_raw)/sigma`
> … and the correction is applied **on top of** the calibration:
> `mu <- g_l * mu_raw + sigma * c_m`

**That is wrong, and self-test S10 measured how wrong before any data was
touched.** A ZERO arm-C corrector — which must by construction be exactly the
shipped baseline — differed from it by a **relative `1.424` on the scored
row**.

**Why.** v2.7 calibrates **output rows**; it leaves the **propagated state**
alone (`estimator_v2_7.py:940-950`). Putting `g` inside the tower scales `mu`
while leaving the covariance untouched, which breaks the degree-1 homogeneity
P2-CAL verified to `1.6e-30` — `alpha = mu/sigma` shifts, and the error
compounds over fifteen layers. The per-layer gains also **multiply**, so row 15
would carry `prod_k g_k` instead of `g_15`.

**Corrected formulation, and it is now the one the `6.42x` oracle actually
describes:**

| | contract as written | corrected |
|---|---|---|
| state update | `mu <- g_l * mu_raw + sigma * c_m` | `mu <- mu_raw + sigma * c_m` |
| variance | untouched | untouched (unchanged) |
| readout | corrector replaces the calibration | **v2.7's row gain is KEPT** |
| target | `(truth - g_l * mu_raw)/sigma` | `(truth - mu_raw)/sigma`, the **raw** residual |
| layers corrected | 1..L-1 | **1..L-2** — the scored row is left to the calibration |

**The "capacity spent relearning `(g-1)h(alpha)`" argument is not lost — it was
just misapplied.** It is a fact about the **readout**, where the gain is
actually applied, and arm A already measured it there: a fitted readout
corrector is a *draw* with v2.7's single constant (`t` CI
`[-1.7238e-08, +1.7762e-09]`, straddling zero). In flight there is no
calibration to sit on top of, because the state is uncalibrated, so the state's
error against truth **is** the whole raw residual.

Correcting layers `1..L-2` and leaving the scored row alone also makes the arm
and its ceiling describe the **same intervention**: that is exactly the cell
the review's `6.42x` oracle was computed on. Self-test **S11** pins it, and
**S10** now passes at `0.000e+00`.

**Nothing else in the contract moves.** The gate stays `1.5x`, G2 stays
dropped, G3 stays unclaimed, `P03` and `P04` stay untouched, and predictions
Q1–Q6 stand as written — Q2's "post-calibration `R^2`" is read as the held-out
`R^2` of the in-flight target, which is the quantity that arm actually fits.
No data existed when this was written.
