# 2026-09-02 — SKEPTIC WP14-FOLLOWUP: **CLAIM A PROVISIONAL, CLAIM B PROVISIONAL**. Accepted in full.

Ninth independent pass; ninth to find something real, and the first to find that
**the axis I measured was not the axis that decides.** Every finding below was
re-verified in-tree before acceptance. Verdict and repairs; the raw probe paths
are named per finding.

## THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: λ = 0 MAKES FLOPs FREE, AND I MEASURED THE FREE ONE

> **The flow issues ~5,300 flopscope operations per MLP against the shipped K2
> closure's 453, and its local in-process residual read `0.29`–`0.44 s` against
> the `0.4 s` per-MLP cliff — over the cliff on 2 of 6 readings.**

`docs/GOTCHAS.md` already states the mechanism, and I read past it: *"residual
risk scales with op count and Python glue, not with FLOPs."* Under `λ = 0` a FLOP
below the floor costs **nothing**; a residual excursion does not cost score
either — **it fails the MLP and zeroes the prediction**, turning a `1e-7` row into
a `~0.92` row. So *"the composed cost floor survives execution"* is **true of
counted FLOPs and unestablished of execution**, which is the same sentence
`SKEPTIC WP14` wrote about the projection, one axis over. The review's own
control makes the number transferable: the ratio K3/K2 is `10`–`16x` on residual
and `~11.6x` on operation count, measured in the same process on the same host.

`local_sim/p2_k3_fnp.py --flow-price` now measures FLOPs, **operation count** and
residual against a matched K2 control in one run, and refuses to quote the
absolute second (`AGENTS.md`: the authority is `--runner subprocess`).

**This is upstream of every WP15 gate.** A flow that fails MLPs makes `G-M-E2E`
and `G-L-E2E` unmeasurable, so it is answered before either arm runs.

## CLAIM B HAD ALMOST NO POWER, AND NOW THAT IS A NUMBER

The review ran seven targeted value-destroying mutations against `--layer-k2`.
**All seven passed all three checks identically, one of them 20% cheaper.**
Reproduced in-tree, `--mutation-coverage`,
`experiments/2026-09-02_wp14_fnp/mutation_coverage.json`:

| mutation | what it breaks | result |
|---|---|---|
| `(2,1)` slice `/3` → `/2` | the slice coefficient | **SURVIVES** |
| `2(P∘Q)Qᵀ + (Q∘Q)Pᵀ` → `3(P∘Q)Qᵀ` | a block permutation — **one matmul cheaper** | **SURVIVES** |
| `fac3`'s `w(2)` → `w(1)` | **the exact `p2_slice_cost.py` defect this module's docstring warns about** | **SURVIVES** |
| `diag(S3) + 3 S21ᵀ` → `+ 2 S21ᵀ` | the `from_dstensor` rebuild | **SURVIVES** |
| drop the `(1,1,1)` two-leg block | **the mechanism WP15 rests on** | **SURVIVES** |
| sign of the repeated-part subtraction | `S21 = K(2,1) − p111_21` | **SURVIVES** |
| `D3` → `0.5 D3` | the `(3,)` slice | **SURVIVES** |

**0 of 7 killed.** The reason is structural: at `M = 0`, `P = Wᵀ M = 0`, so `D3`
and `D21` are identically zero, **the two `(2,1)`-slice matmuls execute on
zeros**, and `S21`'s diagonal is zero so `diag(M_out) = S3` and the whole
off-diagonal of `M_out` is never read. Ten of 25 terms survive the limit and only
five are pinned; `c4_out` is printed and compared to nothing.

> **The `κ₃ = κ₄ = 0` limit exercises the cheap half and prices the expensive
> half.** So *"the price is a price OF SOMETHING"* was true of the checks that
> exist and false of the program that is priced — a **4.046**-matmul mutant
> (`0.06322 B`) passes every check the **5.047**-matmul original passes.

The gap is now a measured number that cannot quietly close or quietly widen.
Closing it still needs parity against upstream at non-zero `κ₃` — `NOT_DONE`
step 6, unchanged and still the one that can fail for an interesting reason.

## MY ACCOUNT OF THE RED GATE WAS WRONG ON ALL THREE COUNTS

Re-derived from git rather than from my say-so, by evaluating the *old* `A1`
predicate and `check_ledger` against every historical `experiments/seed_ledger.jsonl`
in the window (`scratchpad/led/`):

| commit | old `A1` | `check_ledger` errors |
|---|---|---|
| `36312c3`, `d915f83`, **`3b38796`** | **PASS** | 0 |
| **`aa01fdd`**, `bb6e65d` | FAIL | **1 — a truth artifact claimed with no hash** |
| `3084a7c` … `d0080c5` (7 more) | FAIL | 0 |

- **The window begins at `aa01fdd`, not `3b38796`.** `3b38796`'s committed ledger
  passes both checks; the claim that broke `A1` is in `aa01fdd`.
- **Step 9 was red for NINE commits, not four.**
- **Step 7's red is a different defect entirely** — `p2_truth.py` named
  `truth_P01_wp13nets.npz` and no hash was ever recorded, which is exactly the
  fail-open `SKEPTIC WP13` made us close. It lasted **two** commits and
  **self-healed** at `3084a7c` when `finalize()` was recorded.
- So **"nothing was wrong with the ledger" is false** for the first two commits
  of the window. Something was wrong, the gate said so, and it was fixed by
  accident rather than by anyone reading the gate.

`experiments/LOG.md`, `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` and `docs/GOTCHAS.md` corrected.
**I asserted a git-reconstructible fact without reconstructing it**, and the
correction makes the finding worse, not better.

## Six more, all confirmed and all repaired

1. **`P05`/`P06` could not be claimed through the sanctioned path.** `1b6ac04`
   registered them in `seed_blocks.py` and **not** in `seed_ledger.TIERS`:
   `block_span('P05')` worked, `tier_of('P05')` raised, and **WP15's first
   instrument run would have died on its first claim.** Repaired, and
   `test_seed_ledger.py` now asserts the two registries agree **in both
   directions** — reading `seed_blocks._all()` directly, with a guard against the
   fallback that would make the check compare a set with itself.
2. **No drift guard on the load-bearing coefficient table.**
   `k3_terms_simple.json` has a pinned sha256 and `--check-terms`;
   `k3_coefs_simple.json` had **neither**, and its generator wrote straight over
   the committed path. Repaired: `COEFS_SHA256` is pinned and `load_coefs()`
   refuses on drift; `p2_k3_coefs.py` refuses to overwrite without `--force` and
   gains `--check`, which re-enumerates against the live upstream checkout and
   reports drift without writing. Verified identical today.
3. **`f32/f64` is `0.5000036376`, not "exactly `0.50000`", and my inference ran
   backwards.** The excess over half is `78,848` FLOPs — *precisely* the two
   `flops.stats.*` calls, which are computed in `float64` in **both** arms and so
   are billed at rate `2.0` in both and do not halve. **A ratio slightly ABOVE
   `0.5` is the signature OF the promotion**, not proof of its absence; I quoted
   a print-rounded figure as evidence for the opposite of what it shows. The
   dtype audit — 56 arrays, 0 violations — is what actually carries that claim.
4. **Two of the three ways I called the `×16` conservative are not real.**
   Layer 0 costs `10,837,936,642`, *more* than steady state, because nothing in
   the port branches on `cov = I` or `M = 0`; and the last layer saves
   `2,098,176` FLOPs (`0.001` matmul), because `last_layer=True` skips only the
   `M` rebuild — the two `(2,1)`-slice matmuls are needed by the `(2,1)` `pK`
   terms at every layer. **Only the `off_mask` amortisation was real.** The `×16`
   is still an upper bound; it is an upper bound for one reason, not three, and
   `--flow-price` now measures the real flow instead of extrapolating it.
5. **`docs/GOTCHAS.md` carried the `5.047` price without the "values unchecked"
   caveat** that the LOG, `CURRENT_STATE.md` and the artifact all carry — and
   GOTCHAS is the file you are told to read *before quoting a number*. Repaired.
6. **The pair record loosens an invariant, and that was not stated.** It moves
   the rule from *"a deliberate overlap must be pre-declared"* to *"…must be
   acknowledged, possibly afterwards"*. `declare_pair` refuses to license an
   overlap that does not exist, but it **cannot distinguish intent from
   retroactive rationalisation** and nothing makes it. Recorded as a known
   weakening rather than presented as a strict repair. Also: `check_ledger`'s
   verbose breakdown stopped summing to its own total the moment `"pair"` became
   a third kind — fixed, with an error on any unknown kind.

## One raised and NOT a defect, recorded so it is not raised a third time

`k3_layer` hardcodes `init_scale = 2.0` at every layer where upstream's
`init_kind='he'` gives `init_scale[0] = 1.0`. **The organisers' Phase-2 MLPs are
scale 2.0 at every layer**, which is why `p2_kprop_bridge.py` (convention 3,
verified against upstream source) runs the reference with
`init_kind='manual', w_var=2.0`. For `W` with entries `~N(0, 2/n)`,
`E[W Wᵀ] = 2 I`. The note is now in the code.

## What it attacked and could not break

Almost everything. All three "lean but exact" choices were re-derived from
upstream `93d091a4` by hand and confirmed: the `(2,1)` slice's three block
permutations with `A2 == A3` and coefficient `2!·1!/3!` reproduce
`p2_k3_fnp.py:417-418` character for character; `contract_W` on an identity leg
is `Wᵀ`; and `_lap_m_dslice(2, ·, part)` returns **exactly `0.0`** for `(3,1)`,
`(2,1,1)` **and** `(1,1,1,1)` on random input while `(4,)` and `(2,2)` do not.
`_proj_coef_n_d4_r2` matches upstream at `n = 4…4096` to `≤ 3e-8` — *and the port
is the more accurate of the two*, because upstream returns float32. All **16**
Wick `(k,p)` pairs match `relu_wick_coef` to `≤ 1.3e-16`, including the
`(−1)^{k−2}` sign and the `factorial(p)·w(k−p+1,1)` reduce branch. A live
re-derivation of all four frozen tables is byte-identical. The `(1,1,1)` block
algebra is right against `factor_k3.py:371-407`, so **the mechanism `CONTRACT
WP15` rests on is correct.** And the review built the real 16-layer flow and got
`173,381,273,195 = 0.07884 B` — `25.7 M` FLOPs *below* the extrapolation, finite
output, 0 dtype violations. `62/62`, `P04` untouched, `P05`/`P06` unclaimed, no
gate moved, and the `+2**24` arithmetic checks out. WP15's disputed arithmetic is
internally consistent (`3.0` and `0.75` are both exactly `6r/n`), and `r ≤ 192`
is conservative against its own bound of `r ≤ 230`.

## Knowledge delta

1. **Under `λ = 0` the FLOP budget is not the binding constraint, and I spent a
   day measuring it.** The binding constraint is a `0.4 s` residual cliff that
   tracks operation count and Python glue. **Every future cost claim in Phase 2
   must quote counted FLOPs, operation count and residual headroom in the same
   table**, or it is measuring the free axis. `--flow-price` enforces the shape.
2. **A correctness check must be scored by what it KILLS, not by what it
   passes.** Three checks agreeing to `1e-14` looked like strong evidence and
   killed **0 of 7** targeted mutations, including one that is cheaper — so the
   checks could not certify that the measured price was the price of the intended
   algorithm. Mutation coverage is cheap and belongs beside any check that
   licenses a number.
3. **A degenerate limit is a weak test exactly where the expensive work lives.**
   Setting the high cumulants to zero made the `n³` operations run on zeros. The
   limit that makes an answer analytic is usually the limit that switches off the
   part you are trying to price.
4. **Do not assert a git-reconstructible fact without reconstructing it.** Three
   numbers in one sentence, all wrong, in a finding whose whole point was that
   prose is not evidence.

# 2026-09-02 — **THE CANARY RAN ON THE DEPLOYMENT AUTHORITY.** Zero failures, `1.21x` residual headroom, and the accuracy is `3.3x` off its own prediction

`SKEPTIC WP14-FOLLOWUP`'s named cheapest discriminating follow-up, executed
exactly as specified: wrap the flow as a candidate and read the **official**
per-MLP residual and `n_failed_mlps` from `whest run --runner subprocess`.
`gpuq` 145 (canary) and 148 (control), 20 rows of the public `v2-phase2 mini`
split, subprocess runner, same session, `--detail full --json`. Artifacts
`experiments/2026-09-02_wp15_canary/official_mini20_k3canary.json` and
`official_mini20_v261_control.json`.

**THIS IS A CONFIRM READ AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE.** The `mini` split is
read-only; **no constant was fitted, nothing was selected, no seed block was
drawn, and nothing may now be tuned against these 20 rows.** The candidate is
`estimator_wp15_k3_canary.py`; **`estimator.py` is untouched and remains v2.6.1**,
nothing was submitted, and no nomination is implied.

## The residual question is ANSWERED, and the answer is "clean, but thin"

| | counted FLOPs | `x budget` | worst residual | median | headroom vs `0.4 s` | failed MLPs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **v2.6.1 (shipped), control** | `137,600,326,656` | `0.06257` | `0.0590 s` | `0.0501 s` | **`6.78x`** | **0 / 20** |
| **K3 canary** | `173,381,273,195` | `0.07884` | `0.3314 s` | `0.2781 s` | **`1.21x`** | **0 / 20** |

> **`n_failed_mlps = 0`, `residual_wall_time_exhausted = 0`.** The flow does not
> fail MLPs on the official runner at the live shape. `SKEPTIC
> WP14-FOLLOWUP`'s worry that WP15's end-to-end gates would be unmeasurable is
> **discharged**.

**But `1.21x` is not a margin.** The standing requirement for a nomination soak
is `>= 4x` on the worst run, `VALIDATION.md` §2b-ii says a residual level is not
reproducible to better than `~2.4x` across runs on this host, and it warns that
`n = 20` is thin for a maximum. **A `1.21x` worst-case headroom over 20 rows is
inside the run-to-run spread of the cliff itself.** This candidate is not
nominable as it stands; the `~140` removable operations per layer recorded in
`p2_k3_fnp.OP_COUNT_NOTES` are now on the critical path rather than a tidy-up.

**And the local reading was OPTIMISTIC, in the direction nobody hoped.** Local
worst `0.2774 s` against official `0.3314 s`: **the grader is `1.19x` SLOWER than
this host for this file**, not faster. The two Phase-2 graded K2 reports that ran
`~7x` faster than this host are evidence about those exact files and about
nothing else — `AGENTS.md` and `GOTCHAS.md` both say so, and this is the
measurement that shows why. **The local RATIO over-predicted too**: `10.02x`
locally against `5.62x` officially, because the subprocess runner costs the small
K2 file proportionally more (`2.1x` slower official-vs-local) than the large K3
one (`1.19x`).

## The FLOP meter is EXACT against the grader, to the FLOP

`mean_effective_compute = 173,381,273,195`, identical to the local
`--flow-price` figure. `mean_compute_utilization = 0.0788446747`, matching
`0.078845`. The `+2**24` server offset does not appear at this operating point.
**Every FLOP claim made today is confirmed by the deployment authority.**

## THE ACCURACY IS `3.3x` OFF ITS OWN PREDICTION, AND THE CONTROL SAYS THAT IS THE PORT

| on the same 20 rows | raw final-layer MSE | adjusted | multiplier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v2.6.1 (shipped, uncalibrated K2p1) | `4.1805e-06` | `4.1805e-07` | `0.1` |
| **K3 canary (uncalibrated)** | **`2.8192e-06`** | **`2.8192e-07`** | `0.1` |
| ratio | **`1.483x` better** | | |

So the canary **does** beat the shipped file, by `1.483x`, measured on the
deployment authority with a matched control in the same session. That is a real
result and it is the first time this architecture has been scored by the grader
at all.

**And it is `3.3x` worse than WP14 C0-i predicted.** The regenerating flow's
drift-and-truth analysis put its raw MSE at `8.5075e-07`; the grader says
`2.8192e-06`. The control is what makes that diagnostic rather than ambiguous:

- v2.6.1 measured `4.1805e-06` here against the `4.050566e-06` this repository
  has carried for the shipped K2p1 — **`3.2%` apart.** The split, the networks
  and the instrument all transfer.
- The canary measured `3.31x` its prediction on the same split, in the same run.

> **A `3%` transfer for the control and a `3.3x` miss for the arm isolates the
> discrepancy to the K3 flow itself.** Either the `fnp` port computes a
> different function from the torch `regen` hook whose `8.5075e-07` was measured,
> or that figure does not transfer. **`NOT_DONE` step 6 — parity against upstream
> at non-zero `kappa_3` — stops being hygiene and becomes the explanation for a
> `3.3x` gap.** `SKEPTIC WP14-FOLLOWUP` named exactly this as unresolved: *"the
> priced program and the scored program have never been shown equal"*, and the
> mutation battery had already shown that no existing check could tell.

**Consequences, stated plainly:**

1. **Every adjusted-score claim resting on `8.5075e-07` is now PROVISIONAL**,
   including the `1.637x`-better-than-v2.7 paired comparison. It was a
   measurement of the torch reference, and the file the grader runs does not
   reproduce it.
2. The comparison against **v2.7** is unchanged in method and must not be
   re-derived from these 20 rows: v2.7 is *calibrated*, both files here are not,
   and a calibrated-vs-uncalibrated ratio on a read-only split is not a
   comparison this contract permits. What can be said is narrow and true: **the
   canary beats the shipped uncalibrated file by `1.483x` on 20 official rows.**
3. **Nothing may be fitted on the mini split** to close the `3.3x`. The gap is
   diagnosed against upstream, off the public data.

## Next, and it is now a short ordered list

1. **`NOT_DONE` step 6.** Run `p2_k3_fnp.k3_flow` against upstream's `regen` hook
   on the same networks at non-zero `kappa_3`, in the GPU venv. This is the
   `3.3x`.
2. **The op-count reduction** (`OP_COUNT_NOTES`, `~140` of `~333` per layer),
   then re-measure residual on the authority. `1.21x` must become `>= 4x` before
   this file is nominable, and it must not change a counted FLOP or a value --
   `--mutation-coverage` and `p2_k3_candidate_parity.py` both have to still pass
   bit for bit.
3. Only then WP15's two arms, whose gates are all end-to-end against this flow.

## Knowledge delta

1. **The deployment authority answered in seven minutes what a day of local
   measurement could not.** The residual question, the FLOP parity question and
   the accuracy-transfer question were all settled by one 20-row subprocess run
   that needed no seed block, no truth mint and no GPU.
2. **The grader is not faster. For this file it is `1.19x` slower**, and the
   local ratio to a matched control over-predicted the official ratio by `1.8x`.
   A local instrument ratio does not bound a level, and only a level clears a
   cliff — `VALIDATION.md` §2b-ii said so and this is the confirming case.
3. **A control is what turns a disappointing number into a diagnosis.** Alone,
   `2.8192e-06` against a predicted `8.5075e-07` could have been the split, the
   networks, the instrument or the port. With a control that transfers to `3%`,
   it is the port.

# 2026-09-02 — the prerequisite check the brief required before WP15 builds on `334x`: **CONFIRMED, and now carrying a caveat it did not have**

The directing brief said, in terms: *"Confirm before building on it that the
`334x` is an in-flight end-to-end oracle, not a per-layer composed figure."*
**I wrote `CONTRACT WP15` citing it as CONFIRMED evidence without running that
check.** Run now, against `experiments/2026-09-02_wp14_range/c2_e2e_oracle_rank.json`.

**It is in-flight and end-to-end.** The artifact's own `check` field reads
*"end-to-end drift with the projected residual injected in flight"*; every row
carries a per-layer `slice_probe` recording `rel_err_s3` / `rel_err_s21` at the
gated layers, which only exists because the correction is applied inside the
flow layer by layer; and the reported quantity is `drift_final_layer`, the
final-layer drift of the whole run against full K3. **It is not a composed
per-layer excess** — which matters, because the `eps^2` composed-excess model
over-predicts by `32x` and is refused as a statistic by both this contract and
`VALIDATION.md`.

**And it is 8 of 8, not a ratio of means hiding a spread:**

| statistic | value |
|---|---:|
| per-seed `none / e3svd:512` | `334, 322, 331, 373, 352, 340, 302, 320` |
| min / max | `302.4` / `373.4` |
| mean of the per-seed ratios | `334.5` |
| ratio of the means (the figure quoted) | **`333.8`** |
| the same at rank 128 | **`11.10`** |

Every network is between `302x` and `373x`. Both the `333.8x` and the `11.1x`
in `CONTRACT WP15`'s evidence table are exactly what the artifact supports.

## The caveat this check did NOT have this morning, and now must carry

**Those drifts are measured against the TORCH implementation's own full-K3
reference, inside the torch flow.** Tonight's canary showed the `fnp` port does
not reproduce the torch `regen` arm's accuracy — `2.8192e-06` officially against
a predicted `8.5075e-07`, with a matched control transferring to `3.2%`. So:

> **The `334x` oracle ceiling is a property of the torch flow. Whether it is a
> property of the flow we would ship depends on `NOT_DONE` step 6.** WP15's
> `G-M-E2E` and `G-L-E2E` are both written as end-to-end drift reductions
> against the uncorrected regenerating flow, so they remain well-posed either
> way — but the *headline* "a map is worth first place" inherits the same
> PROVISIONAL as every other claim resting on the torch-side accuracy.

`CONTRACT WP15`'s gates are unchanged and no threshold moved; this adds a
qualification to one evidence row, before any data exists for either arm.

# 2026-09-03 — CONTRACT (Rule 1): **WP16 — BLOCKER A, port parity against upstream at non-zero `kappa_3`**

**Class: STRATEGIC.** It decides whether the K3 flow this project would ship
computes the same function whose accuracy (`8.5075e-07`) was measured on the
torch side, and every WP15 gate is written against that flow. Pre-registered
**before any data exists**; HEAD at write time `5fedb4c`; `preflight.ps1` GREEN
12/12 at that HEAD. Directing brief: strategist review of the 2026-09-02
stopping-point audit (parity -> op count -> WP15 arms, in that order).

## Question

`p2_k3_fnp.k3_flow` (the `fnp` port, the thing the grader can run) and
`p2_range_lab.means_of(hook_nl=_regen_hook_nl())` (the torch reference, the thing
`8.5075e-07` was measured on) are supposed to be the same function. The canary
says they are not: the port scored `2.8192e-06` on 20 official rows where the
reference predicted `8.5075e-07`, a **`3.31x` miss**, while the matched v2.6.1
control transferred to `3.2%`. **Where do they diverge, and is it spelling or
precision?**

## Evidence

| # | item | status |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | canary raw MSE `2.8192e-06` on the official `mini` split, `0/20` failed, FLOP parity exact | **CONFIRMED** (grader, 2026-09-02) |
| E2 | v2.6.1 control transfers to `3.2%` on the same 20 rows -> split/networks/instrument are fine | **CONFIRMED** (same run) |
| E3 | reference raw `8.5075e-07` on 8 `P01` nets, torch, f32 | **CONFIRMED** (WP14 C0-i, `gpuq` 121) |
| E4 | `--layer-k2` passes at `kappa_3 = kappa_4 = 0` (mean `0.00`, cov `5.1e-16`, third-cumulant **diagonal** `1.07e-14`) | **CONFIRMED** — and it never tests the `(2,1)` slice |
| E5 | 7 of 7 value-destroying mutations survive all three existing checks | **CONFIRMED** (`mutation_coverage.json`) |
| E6 | counted FLOPs on this path are value-independent | **CONFIRMED** (`p2_slice_cost.py --value-invariance`) |

## Hypothesis + mechanism

**H1 (primary): the port subtracts the `(1,1,1)` block's repeated part from the
slices it regenerates `M` from, and upstream does not.** Derived from upstream
rev `93d091a4`, by hand, before any run:

1. `factor_k3.py` does `K_ds[3] -= pK_111.get_repeated()` — it removes the
   factored block's repeated part **from the stored DS part only**, so that the
   sum does not double count.
2. It then returns `K_out[3] = pK_111 + FactoredTensor.from_dstensor(K_ds[3])`,
   and `FactoredTensor.__add__` **discards the repeated cache** (its own TODO says
   so). So `K_out[3].get_repeated()` recomputes from the concatenated factors.
3. `_factored_get_dslice` is additive over the concatenated `r`-blocks (the
   elementwise products never mix `r` indices), so
   `rep(K_out[3]) = rep(pK_111) + rep(from_dstensor(K_ds[3]))`.
4. `from_dstensor` is an exact right inverse of `get_repeated`: with
   `A = diag(D3) + 3 D21^T` and `D21` diagonal-free, the `(3,)` slice comes back
   as `diag(A) = D3` and the `(2,1)` slice as `(1/3) A^T` off-diagonal `= D21`.
   Checked by hand for both surviving block permutations.
5. Therefore `rep(K_out[3]) = rep(pK_111) + (K_ds3_orig - rep(pK_111)) = K_ds3_orig`
   — **the un-subtracted pK->K output.** The regeneration hook rebuilds `M` from
   *that*.

`p2_k3_fnp.k3_layer` instead computes `S3 = K[(3,)] - p111_3`,
`S21 = K[(2,1)] - p111_21` and rebuilds from those. The port's `p111_3` and
`p111_21` were re-derived here and **are exactly `rep(pK_111)`** (block 1 gives
`w1^3 D3` and `w1_i^2 w1_j D21`; block 2's `(3,)` slice is zero on `C11`'s zero
diagonal and its `(2,1)` slice is `(fac1 . fac3) off_mask` from the single
surviving `({0,2},{1})` block permutation). So the port's `M_out` is wrong by
**`2 x rep(pK_111)`** — it subtracts where upstream effectively adds nothing.

**Why every existing check is blind to it.** At `kappa_3 = 0` we have `M = 0`,
hence `D3 = D21 = 0` and `p111_3 = 0` — so the `(3,)` slice, which is all
`--layer-k2` tests at third order, is **exactly right in the degenerate limit**.
`p111_21` is *not* zero there (it is `fac1 . fac3`, built from the covariance),
but no check reads the `(2,1)` slice. This is the same blind spot `SKEPTIC
WP14-FOLLOWUP` measured as 0-of-7 mutations killed.

**H2 (alternative): f32 precision in a cancelling sum.** Kept live because the
brief names it and because H1 must be shown to be the *whole* gap, not part of it.

## Intervention

The smallest change that discriminates: **run both programs on the same networks
in f64 and compare, layer by layer, at two points per layer.** No fitting, no
selection, no tuning. Then flip exactly one line (`- p111` -> no subtraction)
behind a flag and re-run.

New instrument `local_sim/p2_k3_parity.py`; `k3_layer`/`k3_flow` gain a
`probe=None` callback and a `regen_mode` switch, both no-ops at their defaults.

## Predictions (numbered, before the data)

1. **P1.** End-to-end f64 drift of the port vs the reference at `128 x 4`,
   `regen_mode="sub"` (today's shipped spelling): **> 10%** relative on the final
   layer's means. *(Falsifies H1 if it comes back < 1%.)*
2. **P2.** With `regen_mode="nosub"`: **<= 1e-10** relative at `128 x 4` in f64 —
   i.e. agreement to f64 round-off, not merely "closer".
3. **P3.** The ladder localizes it to the **`(2,1)` slice at the nonlinear point**,
   not the linear point: `mu_pre`, `cov_pre`, `s3_pre`, `s21_pre` all agree to
   `<= 1e-12` at **layer 0 and layer 1** under both modes.
4. **P4.** At **layer 0** the `(3,)` slice agrees under both modes (`p111_3 = 0`
   there) and the `(2,1)` slice does **not** under `"sub"`. This is the exact
   signature that explains why `--layer-k2` passed.
5. **P5.** The transpose orientation is **already correct** (`S21[i,j] = k3[i,i,j]`,
   rebuilt as `3 S21^T`): the transposed comparison will be *worse*, not better,
   at every layer. *(Named as a suspect by the brief; I predict it is not one.)*
6. **P6.** The factor `3` and the sign in `diag(S3) + 3 S21^T` are **correct**.
7. **P7.** Repeating the fixed port at **f32** vs the f64 reference gives
   `<= 1e-4` relative — i.e. precision is a *second-order* effect here and H2 is
   **not** the explanation for `3.3x`.
8. **P8.** Fixing H1 **removes** operations and FLOPs: `p111_3`, `p111_21`,
   `fac1`, `fac3` and `w1_sq` become dead. I predict a **strict decrease** in
   counted FLOPs per layer, so the `10,837,935,618` floor figure is **superseded
   downward** and must be re-metered before any price is quoted again.
9. **P9.** At `1024 x 16` in f64 the fixed port reproduces the reference to
   `<= 1%` end-to-end on all 8 `P01` networks.
10. **P10 (the one that matters).** The raw MSE of the fixed port against minted
    truth on those 8 networks lands inside **`[7.0e-07, 1.1e-06]`**, i.e. it
    reproduces `8.5075e-07` within noise, rather than `2.8192e-06`.
11. **P11.** I predict the `--layer-k2` degeneracy check still **passes
    unchanged** after the fix (it is blind to the change), so it must not be
    quoted as evidence the fix is right.

## Gate

Set now, from the brief, and passed to nothing that has a default:

> **G-PARITY.** End-to-end relative drift of `k3_flow` (f64) against
> `means_of(hook_nl=regen)` (f64) `<= 1%` on all 8 `P01` networks at `1024 x 16`,
> **and** the fixed port's raw MSE against the existing minted truth reproducing
> `8.5075e-07` within its noise band `[7.0e-07, 1.1e-06]`.

A pass on the first clause alone is **not** a pass: two programs can agree with
each other and both be the wrong function. The second clause is what ties the
port back to the number the write-up quotes.

## Falsifier

H1 is rejected if `regen_mode="nosub"` does **not** close the gap at `128 x 4` in
f64 (P2 fails), or if the ladder shows the first divergence **before** the
nonlinear step (P3 fails) — in which case the defect is in the linear step or in
the frozen coefficient tables, and the `(1,1,1)` derivation above is wrong.

## Baseline and tier

Control is the **torch reference on the same weights**, `hook_nl=_regen_hook_nl()`,
which `p2_range_lab --selftest` S2 has already shown is bit-identical to
`p2_pb_rank.predict(cap="dsproj")` at `1024 x 16`. Tier: **DESIGN**, `P01`
`[40,821,001,168 .. 40,821,001,175]` — the *same eight networks* WP13 E2 and
WP14 C0-i used. **This is a deliberate third overlap on that range and it must be
declared as such**: the whole point is to re-drive the networks whose truth is
already minted, and no new statistical claim is made on them. Nothing here reads
the public split; nothing is fitted anywhere.

## Cost model

**Phase 2, `lambda = 0`, so `C = F`** (`VALIDATION.md` section 2b-ii). This slice
quotes **no** cost claim: it changes values, so it changes the price, and P8 says
the price goes **down**. The standing `10,837,935,618`/layer and
`173,381,273,195`/MLP figures are **frozen as superseded** the moment the fix
lands, and Blocker B re-meters from scratch. Residual is reported only as
**headroom against the `0.4 s` cliff**, and never as a local absolute second.

## Statistic

**Deterministic parity, not a statistic.** Relative Frobenius drift per network,
reported for **all 8 individually** with min/max — never a mean, never a ratio of
means. No bootstrap, no interval: there is no sampling here. The only place a
statistic appears is P10's raw-MSE comparison against already-minted truth, which
is a **paired** re-read of an existing artifact and is quoted with its GT noise
floor (`1.72e-08`).

## Seed block

`P01[40,821,001,168 .. 40,821,001,175]`, claimed through `local_sim/seed_ledger.py`
by consumer `local_sim/p2_k3_parity.py`, with a `declare_pair` naming all three
consumers of that range. **No fresh seeds are spent.** `P05`/`P06` remain
untouched for WP15.

## Confounders / scope / what must not change

- **Two venvs.** The port runs in `.venv` (real flopscope, no torch); the
  reference runs in `.venv-gpu` (torch, no flopscope). They exchange `.npz` files
  and a **sha256 of the weights**, so "same networks" is proved, not assumed.
- `estimator.py` is not touched. Nothing is submitted. No board is read.
- The `mini` split is **not** re-read; the `3.3x` is diagnosed off the public data.
- `init_scale = 2.0` at every layer (convention 3) on **both** sides.
- If the fix lands, `--mutation-coverage`, `--layer-k2`, `--layer-price`,
  `--flow-price` and `p2_k3_candidate_parity.py` are all re-run, and the
  candidate `estimator_wp15_k3_canary.py` must be regenerated — the canary that
  scored `2.8192e-06` is **retired**, not amended.

**Samuel's prediction: NOT TAKEN for this contract.** Recorded honestly rather
than fabricated: the brief directed this to run today, and this slice is a
deterministic correctness check that spends no fresh seeds and promotes nothing.
His prediction is being taken instead on the question that follows it — whether
the fix closes the `3.3x` end to end — **before** that data exists.

# 2026-09-03 — WP16 RESULTS: **the `3.31x` was ONE LINE, and G-PARITY passes both clauses**

Contract `7169392`, committed before any data existed. Results here. Every number
below is f64 unless said otherwise, on the eight `P01` networks
`[40,821,001,168 .. 40,821,001,175]` — the same eight WP13 E2 and WP14 C0-i used,
declared as a third deliberate overlap and therefore **CORRELATED EVIDENCE with
both, never a third independent result.**

## The verdict

| | |
|---|---|
| **G-PARITY clause 1** | worst end-to-end drift **`1.692e-11`** vs gate `1e-2`, **8/8 nets**. **PASS** |
| **G-PARITY clause 2** | raw MSE **`8.5075e-07`** vs band `[7.0e-07, 1.1e-06]`. **PASS** — the reference figure to 4 s.f., ratio `1.000x` |
| the defect, kept as a control | **`2.6890e-06`**, ratio `3.161x` — where the grader measured `3.314x` on twenty other rows |

**H1 is confirmed and it is the whole gap.** `p2_k3_fnp.k3_layer` regenerated `M`
from `K[(3,)] - p111_3` and `K[(2,1)] - p111_21`. Upstream subtracts
`pK_111.get_repeated()` from the **stored DS part only**, then returns
`K_out[3] = pK_111 + FactoredTensor.from_dstensor(K_ds[3])` — and `__add__`
**discards the repeated cache**, so the regeneration hook's `get_repeated()`
recomputes from the concatenated factors and recovers `K_ds3` un-subtracted.

**Measured, not argued.** At layer 0, net 0, the two port arms against each other:

| quantity | sub vs nosub |
|---|---:|
| `K[(3,)]`, `K[(2,1)]` (upstream of the branch) | `0.000e+00` |
| `S3` | `0.000e+00` — because `p111_3` is **exactly zero** there |
| `S21` | `2.698e-02` |
| `M` — diagonal | `0.000e+00` |
| `M` — off-diagonal | `1.4605e+00`, and `3 x ||p111_21||` is `1.4605e+00`. **Ratio `1.000000`** |

## A correction to my own contract, made by the data

The contract said the port's `M_out` is *"wrong by `2 x rep(pK_111)`"*. **It is
wrong by `1 x`.** The measured ratio is `1.000000`, not `2`. My reasoning slipped
between two cases — if upstream *added* the repeated part the error would be
doubled; upstream nets out to *neither* adding nor subtracting, so a single
subtraction is a single error. The mechanism, the location and the sign were all
right; the factor was not.

## Predictions, scored

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `> 10%` end-to-end drift at `128x4` under `sub` | **REFUTED.** `2.377e-03` and `2.555e-03` — `0.24%`, not `>10%` |
| P2 | `<= 1e-10` under `nosub` at `128x4` | **HELD.** `2.653e-12`, `3.617e-12` |
| P3 | first divergence at the **nonlinear** point, not the linear one | **HELD in substance, REFUTED as written.** Layer 0: every linear component `0` or `6.9e-17`, and `M` is the first thing that moves. But I wrote "layers 0 **and 1**", and at layer 1 the `sub` arm's linear slices have already inherited the layer-0 error (`1.6e-01`). I predicted the localisation and forgot the propagation |
| P4 | at layer 0 the `(3,)` slice agrees under both modes and the `(2,1)` does not | **HELD, to six digits.** See the table above |
| P5 | the transpose orientation is **already correct** | **HELD.** Direct comparison `9.5e-16`, transposed `3.2e-02` at `1024`. The brief named it a suspect; it was not one |
| P6 | the factor `3` and the sign are correct | **HELD.** Parity to `1.7e-11`, and the battery now kills both `rebuild_3_to_2` and `rebuild_no_transpose` |
| P7 | f32 within `1e-4` of the f64 reference | **HELD with margin.** `4.1e-07` worst; raw MSE `8.5072e-07` against f64's `8.5075e-07`. **H2 is dead: precision is not the explanation, and f32 costs `0.004%` of the MSE** |
| P8 | the fix strictly **decreases** counted FLOPs | **HELD, direction right and magnitude small.** `10,837,935,618 -> 10,828,494,338` per layer; arrays `56 -> 49`. All of it is `O(n^2)`, so the matmul count barely moves (`5.047 -> 5.042`). *(WP17's op-count work later took the same figure to `10,813,796,920` / `5.036`; artifact `layer_price_wp17.json`.)* |
| P9 | `<= 1%` end to end at `1024x16` on all 8 | **HELD by nine orders.** `1.692e-11` |
| P10 | raw MSE inside `[7.0e-07, 1.1e-06]` | **HELD.** `8.5075e-07` |
| P11 | `--layer-k2` still passes, unchanged | **HELD.** `kappa3 1.067e-14`, identical. It was blind to this and must never be quoted as evidence the fix is right |

Nine held, one refuted, one half-refuted. **The refuted one matters most** — see
the knowledge delta.

## The re-metered price. Every earlier figure is SUPERSEDED

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| one layer, f32, `n = 1024` | `10,837,935,618` | **`10,813,796,920`** |
| whole flow, 16 layers | `173,381,273,195` | **`173,230,212,715`** |
| `x` budget | `0.078845` | **`0.078776`** |
| multiplier | `0.10000` | **`0.10000`** — unchanged, still at the floor |
| flopscope **operations** | `5,327` | **`5,119`** (`320`/layer) |
| arrays the dtype audit sees | `56` | **`49`** |

The residual reading from the same run is **not usable**: it was taken on a host
with another project's job running, and `AGENTS.md` forbids quoting a local
absolute second anyway. Only the op count is deterministic.

## The mutation battery: 0 of 7 becomes 9 of 9 on the live path

`SKEPTIC WP14-FOLLOWUP` built a battery of seven value-destroying mutations and
measured **0 killed**, which was the strongest available warning that the port
was unverified. WP16 adds a second detector that needs **no torch at run time**:
a 46 KB committed, hashed golden dump of upstream's own answer at `128x4` f64
(`golden_ref_128x4.npz`), plus five new mutations on the live path.

| detector | killed |
|---|---:|
| `--layer-k2` (the `kappa_3 = 0` closed forms) | `1 / 12` |
| golden parity against upstream | `9 / 12` |
| ... restricted to the **live** code path | **`9 / 9`** |

The three survivors are exactly the three that edit the `regen_mode="sub"`
branch, and each reports drift `3.617e-12` — the f64 baseline. That is not a gap;
**it is the proof that the branch is inert.**

## The structural finding, which outlives the bug

> **In a regenerating flow the entire `(1,1,1)` block is dead work.**

Its all-distinct part is discarded by `from_dstensor` at the rebuild, and its
repeated part cancels exactly against the subtraction upstream makes from the DS
part. So `p111_3`, `p111_21`, `fac1`, `fac3` and `w1_sq` were not merely
mis-signed — **they compute nothing the answer depends on.** Removing them is
what the `9,441,280` FLOPs and `208` operations are.

This does not change `CONTRACT WP15`'s premise, it sharpens it. WP15 says the
regenerating flow's error *is* the discarded all-distinct block; the block being
wholly dead is the same statement, made exactly.

## Knowledge delta

1. **A `0.12%` drift in the means is a `3.2x` miss in the score, and the gate the
   brief specified could not see it.** The defect's end-to-end drift at
   `1024 x 16` is **`1.3046e-03` worst** of the eight (`1.064e-03` best) — it
   **passes** a `<= 1%` drift gate comfortably,
   at both shapes. Only clause 2, against minted truth, catches it. **Relative
   drift in the means is a bad proxy for MSE**, because the means are `O(1)` and
   the error we are chasing is `O(1e-3)` RMS; a perturbation that is negligible
   against the signal is enormous against the residual. Had the contract not
   insisted that "two programs agreeing is not evidence that either is right",
   this slice would have declared the broken port fine. **P1's refutation is the
   same fact seen from the other side**: I expected a big drift because I was
   thinking in score units, and drift is not score units.
2. **A check that cannot see a defect is not weak, it may be checking dead code.**
   Three of `SKEPTIC WP14-FOLLOWUP`'s seven mutations survived because they
   mutated work the correct program does not do. "0 of 7 killed" read as *"the
   checks are weak"*; part of it was *"the program does more than it needs to"*.
   Both were true and only one had been named.
3. **The cheapest possible reference is a committed golden file.** Parity needed
   torch, upstream's checkout, and a second venv — once. After that, 46 KB of
   `.npz` gives every future run of `--mutation-coverage` a real oracle in the
   grader's own venv. The battery went from `0/7` to `9/9` for the cost of one
   CPU minute and one file.
4. **The gpuq snapshot is built from git, so `.gitignore` is part of the test
   harness.** `*.npz` is blanket-ignored here, so the golden file the new
   detector hashes went uncommitted and every brokered run of that check would
   have died on a missing file — the third instance of *"a check that cannot run
   reads as a check that passed"* in this repository.
5. **The change gate caught its own new hole immediately.** Claiming `P01` with
   an artifact name and not finalising it turned steps 7 and 9 RED within the
   hour. That is `SKEPTIC WP13`'s process fix doing exactly its job on the very
   next slice that could have skipped it.

## What this does and does NOT license

- **Every accuracy claim that rested on `8.5075e-07` is restored**, including
  WP14 C0-i's paired `1.637x`-better-than-v2.7 comparison, because the file that
  can be graded now reproduces the torch figure to four significant figures.
- **The `334x` two-slice oracle inherits the same restoration.** Its PROVISIONAL
  was conditional on exactly this, and the condition is met.
- **Nothing has been re-graded.** The canary that scored `2.8192e-06` is
  **retired**, not amended, and no board number exists for the fixed file.
- **`estimator.py` is untouched and remains v2.6.1.** Nothing is submitted,
  nothing is designated, and the `mini` split was not re-read.
- **The residual is still the blocker.** `1.21x` headroom on the deployment
  authority was measured on the retired file; the fix removes `208` of `5,327`
  operations, which is `3.9%` and nowhere near the `>= 4x` the soak requires.
  Blocker B is unchanged in substance and is next.

# 2026-09-03 — WP17: **Blocker B, the operation count. `5,327` -> `~2,650` per MLP, and every float bit-identical**

Class: **IMPORTANT** (the instrument and the candidate file, not a gate and not a
seed block). Written prediction first, `preflight.ps1` GREEN at `f2b0e6a` before
the work, LOG entry with a knowledge delta below. No decision block is spent, no
public data is fitted, and `estimator.py` is untouched.

## Why this is the half that matters

Phase 2 sets `lambda = 0`. FLOPs below the `0.1` floor are worth **nothing**, and
the only cost that can still ruin a run is the `0.4 s` per-MLP residual, which
**fails** the MLP and zeroes its prediction. `docs/GOTCHAS.md` records that the
residual tracks **operation count and Python glue, not FLOPs**, and the graded
canary confirmed it: `2.5x` the shipped file's arithmetic, `11.8x` its
operations, and `1.21x` headroom where the shipped file has `6.78x`.

## The prediction, written before the work

> Most of the operation count is in `wick_coefs` and the per-term loop, and the
> reductions in `OP_COUNT_NOTES` are worth roughly half of the `333`/layer. I
> predict the total lands between `2,000` and `3,000` per MLP, that counted FLOPs
> move by **less than 5%** in either direction, and that **every reduction can be
> made an IEEE identity** rather than an approximation — i.e. that the output is
> bit-identical, not merely close. I do **not** predict this is enough for `4x`
> headroom.

## Result

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| flopscope **operations** per MLP | `5,327` | **`2,646`** |
| ... per layer | `333` | **`169`** normal, **`59`** last |
| counted FLOPs | `173,381,273,195` | **`168,629,787,238`** |
| `x` budget | `0.078845` | **`0.076684`** |
| multiplier | `0.10000` | **`0.10000`** — still at the floor |
| output, both dtypes | | **BITWISE IDENTICAL**, `maxdiff 0.000e+00` |

**The prediction holds on all three counts**: `2,646` is inside `[2000, 3000]`,
FLOPs moved `-2.7%`, and every change is an identity.

## The six reductions, and why each is exact

1. **`wick_coefs` was 144 of a layer's 315 operations** — 46% — to produce
   sixteen `(n,)` vectors. Now **40**. `sigma^j` is built once, left-associated
   in exactly the order the per-pair loop built it; `base(k)` is memoised
   (recomputed twice for `k = 2, 3, 4`); `1.0 * ones * phi / sigma` is spelled
   `phi / sigma`; and the twelve polynomials run as **one padded batched
   Horner**. The padding is exact because `0 * a + 0 == 0` and `0 * a + c == c`.
2. **Last-layer pruning.** The grader reads post-ReLU **means**. At layer 15
   there is no next layer, so the only output ever read is
   `mu_out = K[(1,)] = pK[(1,)]`, which needs `w(0,1)`, `w(3,1)`, `w(4,1)`, `D3`
   and `D4`. **Two of the five matmuls**, `C11`, `D22`, 22 of 25 pK terms, 6 of 7
   `pK -> K` slices, the covariance, `K[4]` and the rebuild are skipped. That
   layer costs **59** operations against 192. `last_layer` previously skipped
   only the rebuild — `0.001` of a matmul.
3. **The four one-dimensional slices as one `(4, n)` expression.** The frozen
   table gives every `(p,)` the same three terms
   (`w(0,p) + (1/6) D3 w(3,p) + (1/24) D4 w(4,p)`), so twelve terms and eight
   accumulations become nine operations. A **regrouping, not a reassociation** —
   every float is multiplied and added in the order it was.
4. **Scaled block products memoised.** `0.5 C11^2` appears in all three
   two-dimensional slices and `0.25 D22` likewise; both were recomputed each
   time. The memo key is `(blocks, scalar)`, not blocks alone, because the scaled
   product is what repeats.
5. **`* 1.0` skipped** where the frozen table says so — 9 of 25 terms, 7 of 19
   `pK -> K` rows — and the single `* -1.0` folded into a subtraction, since
   `a + (-b)` and `a - b` are the same IEEE float.
6. **Constants hoisted.** `off_mask`, the ones vector and the Wick coefficient
   stacks leave the per-layer path entirely; in the candidate they leave
   `predict` for `setup`, which is off the per-MLP budget. `outer(ones, ones)`
   was an all-ones matrix materialised so the meter would charge a spelling that
   did not know it was constant — under `lambda = 0` that honesty was costing
   operations to save FLOPs that are free.

## How "bit-identical" was established, since it is the whole licence

The pre-change module was checked out to a scratch path, imported beside the new
one, and both were run on the same minted network in the same process. The
outputs were compared **as raw bytes**, in `float32` and in `float64`:

    f32:  BITWISE IDENTICAL = True   maxdiff 0.000e+00
    f64:  BITWISE IDENTICAL = True   maxdiff 0.000e+00

and at the live shape the parity artifacts are unchanged to every digit printed:
`1.692e-11` worst end-to-end drift against upstream on 8/8 `P01` nets, raw MSE
`8.5075e-07`, ratio `1.000x`. `--layer-k2` is unchanged (`kappa3 1.067e-14`), the
golden-parity battery still kills `9/9` on the live path, `whest validate`
passes, and `p2_k3_candidate_parity.py` is green with **counted FLOPs matching
exactly and `rel-rms 0.000e+00`**.

## A defect in my own instrument, found by disbelieving a number

`p2_k3_parity.py` kept `--regen-mode` defaulting to `"sub"` after
`p2_k3_fnp.k3_layer`'s default became `"nosub"`. One dump named
`port_wp17_1024.npz` therefore contained **the defect**, and compared at
`1.199e-03` where the fixed port compares at `1.692e-11`. Nothing errored; the
file was simply mislabelled. It was caught because `1.199e-03` was recognisable
as the defect's own number from four hours earlier. **A default that disagrees
with the thing it drives is a silent mislabel, and the only reason this one was
cheap is that its wrong answer had already been given a name.**

## What is NOT established

- **The residual is not measured.** Four local readings today put the matched K2
  control at `0.0277`, `0.0322`, `0.0430` and `0.0340 s` on the same host — a
  55% spread driven by another project's jobs — and the K3/K2 **ratio** moved
  with it (`10.02`, `11.98`, `12.76`, `7.28`). **Under contention even the ratio
  to a matched control in the same process is not stable**, which is a new fact:
  `VALIDATION.md` §2b-ii offered the ratio as the transferable quantity, and it
  transfers only on a quiet host. The authority is
  `whest run --runner subprocess`, and that run is queued.
- **Halving the operations does not obviously buy `4x`.** If the residual were
  purely per-operation, `2,646 / 5,327` would take the graded `1.21x` to about
  `2.4x`. The soak requires `>= 4x` on the worst run. **On the arithmetic
  available, this is not yet enough**, and the remaining exact reductions are
  nearly exhausted at ~165 operations a layer against a `~120` target.
- Nothing has been graded, submitted or designated. `estimator.py` remains
  v2.6.1.

## Knowledge delta

1. **Half of a "third-order cumulant flow" was polynomial evaluation.** 144 of
   315 operations a layer went on sixteen `O(n)` vectors, in a program whose
   headline cost is five `n^3` matmuls. Under a cost model that charges
   arithmetic, that work is invisible — it is `0.001%` of the FLOPs. Under one
   that charges **operations**, it was the largest single item. Which half of the
   objective is free decides where the code's problems are.
2. **"Charge honestly for a spelling that does not know a value is constant" is a
   FLOP-era instinct that costs operations.** `outer(ones, ones)` existed so the
   meter would not be flattered. Under `lambda = 0` it bought nothing and cost
   two operations a layer, on the axis that can fail an MLP.
3. **Bit-exactness is available far further than expected.** Batched Horner over
   zero-padded coefficients, memoised sub-expressions, skipping `* 1.0`, folding
   `* -1.0` into a subtraction, and stacking four slices that share their
   arithmetic order are all IEEE identities. The reductions that would require
   reassociation — factoring `0.5 C11^2 X + 0.25 D22 X` — were **left undone**,
   because a change that is merely "small" needs a measurement and a change that
   is an identity needs only a comparison.

# 2026-09-03 — PRE-REGISTRATION: the official read of the fixed canary (SKEPTIC WP16's named follow-up)

`SKEPTIC WP16` returned **ACCEPT** and named the cheapest discriminating
follow-up: re-run the regenerated canary through
`whest run --runner subprocess` on the same 20 `v2-phase2 mini` rows the retired
canary was scored on, **with v2.6.1 as a matched control in the same session**.
Registered here **before the run completes** — job `174` was still QUEUED when
this was written, and the control had not been submitted at all.

**Tier: CONFIRM, read-only.** No seed block is drawn, nothing is fitted, nothing
is selected, and the rows have already been read. This measures three things and
no others: the official per-MLP **residual**, `n_failed_mlps`, and the raw MSE.

## The prediction, taken from SKEPTIC WP16 and adopted unchanged

| # | prediction |
|---|---|
| **Q1** | raw MSE lands in **`[7.5e-07, 1.15e-06]`**. Above `~1.3e-06` **falsifies** "one line was the whole of the `3.31x`" and says something else is also wrong |
| **Q2** | `n_failed_mlps` is **0** |
| **Q3** | worst-MLP residual headroom is **`> 1.21x`** (the retired file's) and **`< 4x`** (the soak requirement). My point estimate is `2.0–2.8x`, from `2,708 / 5,327` applied to the retired file's `0.3314 s` |
| **Q4** | the v2.6.1 control reproduces its own `4.1805e-06` to within `1%`, since it is the identical file on identical rows |

**Why Q4 is not decoration.** The 2026-09-02 run is what made a disappointing
number a *diagnosis* rather than an ambiguity, and it did so only because a
control transferred to `3.2%`. Without it, a surprising MSE here could be the
split, the harness, the host or the fix.

**Why the band is `[7.5e-07, 1.15e-06]` and not centred on `8.5075e-07`.**
`SKEPTIC WP16` measured the P01-to-official transfer ratio for two estimators —
`1.048x` for the defective K3, `1.096x` for the K2 closure — predicting
`~8.9-9.3e-07` officially. That is an inference from two estimators on 8 against
20 networks with no interval, so the band is wider than the point estimate and is
**not** the `[7.0e-07, 1.1e-06]` band `CONTRACT WP16` clause 2 used offline.

## What this run CANNOT settle, stated now

Neither this nor anything offline can rule out a defect shared by upstream,
`p2_range_lab.run_flow` and `bridge.build_mlp`: golden parity is blind to it by
construction, and clause 2's band was set from the same program. `SKEPTIC WP16`
bounded that risk at **layer 1 only**, by checking the minted truth against the
closed form `||W1[:,j]|| / sqrt(2 pi)` (rms-z `0.93-1.05` on 8 networks x 2
replicas). **An official raw MSE near `9e-07` would bound it at every layer**,
because the grader's own labels are independent of all three.

# 2026-09-03 — SKEPTIC WP16: **ACCEPT**, with eleven documentation defects and one gate pointed at the wrong axis

Audited at `82f798e`. Verdict **ACCEPT** on the parity claim. The Skeptic did not
take the derivation on trust — it re-derived `H1` from `factor_k3.py` by hand,
evaluated both block-permutation sums itself, and confirmed the mechanism in the
raw `.npz` dumps rather than in the prose.

## What it independently established, and it is more than the slice claimed

1. **The reference really is upstream, and observing it does not perturb it.**
   The worry was real — `get_dslice` writes into `self.repeated.slices`, so the
   observer could have populated a cache the regeneration then consumed. It ran
   `p2_range_lab.means_of(hook_nl=_regen_hook_nl())` against
   `p2_k3_parity.run_ref` on the same weights: **bitwise identical**, as are an
   observe-only hook and a no-op hook, and the committed golden file. Mechanism:
   `factored_nonlin_kprop_k3`'s own term loop already calls `get_dslice` on
   `WK[3]` before `pK_111 = WK[3].clone()`, so the cache is populated whether or
   not anyone looks.
2. **The FLOP delta reconciles EXACTLY, and in closed form.** `sub - nosub` at
   `n = 128`, depths 1-4, is **`147,968` per layer `= 9n^2 + 4n`** — which at
   `n = 1024` is exactly the claimed `9,441,280`. Op delta exactly `13`/layer
   → `208` at depth 16; `56 - 49 = 7` audited arrays = the 7 removed
   `audit.check` names. **Nothing else is gone.** This is a much sharper check
   than "the number went down" and it is the one I did not do.
3. **The minted truth is not circular.** It checked
   `truth_P01_wp13nets.npz` against the exact layer-1 closed form
   `||W1[:,j]|| / sqrt(2 pi)`: **rms-z `0.93-1.05`** on 8 networks x 2 replicas.
   Weights, orientation, input distribution and Monte-Carlo scale are all
   confirmed independently of both programs, and the artifact's sha256 matches
   the ledger's `finalize` record — not re-minted.
4. `M_sub - M_nosub = -3 p111_21^T` to **`3.2e-15`** relative, magnitude ratio
   `0.9999999999999999`, and `||p111_3|| = 0.0` exactly.
5. `git show 18e88aa:estimator_wp15_k3_canary.py` computes, line for line, what
   `--regen-mode sub` computes today — so the control really is the graded
   spelling.

## What it found wrong, and all of it is now fixed

**One is a real gate defect, not hygiene.** `p2_k3_candidate_parity.py` gated
counted **FLOPs** exactly and merely *printed* the operation count — **it gated
the axis `lambda = 0` makes free and left the axis that can fail an MLP
unguarded.** Repaired: the op delta is now a gate with a stated slack of 16 for
the operations the candidate legitimately pays and the lab flow does not (the
per-width constant build and the weight `astype`, both once per MLP). And the
check had **never been run at `1024 x 16`** — it is the only thing tying the
shippable file to the price every document quotes. Queued.

The rest are stale numbers, and the list is embarrassing in a specific way: **I
updated the prose faster than I updated the things the prose is about.**

| # | defect | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| A | `p2_k3_fnp` docstring said `"sub" remains the default` — the **opposite of the code** since `57a4df3` | yes |
| B | `p2_k3_parity` still defaulted `--regen-mode` to `sub`; `--port` with no flag dumped the defect | yes, at `08eefa0`, before the Skeptic reported |
| C | `--flow-price` hard-coded the superseded `16 x 10,837,935,618` extrapolation, so its own new artifact carried a wrong reference and printed a wrong shortfall | yes — it now extrapolates from the run's own measured layer |
| D | P8's headline per-layer FLOP figure had **no committed artifact**, prose only, in four documents | yes — `layer_price_wp17.json`, and the figure is now `10,813,796,920` |
| E | `docs/VALIDATION.md` §2b-ii — **binding law** — still carried `173.38 B`, `5,327`, `0.2774 s`, `1.4x` | yes, with a superseding block |
| F | `docs/GOTCHAS.md` and write-up §6.5 carried superseded FLOP tables | yes |
| G | `CURRENT_STATE.md`'s `SKEPTIC WP14-FOLLOWUP` block still said the port was "still unchecked against upstream" | yes |
| H | `1.199e-03` was quoted as the defect's drift — it is **net 0's**, not the worst (`1.3046e-03`), and my own contract says min/max, never a mean | yes |
| I | write-up §6.6 published a `~12x` residual taken from the very run the LOG calls unusable | yes — the residual column is gone and the reason is stated |
| K | `p2_k3_candidate_parity` had never run at `1024 x 16` | yes — `candidate_parity_1024x16.json`: values `0.000e+00`, FLOPs identical, **operations identical** |
| L | the new op-count gate's slack of 16 was exactly the delta at depth 16, because the weight `astype` was metered **once per layer** — a slack that scales with what it bounds is not a bound | yes — the cast is guarded by a Python `dtype` comparison, the delta is now `+0`, and the slack is `4` |
| J | write-up §6.6 put `5,119` ops and the retired file's `1.21x` in one breath without the word "retired" | yes |

**Two corrections to my own numbers.** Clause 2 is **nearly redundant with
clause 1**: the Skeptic scored the *torch* dump against the same truth and also
got `8.507508e-07`, so `1.000x` is arithmetically forced once clause 1 passes at
`1.7e-11` — it ties the port to truth, but it is not independent corroboration of
the value, and I presented it as if it were. And **`3.314x` is a cross-sample
ratio** (20 graded rows over 8 offline networks); the paired figure is `3.161x`.

## The process hazard it hit, which is mine

It first measured **five different FLOP/op counts for one command** and was ready
to report flopscope non-determinism. **It was me, committing `ae44369` into the
tree while its audit ran.** It recovered by pinning to `82f798e` with
`git archive`. Worse: a `workerq` job it submitted picked up a git snapshot with
`p2_k3_fnp.py` half-optimised and the canary not, and **correctly FAILED** the
price check — the check doing its job, and also proof that **any measurement
taken on this repository today without pinning a commit is unattributable.**
Launching a Skeptic and then continuing to commit is a defect in how I ran the
slice, not in the slice.

## The unresolved ambiguity, in its own words

Whether the fix delivers `8.5075e-07` **on graded data** is not settled by
anything here and cannot be. The only transfer evidence is that the
P01-to-official ratio is `1.048x` for the defective K3 and `1.096x` for the K2
closure, predicting `~8.9-9.3e-07` officially — an inference from two estimators
on 8 against 20 networks with no interval. Separately, **neither of us can rule
out a defect shared by upstream, `run_flow` and `build_mlp`**: golden parity is
blind to it by construction and clause 2's band came from the same program. The
layer-1 closed-form check bounds that risk **at layer 1 only**.

**Its cheapest discriminating follow-up is pre-registered above and queued**: the
regenerated canary through `whest run --runner subprocess` on the same 20 rows,
**with v2.6.1 as a matched control in the same session** — which my queued run
did not have until the Skeptic said so. Band `[7.5e-07, 1.15e-06]`; above
`~1.3e-06` falsifies "one line was the whole of it".

# 2026-09-03 (LATE) — **THE DEPLOYMENT AUTHORITY CONFIRMS THE FIX: `8.75e-07` RAW, `0` OF `100` FAILED — AND `G-M-DEPTH` FAILS**

Two results, from `gpuq` 174/178 (official runner) and 176/177 (Arm M).

> **THE `3.31x` IS FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR ON GRADED DATA.** The retired canary
> scored `2.8192e-06`; the fixed one scores `8.75e-07` on five times as many

**What this licenses and what it does not.** It licenses the accuracy claim: the
regenerating K3 flow, at the multiplier floor, is **`4.63x` better than the
shipped file on the organisers' own data**. It does **not** license nomination:
the `>= 4x` residual soak has not run, `certify_candidate` has not run, the Linux
memory gate has not run, and **nothing may be fitted or selected on these rows** —
this is a CONFIRM read and both arms were run to measure, not to choose.

**Which file this measured.** Job 174's snapshot is commit **`ae44369`**,
`2,708` operations — not HEAD's `2,646`. Every change since is bit-exact, so the
**accuracy figure is identical** to HEAD's and the **residual figure is a
conservative upper bound**. The `62`-operation difference is not re-measured and
is not claimed.

**And the residual did not fall the way the op count did.** Ratio of mean
residual to the control: `0.2233 / 0.0384 = 5.82x`, against a local operation
ratio of `5.98x` — those agree closely, which is the first clean confirmation
that **operations predict residual**. But the retired file's OFFICIAL worst was
`0.3314 s` at `5,327` operations, and halving the operations moved the MEAN to
`0.2233 s`. Mean-then and worst-now are not comparable, which is exactly why the
worst-MLP figure is being re-read rather than inferred.

## 2. `G-M-DEPTH` FAILS — Arm M's cheap version is not viable

`1024 x 16`, f32, **16 `P01` networks** `[..176..191]` (disjoint from the eight
WP13/WP14/WP16 share), layer-averaged over layers 4..14 exactly as
`CONTRACT WP15`'s composition rule specifies. f64 control on 2 of them.

| `k` un-regenerated layers | f32, 16 nets | f64 control, 2 nets | gate |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 (the regenerating flow) | `0.0000` | `0.0000` | — |
| 1 (age `l-1`) | `0.3381` | `0.3461` | |
| **2 (ages `l-1, l-2`)** | **`0.5734`** | **`0.5829`** | **`< 0.70` — FAILS** |
| 3 | `0.7322` | `0.7414` | `>= 0.70`, but not the gate that was written |

Per-network spread at `k = 2` is `0.5532-0.5933` — tight, so this is not a
sampling accident. f32 and f64 agree to `1.6%`, so it is not a precision
artifact.

**Prediction P1 is REFUTED.** It said *"age `l-1` alone explains `>= 50%`;
`{l-1, l-2}` `>= 70%`. Refuted if `l-1` alone is `< 30%`."* Measured: `l-1`
alone is `0.3381` — above the `30%` refutation trigger but well below `50%` — and
`{l-1, l-2}` is `0.5734`, not `>= 70%`. The direction came from WP4's
`0.42-0.70` single-layer share, and the true single-layer share is `0.34`.

**Arm M is NOT killed, and that distinction is the contract's own.** The
falsifier is *"three ages together explain `< 70%`"*, and three ages explain
`0.7322`. So the falsifier does **not** fire. What fails is the gate as written,
and the consequence is a cost one: `E21`'s memory is **three generations deep,
not two**.

**Why that is close to fatal on arithmetic rather than on evidence.** The
contract already priced this: carrying one extra generation exactly turns `K[3]`
into rank `2n`, costs two extra `contract_W` matmuls and breaks the `A2 == A3`
collapse in the `(2,1)` slice — **~5 extra matmuls a layer against a margin of
`1.36`**. Three generations is worse. A rank-`r` sketch replaces each with an
`(n x n)(n x r)` product at `r/n` of a matmul, and the affordability horizon is
`r <= 192`. So Arm M survives only as **a rank-`r <= 192` sketch of three
generations recovering `~73%` of `E21`** — and `73%` of `E21` is not `73%` of the
error, because `E3` carries ~40% of the regenerating flow's error and this
measures only the `(2,1)` slice.

**What must NOT be concluded**: that `k = 3` "clears the gate". The gate was
written on `k = 2` before the data existed, and moving it to `k = 3` after seeing
that `k = 3` passes is exactly the post-hoc gate move `VALIDATION.md` forbids and
that `SKEPTIC WP14` caught once already. The honest statement is: **the gate
failed, the falsifier did not fire, and the arm now needs a cost case it did not
need before.**

## Knowledge delta

1. **Operations predict residual, and now there is a clean number for it.** The
   official mean-residual ratio to a matched control is `5.82x` where the local
   operation ratio is `5.98x`. Every earlier attempt to establish this was
   contaminated by host load; the deployment authority, running both arms on 100
   rows, is not.
2. **A `raw` report does not print what a residual gate is written on.** The
   `>= 4x` requirement is on the worst MLP; `--detail raw` gives an aggregate.
   Four hours of local residual measurement, all of it unusable, and the number
   that decides was one CLI flag away.
3. **`E21`'s memory is three deep, not two, and the difference is a cost case.**
   `0.34 / 0.57 / 0.73` for one, two and three generations. WP4's locality
   result pointed the right way and was quantitatively optimistic — the
   single-layer share is half what its range suggested.
4. **The fix is confirmed by an instrument independent of every program in the
   chain.** `SKEPTIC WP16` could bound the shared-defect risk at layer 1 only.
   `8.75e-07` on the grader's own labels bounds it everywhere.

# 2026-09-03 (LATE) — the WORST-MLP residual: **`2.23x`. Blocker B does not clear.**

`gpuq` 182, `--detail full --format json`, snapshot `22db10a` whose canary is
**byte-identical to HEAD** (`git diff` empty), so this is the `2,646`-operation
file and not a stale one. Artifact
`experiments/2026-09-03_wp17_official/official_residual.json`.

| per-MLP residual, 100 official rows | s |
|---|---:|
| min | `0.1493` |
| p50 | `0.1537` |
| p90 | `0.1575` |
| p99 | `0.1593` |
| **max** | **`0.1797`** |

| | |
|---|---|
| **worst-run headroom vs the `0.4 s` cliff** | **`2.23x`** |
| mean headroom | `2.60x` |
| `n_failed_mlps` / residual-exhausted flags | `0` / `0` |
| standing soak requirement | **`>= 4x` on the worst run of `3 x 100`** |
| **verdict** | **DOES NOT CLEAR** |

**The distribution is remarkably tight, and that is a real finding.** `p99` is
`0.1593` and the maximum is `0.1797` — the worst MLP is **13% above the 99th
percentile**, and the whole 100-row spread is `1.20x` from min to max. When the
`>= 4x` bar was written, `VALIDATION.md` §2b-ii put run-to-run spread at
`~2.4x` — that figure came from the LOCAL instrument on a contended host. **On
the deployment authority the per-MLP spread is `1.20x`, not `2.4x`.** The bar was
calibrated against noise the authority does not have.

**That is an observation, not a licence to move the bar.** The `>= 4x`
requirement is a standing policy and this entry does not change it. It is flagged
because the evidence the policy was written on has been superseded by better
evidence, and **that is a decision for Samuel and the strategist, not for the
agent that would benefit from the answer.**

**What `4x` would take.** Worst must be `<= 0.1 s`, from `0.1797` — a `1.8x`
residual reduction. The official mean-residual ratio to the matched control
(`5.82x`) tracked the local operation ratio (`5.98x`) to within 3%, so
operations are the right lever: `~1,470` operations per MLP, `~92` a layer,
against today's `2,646` / `165`. **That is essentially the brief's own `~120`
per-layer target, and it needs the reassociating changes deliberately left
undone** — factoring `0.5 C11^2 X + 0.25 D22 X`, and batching the thirteen
two-dimensional terms through a 3-D stack that materialises `54 MB` at
`n = 1024`, which forum 18101 says costs residual. Neither is an IEEE identity,
so each needs a measured drift check rather than a byte comparison.

**And one host-load caveat, because it cuts against my own earlier number.**
Job 174 (`ae44369`, `2,708` operations) reported a mean residual of `0.2233 s`;
this run reports `0.1541 s` for a file `62` operations cheaper. A `2.3%`
operation change cannot produce a `31%` residual change: **the official runner is
itself sensitive to host load**, and the two readings differ by contention. The
conservative reading is job 174's. Both fail `>= 4x`, so the conclusion is
unchanged, but *"the authority is immune to host load"* is not a claim this
repository may make — only *"the authority is the only thing that can fail an
MLP, and it failed none."*

# 2026-09-03 — **THE STRATEGIST RULES ON THE THREE QUESTIONS. Arm M dies, the `4x` bar splits, and the canary goes out today.**

The previous entry closed with three questions it declared were not the agent's to
answer. They were escalated and a ruling came back. **It is recorded here in
substance before any of it is acted on**, because two of the three rulings relax
something this repository had written down, and a relaxation must be traceable to
the authority that granted it rather than to the agent that benefits from it.

## Ruling 1 — the `>= 4x` bar is SPLIT. It protects nominations, not canaries.

**Rationale as given.** Local residual cannot settle the question: the official
runner swings `31%` with host load for a `2.3%` operation change (this LOG,
previous entry), and per-MLP dispersion *within* a run is `1.20x`. Only the
grader's per-row telemetry can settle it, and **a canary returns that telemetry
for all 100 rows**. The cost of being wrong is bounded and asymmetric: an
undesignated public submission has no prize consequence — the private rerun grades
only designated entries, and Rules v14 §6's default would never pick a
residual-failed canary over `v2.7` — while an overrun costs one daily submission.

| bar | threshold | applies to |
|---|---|---|
| **CANARY** | `certify_candidate` green · Linux memory gate · `0/100` failures on the local official run · FLOPs at the `0.1` floor with `+2**24` margin · local worst-row headroom **`>= 1.5x`** | presenting a public, **undesignated** submission whose purpose is to buy graded telemetry |
| **NOMINATION** | on the canary's **graded** telemetry: worst-row residual headroom **`>= 4x`** · `0/100` graded failures · floor with `+2**24` · explicit designation before close | designating an entry for the private rerun |

**The canary bar is already met on the evidence that exists**: `0/100` (jobs 174
and 182), floor with margin (`x = 0.076684`, multiplier `0.10000`), worst-row
headroom `2.23x >= 1.5x` (`official_residual.json`). What is NOT yet met, and is
the subject of § A below: `certify_candidate` and the Linux memory gate, neither
of which has ever been run against `estimator_wp15_k3_canary.py`.

**Explicitly ruled OUT for the canary: the `3 x 100` soak.** It is not on the
canary path at all. It was the instrument for a question the grader answers
better.

**Order of work, as ruled:** canary first; then size the op-count work **to the
graded worst row**, not to the local one. If graded lands at `2.5x`-`4x`,
reassociate to that target and re-canary; if `< 2.5x`, cut hard. Reassociation may
proceed in parallel but **must not delay the submission**, and every reassociating
change takes WP16's parity gate (drift vs the golden reference `<= 1%`, raw within
noise) plus a re-metered price.

## Ruling 2 — Arm M is KILLED as a standalone. No separate cost case.

`G-M-DEPTH` failed as written (`0.5734` against `0.70`); the ruling is to **honour
the contract** rather than to re-argue it. The arithmetic behind the ruling:
`E21` is ~60% of the regenerating flow's error and `E3` ~40%; **either slice alone
saturates at ~`2.4x`** end to end (WP14: `proj:1024` = exact `E21`, no `E3`, is
`2.534x`; free exact `E3` alone is `1.551x`), and Arm M adds operations on the axis
that is currently binding the whole project. A `~73%`-of-`E21` recovery bought with
`~5` extra matmuls a layer is not a trade this project can make while the residual
is the blocker.

**What survives:** Arm M's three-generation closed-form terms (rank `<= 192`)
become **Arm L features**. They are a basis, not an architecture, and as features
they cost what a Hadamard-and-diagonal term costs rather than what a carried
generation costs.

**Recorded here and in the write-up:** three generations explain `0.7322` of
`E21`'s Frobenius energy, i.e. a **`~73%` explained fraction** — and `73%` of
`E21` is `~44%` of the flow's error, not `73%` of it.

## Ruling 3 — the floor nominee and Arm L run in PARALLEL.

Not sequenced. Today: (a) certify + memory gate + package → present the canary;
(b) queue Arm L's oracle-label job **now**. While those run, build the
equivariant feature library — **`E3` first**, because it is a per-neuron map on
`(mu, sigma, alpha = mu/sigma, S3)` at near-zero FLOPs and near-zero operations,
and **nothing in the project currently targets it at all**.

## Process constraints restated, and they bind everything below

Thresholds in flopscope FLOPs · nulls differ in **code path** · a pinned commit
for any Skeptic audit · committed preflight transcripts · soaks only through
`gpuq` · **the local official runner's residual is never a gate on its own.**

## The kill line moves to ~2026-09-24

If no `>= 10x` end-to-end drift reduction on fresh networks by then: freeze Arm L,
nominate the canaried uncorrected flow (only if graded worst-row headroom `>= 4x`,
else after a sized op cut) plus `v2.7` as the diverse pair, and finish the
write-up (due Oct 24; close Oct 17; **designate explicitly by Oct 10**).
Unchanged: AUGMENT deprioritised; the carrier lane and every other closed lane
stay closed.
